Researchers say prescribing exercise to people with heart problems could slash hospital admissions, with home-based digital programmes just as beneficial as in-person sessions.

Experts at the University of Glasgow analysed 107 trials involving 26,886 people with coronary heart disease, which happens when fatty deposits narrow or block the arteries that supply blood to the heart. Most patients had had a heart attack, experienced chest pain, or undergone a heart procedure.

The new review found that working out can play a “vital role” in recovery, as exercise-based rehabilitation slashed the risk of heart attacks by 28 per cent.

It also helped reduce hospital admissions by 35 per cent.

Dr Grace Dibben, from the University of Glasgow, said the review “shows that exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation can reduce the risk of heart attack and hospital admission while helping people return to healthier, more active lives.

“Many people lose confidence after a heart attack or cardiac procedure and worry that physical activity could be dangerous.

“Appropriately prescribed exercise is not only safe for most patients, but can play a vital role in recovery and long-term heart health.”

Home-based digital programmes were just as beneficial as in-person sessions ( Alamy/PA )

The analysis included 22 new trials featuring almost 3,500 people. The studies included patients in low and middle-income countries who were testing digital programmes.

Researchers suggest exercise completed in the home may be just as beneficial as attending in-person sessions.

Professor Rod Taylor, also of the University of Glasgow, said: “This review confirms that exercise is a great tool for improving the overall health of people with coronary heart disease.

“By adding newer studies to this update, we’re able to see that digital programmes work as well as in-person programmes, which really changes the game here.

“These approaches may help us reach people who cannot attend traditional centre-based services.”

Dr Dibben added: “Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation is an inexpensive and cost-effective intervention, but right now it’s underfunded and unprioritised.

“We want this option to be available to everyone.

“This new research shows you don’t even have to go into a rehab centre to benefit – you can participate from home and still see the benefits.”

The Asian Games open Saturday in Nagoya, Japan, and are often identified as the second most important multisports event after the Summer Olympic Games.

They date from the first edition in 1951 in New Delhi, India, and were last held in 2023 in Hangzhou, China. Those games were delayed a year because of the COVID-19 pandemic. The previous games were in 2018 in Jakarta, Indonesia, and this is Japan's third time as the host.

Here's a by-the numbers look at the Asian Games that run from Saturday through Oct. 4.

1

A lone Italian cruise ship, the Costa Serena, will function as a floating athletes villages with accommodation for up to 5,000 athletes and officials. Athletes will also be housed in hotels and in converted containers. The games will not offer a formal athletes village as organizers hope to save money after billions were spent on the Tokyo Olympics, held in 2021 after a year's delay because of COVID-19.

3

Nagoya is Japan's third largest metropolitan area behind Tokyo and Osaka. It's an industrial city located in central Japan on the Pacific coast with a metro population of about 9.5 million.

43

This is the number sports to be contested. Some are familiar Olympic disciplines. Others can be found only in the Asian Games. They include the team sports of kabaddi and sepaktakraw and martial arts like jiujitsu and a style of wrestling called kurash. Sports like teqball, padel and mixed marital arts have also been added.

Of course, there are old standbys like track and field, swimming and soccer.

45

This is the number of countries and regions participating. North Korea is sending about 100 athletes. That's down from almost 200 in China three years ago. North Korea did not go to Japan for the Tokyo Olympics.

The list runs from Afghanistan to Yemen. In addition, an Olympic Council of Asia refugee team is entered.

201

The number of gold medals China won in 2023. It was followed by Japan with 52 and South Korea with 42. The next three were India (28), Uzbekistan (22) and Taiwan (19).

900

Host Japan is sending the most athletes with about 900. China, with 1.4 billion people, is sending 815 and Hong Kong, with a population of only 7.5 million, is sending about 580 — an extraordinary number for such a small region.

China's delegation includes swimming prodigy Yu Zidi. As a 12-year-old last year at the swimming World Championships in Singapore, she finished fourth in all three of her individual races: 200- and 400-meter individual medley, and the 200 butterfly. She also earned bronze in a relay, though she did not swim in the final.

11,000+

The 2024 Paris Olympics fielded about 10,700 athletes. The Asian Games will have more than 11,000. The Asian Games may not be as prestigious as the Summer Olympics, but they are larger in participation.

Organizers have not been clear about exactly how many athletes are signed up. They say about 17,000 officials and more than 11,000 athletes are registered and have acknowledged numbers have soared above expectations in the last several months.

Almost 12,000 athletes competed three years ago in the Asian Games in Hangzhou, China. Nagoya seems likely to reach that level.

A last-minute crunch to find enough rooms has also been reported. Hotel rooms in Japan are typically small and this has drawn scrutiny from some athlete groups. Basketball players, as often happens, have said the beds are too short.

Imroze Ahmed, the head of the delegation from Bangladesh, acknowledged some problems but said they should be “settled” in a few days as the games get rolling.

“You can't blame anyone for this,” he said. “Such a big organization, big events.”

___

Social media users are mocking the physical condition of 84-year-old Sen. Mitch McConnell — with one vicious video turning him into the murdered man at the center of the movie “Weekend at Bernie’s” with the help of artificial intelligence.

“Mitch McConnell takes on the role he was born to play: Bernie Lomax,” says a description of the 64-second clip posted on YouTube by AI creator The Maitrix. “No politicians were required to move under their own power during the making of this video.”

The 1989 dark comedy cult classic revolves around the slapstick antics of two young insurance company employees who spend a weekend in the Hamptons pretending their slain boss is still alive to avoid being blamed for his death.

Other AI videos show McConnell performing acrobatic flips in a wheelchair after zooming down a ski jump or an X Games-style “mega ramp,” with the aging Kentucky Republican casually adjusting his glasses after nailing one landing.

A McConnell spokesperson didn't immediately return a Thursday afternoon inquiry from The Independent.

open image in gallery Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell is inserted into a scene from ‘Weekend at Bernie’s’ following his return to work on September 14, 2026, after a three-month absence ( YouTube/The Maitrix )

McConnell returned to work on Monday, looking frail and using a wheelchair after a three-month absence sparked by a fall in his Washington, D.C., home.

McConnell's long time away from the Capitol prompted widespread speculation about his health and a demand from Democratic Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear that he provide details or resign.

On Wednesday, a video clip of McConnell being coached by fellow Republicans before casting a tie-breaking vote to move the annual farm bill out of the agriculture committee renewed questions about his fitness.

In a statement posted later on social media, McConnell said, “I was proud to vote yes on the Farm Bill on behalf of the hardworking farm families across Kentucky.”

In addition to the AI videos mocking him, multiple social media users reposted and captioned a clip shot Monday by TMZ that shows McConnell sitting motionless in a vehicle and staring straight ahead.

open image in gallery An aide helps McConnell, in a wheelchair, into a meeting of the Senate agriculture committee on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, in Washington ( Getty )

The cruel cracks include “Actual footage of me on 100mg of edibles when I’m out in public,” “Me at the red light while the homeless guy stares in my window” and “dog in the passenger seat on the way to get one last ice cream cone before being put down.”

McConnell, who's been a senator since 1985 and plans to retire in January, holds the record for being the chamber's longest-serving party leader, from 2007 to 2025.

He was majority leader from 2015 to 2021, during which he blocked President Barack Obama's 2016 nomination of Merrick Garland to the Supreme Court on the grounds that the vacancy should be filled after that year's presidential election.

McConnell later pushed through President Donald Trump's 2020 nomination of Amy Coney Barrett just weeks before that year's election, which Trump lost to Joe Biden.

GOP U.S. Rep. Andy Barr and Democratic Kentucky state Rep. Charles Booker are vying to succeed McConnell, with the Cook Political Report rating the race “solid” Republican.

A human rights group in Haiti has published a report that reveals new details about one of the country’s biggest massacres in recent years and unveils security holes as authorities struggle to contain violent gangs.

The National Human Rights Defense Network said its report is backed by interviews with judges, police officials, armed civilians, the former head of a police station and more than 100 victims and their relatives.

The report provides the most complete account to date of the attacks that gangs recently launched on the once peaceful farming community of Kenscoff near Port-au-Prince, with at least 164 people killed, more than 70 kidnapped and dozens missing.

Strengthening security could have limited killings

The human rights group asserted in its report released Wednesday that a “timely strengthening” of security could have prevented or limited the killings.

“This lack of response is all the more concerning given that available information indicated the existence of a serious and imminent threat to the population,” it said.

A spokesperson for Haiti’s National Police did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Thursday.

The human rights group noted that Kenscoff remained vulnerable after an attack in January 2025 left at least 139 people dead or missing.

“Serious institutional failures that contributed to the perpetration of this massacre had been highlighted. Unsurprisingly, security was never truly restored in the town,” the group said.

It asserted that soldiers and special police units assigned to strategic locations in Kenscoff after the 2025 attack were recalled “for reasons that remain completely unknown.”

Security personnel had been cut

Overall, security personnel in the area were reduced by 60%, according to the report.

By July of this year, gangs attacked Kenscoff again, pulling back only to organize an even bigger attack in late August. A week before the massacre began, an armored vehicle was moved given a lack of personnel, “leaving a new opening for armed terrorist bandits and further weakening the city,” the report found.

Requests from the former head of the Kenscoff police station for two additional armored trucks were ignored prior to the attack, it added.

Days before the massacre, the group said that “armed terrorists” used surveillance drones to track movements and positions of law enforcement. They deployed scouts to the area, then infiltrated it and began monitoring roads, “identifying individuals likely to pose a threat to them.”

The human rights group said government officials told them they did not hear plans about the attack but did notice drones flying over the city hours before it began.

Tree trunks used to block roads

Another warning sign: tree trunks were used to block several roads hours before the massacre.

One of the first victims was a 21-year-old man ordered to carry stones to block a road before he was shot in the head, the report stated.

Among those killed were nearly two dozen people ages 65 to 90; 36 women; and seven children, including a 4-year-old. Victims included farmers, two pastors and a school principal who was beheaded, according to the report.

One man who worked at the Kenscoff police station had his eyes gouged and arms torn off, the report found.

Gang members killed people sheltered at a school and a church, using bodies as barricades as police and civilians battled them for several hours.

The report stated that armed men staged several attacks before entering Kenscoff to lure away police and weaken their defenses.

The human rights group identified the victims and the manner in which they were killed as it called on the government to provide financial, medical and psychological aid to survivors and their families.

Report criticizes police passivity

Between January and August this year, security operations had managed to reduce violence in Kenscoff by 66% prior to the attack, according to the nonprofit Armed Conflict Location & Event Data.

But the report criticized what it called police passivity and the “disdainful disinterest” of high-ranking police officers to protect the people of Kenscoff. It also questioned why a new U.N.-backed gang suppression force “remains barely perceptible on the ground, and its contribution to security operations remains difficult to identify.”

A spokesperson for the force did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Thursday evening.

In late August, the force said it was relieving Haitian police in certain areas to free up units so they could strengthen the protection of communities in Kenscoff.

The human rights group noted that another armed attack was launched within Kenscoff in mid-September.

Kenscoff’s mayor issued a statement on Tuesday warning that drones continued to fly over his community and that disturbing videos and messages are being posted online as threats.

“The convergence of these various signals must not be trivialized or ignored under any circumstances,” he wrote.

___

Associated Press reporter Evens Sanon in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, contributed.

News.title: Thames Water’s £10 billion creditor rescue deal should be ditched, say MPs

Thames Water’s rescue deal by lenders should be rejected and the Government should take it back into public control after the stricken supplier has been left in a damaging “doom loop”, according to an influential group of MPs.

A report by the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Efra) Committee said the £10 billion takeover plans by a consortium of over 100 creditors in Thames Water does not have “the interests of the public, the company or the environment at heart”.

The cross-party committee gives a stark warning that the top priority for the bidders, called London & Valley Water, is to “extract immediate value from Thames Water, not steer it to long-term success”.

The report also raises concerns among the MPs on the committee over the lack of information available on the many creditors in what it claims is an “opaque” consortium.

The rescue plan by creditors – including UK and US investment companies such as Elliott Management and American private capital firm Apollo Global Management – is seen as the final realistic option to avoid Thames Water being placed into a special administration regime after a previous deal with US private equity giant KKR collapsed in May last year.

Creditors – who collectively own about £17 billion of Thames Water’s debt mountain of more than £20 billion – have already been sent back to the drawing board after former environment secretary Emma Reynolds warned in June she did not believe their plan went far enough to protect customers or the environment.

The Efra Committee said laws needed to be changed to allow the Government to trigger a special administration on performance grounds without having to wait until the company collapses into insolvency – something that may risk a legal challenge from Thames Water creditors, it argues.

This has left Thames Water – the UK’s biggest water supplier – in a “doom loop”, according to the MPs.

Alistair Carmichael, chairman of the Efra Committee, said: “We believe Thames Water can be turned around, but not by giving the keys back to the people who have been joy riding in the family car.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham signalled before taking the reins at Number 10 that he wanted to bring in a 10-year plan to renationalise the water industry (Stefan Rousseau/PA) ( PA Wire )

“The Government should reject offers from the company’s creditors in return for relief from fines for pollution and poor service.

“We do not believe this opaque consortium of 100 hedge funds and others has the interests of the public, the company or the environment at heart.

“This will likely see Thames Water placed in Special Administration once its money runs out at the end of the year.

“But this may be the only way to reset the fortunes of this company and put it on a sustainable footing in the long-term.”

He said the cost to the Government could be recouped by a future sale of Thames Water in the future once its finances and performance are back on track and a buyer can be found.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham signalled before taking the reins at Number 10 that he wanted to bring in a 10-year plan to renationalise the water industry, saying reform was needed to put the public interest first.

But the Government has since remained tight-lipped on any renationalisation plans for Thames Water, despite the company warning it only has enough money until the year end.

Mr Carmichael said: “We recommend strengthening the Special Administration Regime so that a future regulator can intervene earlier and with legal certainty where it sees chronic failure.

“A loophole that allows bondholders to take control of a water company without oversight must also be addressed.

“The chaos of another Thames Water-style saga must not be repeated, and steps must be taken to stop the ‘doom loop’ that besets some companies, where fines for failure compound their inability to improve and leads to increased customer bills.”

A spokesman for London & Valley Water said: “This group of investors has never been in control of the company and has never received a dividend from Thames Water.

“They have stepped in to fund a significant revenue shortfall to ensure Thames Water’s record capital investment programme can continue without disruption.”

He added: “Our enhanced proposal will address all feedback from Ofwat and ministers and is the fastest route to fix Thames Water’s complex problems.”

A Thames Water spokesperson said: “Thames Water needs to be recapitalised and put on a firm financial footing… anything that delays the recapitalisation risks slowing the turnaround.”

News.title: NHS nurses found maggots in wounds during the UK’s ‘suffocating’ heatwaves
News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

One nurse reported seeing maggots in wounds as patients deteriorated in “suffocating atmospheres” during the summer heat on NHS wards.

The survey of 2,471 nurses for the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) found that high temperatures affected care, with examples of poorer outcomes for patients.

The results have prompted the RCN to call for more government investment so hospitals can better cope in warm weather.

According to a nurse surveyed, the children’s ward in Yorkshire reached 44C, while one in the North West said the situation was “horrendous” with patients “suffering more from the effects of heat than the actual reason they are in hospital”.

Another said patients fainted, and other patients suffered dehydration, particularly older people.

One common theme in the survey was the effect on people with heart failure and respiratory conditions, who seemed to fare worse because of the heat.

A nurse in the East of England described “patients with heart failure sitting in over 30C heat and a new ward with blocked windows”.

open image in gallery Almost 2,500 nursing staff were surveyed during the summer heatwaves ( PA )

A nurse in Wales said: “We had two frail patients for whom the extreme heat directly impacted their deaths.

“Whilst it was not the only cause, if you are in respiratory failure, the heat is a death sentence.”

In one London hospital, a nurse said the heat contributed to increased respiratory distress in newborn babies.

Another in a South East NHS hospital said high temperatures meant “wounds heal slower, mobility declines, and the simple act of resting becomes a battle against suffocating heat”.

A palliative care nurse working in a South West hospital said “we had a palliative patient with chronic ulcers on the ward.

“In the hospital’s care, during the last heatwave, the wounds festered enough that they attracted flies and were found to have maggots.

“Some of his and his relatives’ last memories will be knowing of and, in his case, feeling maggots in his wounds.”

A nurse treating cancer patients in London said: “I’ve seen patients sweating and dripping due to the heat during chemotherapy.

“There is no air conditioning running in the unit. During one particularly hot period, patients were visibly sweating throughout their treatment. This feels like a safety concern, not just a comfort issue.”

open image in gallery Temperatures in the UK reached 35C during May, June, July and August ( Getty )

Another nurse said: “I have actually cried for them [patients]. It’s inhumane. I don’t think a veterinary surgeon would be allowed to operate under such conditions.”

Multiple nurses also reported mental health patients becoming more challenging, leading to more assaults on staff.

Some 74 per cent of those polled said they had little or no confidence that the government was taking sufficient action to reduce the impact of climate change on the NHS and social care.

Freedom of Information figures released earlier this month suggested more than 1,000 operations at NHS hospitals were cancelled because of the heat during record-breaking heatwaves in May and June.

Temperatures in the UK reached 35C during May, June, July and August, the first time this has happened.

RCN chief executive Professor Nicola Ranger said: “This testimony reveals the devastating impact of extreme heat on patients, with increased death, deterioration, and conditions in services which, frankly, are an assault on people’s right to dignified, safe care.

“The reality is that climate change is here, but long-term underinvestment in our health and care services has left them so unprepared.

“Staff did everything they could in record-breaking temperatures to keep patients safe and comfortable, but they were fighting a losing battle in buildings which often lack even the most basic cooling facilities. It’s been incredibly traumatic.

“We are all aware of the pressures that winter brings, but extreme heat is here to stay, and the clock is now ticking to accelerate investment in hospitals, care homes and other settings to ensure they are prepared.

“This summer was our warning. By next, we need everywhere to have effective cooling facilities in place, or patients will suffer shocking harm once again.”

The Department of Health has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing
News.content:
There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

News.title: Banton shows his worth as England cruise to series victory against Sri Lanka
News.content:
A patchy Test team and a one-day international side learning on the job should not obscure the fact that under Harry Brook, England have built a formidable T20 outfit.

Missing a slew of first-choice players, they dispatched Sri Lanka with a game to spare and an emphatic show of their depth in the format, with Sonny Baker and Tom Banton – two men still finding their feet in the side – to the fore. England have now won 20 of the 23 completed T20s since Brook took over last year, and six matches in a row this summer. It is easily their best format and, as Liam Dawson said, they have “match-winners throughout” and plenty of “freak” performers.

In this six-wicket win, Baker’s one for 15 limited England’s target to a paltry 146, which Banton, a natural opener who is being recommissioned in the middle order, helped knock off with 47 balls remaining. “Tonight was a special performance, very clinical,” said Brook.

News.title: Interest rate increase ‘likely’, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Andrew Bailey has said that interest rates are likely to rise if the Middle East war rages on, warning inflation is now on course to hit 4pc.

The Bank of England opted to hold borrowing costs at 3.75pc on Thursday, the sixth time in a row it has left them unchanged.

However, the Governor said a “material” increase in energy prices since July would push up inflation to twice the Bank’s 2pc target.

He warned the outlook for inflation “continues to be on the upside” and criticised the “seeming loss of urgency to find solutions” to the war in Iran.

Oil prices are back above $100 a barrel and analysts expect average gas and electricity bills to rise above £2,000 this winter as the conflict continues.

Mr Bailey said: “So far, higher global energy costs have had a limited effect on price and wage setting in the UK.

“But the longer this volatility persists, the bigger the impact it will have on inflation, and the more likely it is we will need to raise Bank Rate to ensure that inflation falls back to our 2pc target.”

Investors expect the Bank to raise interest rates as soon as November, which has pushed average mortgage rates to their highest level in three years.

The average five-year fixed mortgage deal has risen to 5.87pc, according to Moneyfacts, which is the highest level since November 2023 and up from 4.95pc before the Iran war.

Thursday’s rate hold leaves the Bank out of step with central banks around the world after the US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank voted to raise borrowing costs this month.

However, economists said there had been a change in tone from policymakers over the threat posed by energy prices and whether this would feed into the wider economy.

The Bank of England predicted that inflation would hit 4pc early next year, just as most workers are negotiating pay rises.

Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said: “It seems as though a majority of the MPC is on the cusp of wanting to tighten policy.”

In a warning on the impending pain facing households, Mr Bailey told the Chancellor that energy bills would rise by 24pc early next year under the Ofgem price cap.

This will push up annual average bills by £413 to £2,136, which the Governor blamed on the war in the Middle East.

The Governor is required to write a formal letter to the Chancellor every time inflation is more than a percentage point above its 2pc target.

Official data showed inflation rose to 3.1pc in August.

Mr Bailey said: “The energy price shock has been the most important factor driving recent short-term movements in inflation.”

Despite expectations of higher rates, the FTSE 100 rose on Thursday at its steepest pace since July, climbing more than 1pc, as the Bank of England eased the pressure on the UK bond market.

Policymakers also confirmed a Telegraph report that the Bank will stop selling the long-dated bonds it amassed during the financial crisis and lockdown.

The Bank will continue actively selling £20bn of government bonds per year until the rest of the stockpile is wound down to zero in 2034.

The announcement triggered a sharp fall in the cost of borrowing for the Treasury, with the yield on 30-year UK gilts falling at the fastest pace since May.

News.title: Next-generation antivenom fights India’s deadliest snakes
News.content:
The process to make antivenom has barely changed in a century: snakes are milked, their venom is injected into horses, and their antibodies are harvested to form the basis of the product. The resulting treatments are difficult to administer, can trigger severe side effects, and the quality varies from batch to batch.

“The big four snakes contribute to 70 per cent of poisonous bites [in India]… so 30 per cent of poisonous snakes are not covered, even to begin with,” said Dr Yogesh Jain, a public health physician in Chhattisgarh state and a member of The Global Snakebite Taskforce.

“But there are huge quality and efficacy issues even against these 70 per cent of bites. We’re relying on a 100-year-old technique of getting antivenoms, and at least 50,000 people are dying every year,” he told The Telegraph.

“There’s a real need for new technology. We don’t have a safe and appropriate antivenom for the largest majority of people in rural India.”

Now, scientists are hopeful that they have developed a potential alternative.

In the latest study, published last week, researchers showed that an experimental antivenom cocktail with five components protected mice against lethal doses of antivenom in Indian cobras, even when delayed by up to 20 minutes – a scenario that mimics the real-world lag between a bite and treatment.

“If you go 10 years back, people didn’t think you could make sufficiently simple products with new, modern biotechnology that could cover all these different snake venoms,” said Prof Andreas Laustsen-Kiel, head of the Section of Biologics Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark and co-author of the paper.

“People simply believed it was too complex, too expensive to manufacture, and so on… But the data we are gathering is convincing enough to say this is something that could make a huge dent in the lost lives and limbs snakebite causes every year.”

The antivenom itself was based on lab-made nanobodies – antibodies derived from a group of animals including camels, llamas and some species of shark. Scientists believe their structure means they could be a more potent, more precise, more temperature-stable alternative to man-made monoclonal antibodies – and cheaper to manufacture.

“The latest study builds on an earlier discovery of nanobodies that can protect across a broad spectrum of African snakes,” said Prof Nicholas Casewell, director of the Centre for Snakebite Research and Interventions at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, who has previously collaborated with Prof Laustsen-Kiel.

“In this paper they have iterated and demonstrated that a narrow number of nanobodies can protect against Indian cobras and king cobras. This demonstration brings the nanobody technology closer to market,” he added.

But that is likely still years away, depending on how much funding the researchers can attract. The next steps – a larger animal study, scaling up manufacture, and launching human trials – are expensive.

“If money was no issue, we could probably be testing in humans in 1.5 to three years from now,” said Prof Laustsen-Kiel. “But since money is a big issue, it is more likely that human trials won’t be able to start until 2.5 to four years from now.

“But I really think that this [study shows] there’s no doubt that biotech can deliver better antivenoms. The question is whether people are willing to fund it,” he said.

News.title: Manchester United hounded off pitch by own fans
News.content:
The joke goes that Michael Carrick has already bettered Ruben Amorim’s efforts by reaching the third round of the League Cup, but Manchester United will need to find a way past free-flowing Brighton if they are to go any further.

United were eliminated in the second round by League Two Grimsby Town last season, but start the competition a stage later because they are one of nine Premier League clubs playing in European competition.

Brighton knocked United out of the FA Cup in the third round, with Danny Welbeck scoring at Old Trafford, meaning the club played just 40 matches in 2025-26.

Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the new season.

The no-show at Hull and derby defeat by City’s 10 men were especially dispiriting, and the relationship between the club and supporters is becoming increasingly strained.

There were no flags on the Stretford End for the game against City, as fans voiced their opposition to what they view as a heavy-handed ticketing policy. The club says the measures are to stop ticket-touting but critics believe many innocent season-ticket holders are being caught in the crossfire and having their tickets revoked.

Discontent is never too far away given the continued presence of the Glazer family, and confidence is fragile regarding the club’s sporting direction under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

The news that 15-year-old JJ Gabriel, possibly the country’s outstanding academy player in his year group, wants out (broken by Matt Law in a Telegraph Sport exclusive) nagged at some of those fears.



Gabriel could have been in contention for a place on the bench this evening, but that is now surely out of the question even if United say they have not given up hope of persuading him to stay.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Spurs finally score... but still lose
News.content:
“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

News.title: England cruise to victory led by ‘absolute freak’ Brook
News.content:
Whatever his returns, there has been an extra focus to Brook’s approach this summer, possibly because he has learnt from a grievous indiscretion in Wellington last winter. While others chase the Indian Premier League, he is totally committed to England, taking his break while that tournament is on and playing every match in all formats for his country.

Brook had come to the crease at the fall of the first wicket and, while it is early days, England appear to have added another arrow to their quiver. They handed a debut to opener Aneurin Donald, with his cap presented in the pre-match huddle by Pietersen, the new “specialist mentor”.

Donald has been selected as an “intent merchant”, charged with going extremely hard from the first over, aping Phil Salt, who is missing with a quad injury. He did what he was asked to do, smearing his first ball for two, then pulling six to leg and hammering four through the offside before the first over was out. Another big shot, off Wellalage, in the second saw him well caught in the deep, but 12 off five had kickstarted the innings.

News.title: Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town
News.content:
At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso welcomes end of £1bn Chelsea civil war after Boehly exit & reveals how Eghbali sealed his move to Blues
Sports.content:
Next

XABI ALONSO has welcomed the end of Chelsea’s boardroom civil war.

Behdad Eghbali and his Clearlake Capital group have completed a buyout of Todd Boehly and business partner Mark Walter in a deal reported to be worth almost £1billion.



Alonso, 44, thanked Boehly, 52 and Walter, 66, for their work since the BlueCo consortium’s takeover in 2022. But the new Blues boss is happy now to be serving one master.

The Spanish tactician said: “It’s an important day for the club when there is an important change in the structure of the club and the ownership.



“I know they played an important role and now that Behdad is taking more control, almost full control, it’s good that the main one is clear.

“I have very good relations with Behdad, he was the one that came to Madrid to explain to me the project, to convince me and we are working well together.



“This is phase one that we have completed in the project of the squad and now we move on together.

“It is good with Behdad and with the sporting directors that we are working together to take the decisions. It starts moving, everything. I have to thank the former owners for the work they’ve done.”

The buyout by Eghbali and co-founder Jose Feliciano will change little or nothing in the day-to-day running of Chelsea.

Eghbali has been the main man at Stamford Bridge since January 2023, overseeing every aspect of how the Blues are run.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But Boehly’s departure means there are no longer internal obstacles to Clearlake and Eghbali making big decisions about the long-term future, including the much-delayed plans for a new stadium.

The American businessman became the public face of the BlueCo regime soon after the May 2022 takeover from Roman Abramovich — despite having a stake of just 12.8 per cent, compared to Clearlake’s 61.5 per cent.

His title of club chairman, tendency to wear a baseball cap and willingness to give interviews floating ideas like a North v South Premier League All-Star game, made it easy to latch on to him.

Boehly and fellow businessman Walter brought something to the table Clearlake did not have — experience of running successful sports teams, most notably baseball’s LA Dodgers.



But after a spell as sporting director in the summer 2022 transfer window — with mixed results — Boehly took a back seat and Eghbali was at the wheel for both football and non-football issues.

As Alonso revealed, it was Eghbali who travelled to Madrid to talk him into becoming the sixth permanent boss of the BlueCo era.

And it is with Eghbali he interacts regularly, including when the billionaire financier visits the dressing room after games.

Boehly backed the appointment of Alonso. But he and Eghbali clashed on a number of issues, on and off the field, including the sacking of manager Mauricio Pochettino in 2024.

But since the autumn of that same year, it was clear they were not going to be able to work together in the long term.



Matters came to a head in the summer when Walter came under pressure from a probe by the US authorities into his business affairs.

He denies any wrongdoing. But with Boehly’s five-year term as chairman due to finish at the end of the season, it was a good time to part ways.

As SunSport revealed, the impasse over a new 60,000-seater stadium complex was a key factor.

Boehly and Eghbali broadly agreed on what Chelsea needed but their visions differed in detail.

And neither was willing to pump in more money and take on more debt to fund a project in which the other would still have a significant say.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Blues still face significant challenges externally, as they wait to see if their preferred site in Earl’s Court becomes available.

But everyone in the boardroom will now be pulling in the same direction. With no Boehly around to take any credit or blame, it is Eghbali who will be steering the ship — and under more pressure than ever to deliver success.

Sports.title: Tuchel talking to wrong fan-base about scars… England boss must be bold with squad AND tactics, not just Southgate 2.0
Sports.content:
Next

DID Thomas Tuchel make a major tactical balls-up against Argentina? Is water wet? The Pope Catholic?

We finally got the answer to one of these imponderables from the man himself this week during an hour-long interview with Daniel Sturridge.

Tuchel, that is, not the Pope.



During a sit-down chat titled Reflections, the England boss admitted he went too defensive, too early against the Argies in World Cup semi-finals.

As we all know, Harry Kane and Co sat back to try to defend a 1-0 lead with the best part of half an hour to go, only to concede twice late on.



The German also spoke of his “scars”, and those of his team, after the heartbreaking exit, adding that it was his pain to bear.

You’re talking to the wrong fanbase about scars, old boy.



Whether it was the Hand of God, going out on penalties to West Germany in 1990 or failing to qualify entirely four years later.

The Beckham red in Saint-Etienne, the fluke Ronaldinho freekick, more penalty heartache at the hands of Portugal and the winker, Cristiano Ronaldo.

Embarrassment in South Africa, via a Frank Lampard goal that never was, and group-stage humiliation in Brazil. We’ve seen it all.

That’s without mentioning the number of gut-wrenching defeats at Euros over the years, including in the last two finals.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Every England football fan has scars, either from watching garbage under Graham Taylor, Steve McClaren and Roy Hodgson, or suffering heartbreak under Bobby Robson, Terry Venables and Gareth Southgate.

After 60 years of punishment, we’re covered in them.

The point is that Tuchel was meant to be the man who came in and changed all that, who didn’t make catastrophic tactical decisions with a World Cup final on the line.

Instead, at the critical point in a seismic match, what we got was Southgate 2.0.

While generally beloved as England chief, Southgate was always out-matched whenever it came down to the really big games against the likes of Roberto Mancini and Luis de la Fuente.



We can’t keep going round and round in circles making the same mistakes, otherwise we risk wasting another excellent crop of English players.

There’s been a pattern over the years of England coaches managing expectations downwards before a ball has even been kicked.

To talk about pain and gaps to the “top nations” rather than backing this latest golden generation to close that gap themselves.

Southgate’s caution cost England in too many big matches. Tuchel cannot inherit that same flinch.



We are all tired of talk about mental scars, of self-flagellation after another disappointment and insisting that lessons will be learned. It’s time to deliver.

After all, there were actually some positives to take from a World Cup in which we achieved our best finish since 1966.

The night, or rather early morning, at the Azteca will always be one of the great England wins, overcoming a good Norway side and thumping France, albeit in a game nobody wants to play in.

We need to look forward and Tuchel has to divert all of his energy into England’s response. We all know Atlanta was a mess — now what is he going to do about it?

There can be no better opportunity to get the country back onside than against the world champions Spain at Wembley tomorrow week.



He will announce his squad for the upcoming international break today, and it is an opportunity to give some fresh blood, who perhaps aren’t bearing so many scars, a crack.

Cole Palmer is a no-brainer, as are Alex Scott and Morgan Gibbs-White.

It might be too early for Rio Ngumoha, 18, and Max Dowman 16, but they should get a look-in over the next 18 months.



The vast majority of England fans will tell you we’d rather go down fighting than clinging on for dear life with ten men camped on the edge of our own box.

We don’t want more of the same. That is what Tuchel promised, and that’s what he NEEDS to deliver.

LAMP LIGHT

FRANK LAMPARD is already back under the spotlight — and not for the right reasons.

His Coventry side have played well in spells on their long-awaited return to the Prem.

But they have zero cutting edge up front and they’re so bad defensively they make Chelsea look like prime, early 90s AC Milan.



It’s not the greatest recipe for success in the world’s toughest league and, on the evidence of the first few weeks, they look certainties to go back down.

Lampard repaired his damaged reputation by winning the Championship title last season — but a disastrous campaign in the top flight will be difficult to recover from.

DE-DAY DATE

AT what point do Tottenham fans seriously start to panic?



They look just as bad as they have done for the past two seasons, despite investing the GDP of a small country in the squad this summer.

The pressure is seriously mounting on boss Roberto De Zerbi, who did his best Pep Guardiola imitation last week by publicly dressing down forward Mathys Tel, 21, on the pitch after the bore draw with Everton.

It seemed to go down as well as a cup of cold sick. So Saturday’s lunchtime game against a rebuilding Aston Villa is a fascinating one, and if they drop points again you get the feeling the atmosphere is going to be unbearably toxic.

GRACE RACING

IF only a few of our do-gooder MPs were at Doncaster last weekend, they’d have seen horse racing needs cherishing.

The Government have it in for the gambling industry right now, which in turn means the future of the second-most popular sport in the UK is under growing threat.



But if they’d gone to Donny, they’d have seen 30,000 people having a few bets and a blinding day out.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And the scenes after Saffie Osborne, 24, became the first woman to win a British Classic in the St Leger will live long in the memory.

Racing is such a precious sport to millions — if you get a spare minute, maybe remind your local MP of that.

Sports.title: Only winners at Man Utd are Amazon Prime with documentary to provide epic content after horror results & JJ Gabriel saga
Sports.content:
Next

THE only winners at Manchester United are Amazon Prime.

The streaming giant’s All or Nothing documentary is already shaping up to be box office — only they should scrap the “All” from the title.



Old Trafford’s crisis start to the season hit a new low as Brighton became the first team in over 50 years to win at Old Trafford after trailing by two goals to dump the hosts out of the cup.

Hull was the warning shot. The left-back crisis was ignored before Luke Shaw dropped like a fly, two leads were squandered at Everton before the VAR controversy in the poor derby defeat to Enzo Maresca’s ten men.



The morning after academy crown jewel JJ Gabriel asked to leave, ditching the chance for a historic debut, another collapse exposing just how quickly things are spiralling.

Now Fulham on Sunday is suddenly massive for Michael Carrick.

He still retains the backing of the board but he could kick off with United as low as 17th, meaning their support could soon waiver with another shambolic loss.

Carrick cut a forlorn figure on Wednesday and certain results haunt United managers.

For Erik Ten Hag, it was the chaotic FA Cup semi-final against then-Championship side Coventry City.

Ruben Amorim will forever be remembered for the League Cup exit to League Two side Grimsby Town. Carrick can only hope the Brighton collapse doesn’t stick in the memory the same way.



The United legend has enjoyed a relatively tranquil 11 months in charge after taking over from Amorim, initially temporarily, in January.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But any hope that momentum might carry over has vanished within the first month.

It’s now two wins from six games and four points from four in the league. Carrick is under real pressure for the first time.

United lost at Old Trafford after leading by two goals for the first time in 50 years. It was their first home defeat after leading at half-time since May 1984.

Carrick’s decision-making has come under fire and his in-game management quizzed.



Starting Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro, the club’s rawest centre-backs, against Brighton — who always do a number on United — was a desperate mistake.

The needless subs at Everton led to mistakes before Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stoppage-time screamer.

Yes Carrick, who won 12 of 17 matches last term, has made recent mistakes – but he has been left dangerously short squad-wise as United’s recruitment strategy failed to provide him with the tools.

An overhaul of the defence has been promised for next summer, but prioritising one area at a time is not becoming of any serious sporting organisation.



Carrick does not have a backline that can compete for the top four, never mind the title. He cannot work miracles.

The baffling decision not to sign a left-back has already been exposed by Shaw’s predictable injury.

Neither Patrick Dorgu nor Noussair Mazraoui are capable of filling in convincingly, Diogo Dalot making his 251st appearance for the club is an indictment in itself and Matthijs de Ligt has been out for eight months.

The club still rely on the same weak defensive core that needed replacing years ago and United have always spent more after failing to qualify for the Champions League.

Ineos are failing miserably, their sister clubs Lausanne and Nice sit rock bottom of their respective leagues, as do United’s women’s team, who have been told transfer spending is unsustainable in the WSL.



Defeat at Fulham, who are searching for their first win this season, would cap one of the worst weeks in living memory after academy wonderkid Gabriel begged to become a free agent.

The original plan to include him in the matchday squad against Brighton was shelved following his termination request and the fact a 15-year-old has refused to train this week.

Many in academy circles believe United are watching a future £100m player slip through their fingers, with Real Madrid leading the race to lure him away when he turns 16 next month.

And then there are the already disgruntled fans, who are patient with managers but have every right to find fault with the haphazard ownership.

Another protest was staged before the derby over the club’s handling of the ticket-touting crackdown.



Around 500 supporters demonstrated outside Old Trafford on Sunday before the Stretford End banners were replaced with one reading: “The way you treat us is a disgrace.”

Ratcliffe and Avram Glazer were in the directors’ box well aware of the sentiment against them as thousands poured through the Munich tunnel outside demanding they sell up.

The Glazer ownership model of borrowing against the club’s assets has drained United of resources and played a major role in rotting structures from the top down.

To make matters worse, Carrick and his players were brutally booed off during a toxic night to chants of “what the f***ing hell was that?” after the dire Brighton collapse.



On the pitch, fitness levels have increasingly come under scrutiny. Tielemans’ interview telling Rio Ferdinand that players mostly focus on ball work has been doing the rounds.

Sky pundits Jamie Redknapp and former United defender Ashley Young also queried Carrick’s side’s physical levels and inability to match Brighton’s runs and intensity.

United signed two unfit players this summer as Karl Darlow missed all of pre-season and Carlos Baleba will not play until October 10 at the earliest.

The mentality has been a deep-rooted problem for years, but last season offered hope this group had finally learned to absorb setbacks.



Now the old cracks are showing again. So often the saviour, skipper Bruno Fernandes looked fed up too.

When United are winning, the bulk of this squad look happy, confident and all guns blazing. But throw a setback at them and suddenly the swagger disappears. They retreat into the same bad habits that plagued previous managers.

You felt it the moment Erling Haaland scored in the derby. Whatever the wrongs of the Enzo Fernandez offside call – and the subsequent apology – United never seemed likely to get back into the game.

A setback quickly becomes a crisis, confidence drains away and the team loses its shape and belief, perhaps the most worrying part for Carrick.

After a kind start, the fixture list turns ugly after the international break, with Tottenham, Atletico Madrid, Leeds, Como, Bournemouth, Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa in a month.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

As Ten Hag and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer can vouch, October and November can be sacking season at Old Trafford.

Carrick is safe for now, but the cameras will be primed and ready for the next must-see slip-up, which could prove fatal.

Sports.title: Gary O’Neil shares heartbreaking statement announcing death of his ‘incredible’ dad as Ipswich lead tributes
Sports.content:
Next

GARY O’NEIL has announced the tragic news that his dad has died.

The Ipswich boss released an emotional statement on Instagram paying tribute.



O’Neil shared a picture as a child of himself and his late father, Graham.

He said: “Thanks for everything Dad!



“I couldn’t have done any of it without you.

“You taught me football, you taught me values and you taught me how to look after everyone that’s important to me.

“What an incredible example you set!!

“I’ll miss you forever mate!

“Rest in peace, Dad!! Love you.”

Ipswich paid tribute on social media by saying: “All at Ipswich Town are deeply saddened by the passing of Gary O’Neil’s father, Graham.



“Our thoughts, condolences and love are with Gary and his family at this incredibly sad time.”

Aston Villa‘s Joao Gomes, who played under O’Neil while at Wolves, said: “I’m sorry for you, Boss.”

Former EFL star and Sky Sports pundit Luke Chambers said: “Thinking of you mate.”

Steve Sidwell, who was once in the England Under-21 squad alongside O’Neil, replied with a blue heart emoji.

Portsmouth star Marlon Pack said: “Sorry for your loss mate.



“Thoughts with you and the family.”

O’Neil joined Ipswich in June following their promotion to the Premier League.

The Tractor Boys have won two of their four top flight games so far, picking up three points against Sunderland and away at Crystal Palace.

They have suffered defeats away at Manchester United and at home to Liverpool.

Following last weekend’s Palace win, O’Neil said he is loving his time at Portman Road.

He said: “It’s been the best four months of my career, playing or managing. I’ve loved it, every minute of it.

“The playing group just gives everything. We’ll lose some, but we’ll give everything when we lose.”

Sports.title: Crystal Palace 4 Lech Poznan 0: Eagles storm to win on Europa League debut through chaotic first-half blitz
Sports.content:
Next

YEREMY PINO helped Palace to a dream Europa League debut – as did the worst long throw you will ever see.

Poznan’s Terry Yegbe launched an awful throw-in towards his own box – and away from any team-mates – to allow World Cup winner Pino to steal in and notch a tenth-minute opener.



Chris Richards then powered home a routine corner from captain Adam Wharton, before Pino won a penalty which Jorgen Strand Larsen converted, all within 34 minutes.

It provided the perfect start to the Eagles’ maiden campaign in this competition, having won the Conference League last term, and a most welcome win for new boss Pierre Sage.



This was the first time Polish champs Lech Poznan had played an English side since beating Manchester City 3-1 in November 2010.

That game inspired City fans to pinch ‘the Poznan’ goal celebration, where supporters turn their backs to the action, link arms and jump around like mad.

Wharton captained a full-strength Palace on what was his 100th appearance for the club.

Poznan had chances but, really, once Palace went into a two-goal lead, the hosts were in cruise control.

The first was a complete gift thanks to Yegbe’s inexplicable long-throw which Pino ruthlessly punished, while the second was so simple as Richards gleefully headed in Wharton’s corner.

Both were moments to wince at for Poznan’s English set-piece coach, Andy Parslow.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It was 3-0 and game over after just 34 minutes when Pino was tripped for a penalty he desperately wanted to take, but instead Strand Larsen did the honours and rifled into the net.

The Norwegian giant then had consoling words with Pino during the celebration and ahead of the restart, presumably to explain why he had pulled rank to take it.

Yegbe’s day almost got worse when Strand Larsen’s pass flew in off him from a full 35 yards – but the hilarious own goal was mercifully ruled out for offside.



At that point, Lech’s numerous travelling fans did ‘the Poznan’, though it may have been because they no longer wanted to witness their team’s bad defending.

Poznan went down to ten men for the final few minutes when Radoslaw Murawski was given a second booking for a barge before sub Eddie Nketiah fired home a cool fourth.

The result was a welcome boost for Palace, who sit 16th in the Premier League after losing 3-2 at home to Ipswich at the weekend.

Sports.title: Real Sociedad 1 Bournemouth 2: Kluivert and Rayan score to give Cherries dream start to first ever European campaign
Sports.content:
Next

JUSTIN KLUIVERT and Rayan were on target to bag Bournemouth a glittering European debut.

The first half couldn’t have gone any better with two goals in 20 minutes making the Cherries look like Europa League veterans.



The hosts cranked up the pressure in the second half with Sergio Gomez on target on 58 minutes.

Djorde Petrovic then became the hero as he produced a string of jaw-dropping stops to save his side in the dying moments.



Marco Rose’s team entered the record books by playing in Europe for the first time in the club’s 127-YEAR history.

Goosebumps filled the away end as Bournemouth’s Adam Smith led his side out and became the oldest English outfield player in a major European competition in 64 years.

At 35 years and 141 days, Smith is the oldest non-goalkeeper to make his European debut since Reginald Pickett for Ipswich against AC Milan in November 1962 at 35years and 317days.

Kluivert soon side-footed Bournemouth into the lead but the offside flag went up while he was already wheeling away in celebration.



However, VAR awarded the goal as there was no offside before Adrien Truffert’s ball and Bournemouth were officially cherishing their first ever European goal.

The Cherries were flying and just nine minutes later a peach of a ball from Alex Scott was played to Rayan who was charging towards the back post.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The Brazilian forward rose highest to steer it into the far corner with his head.

Bournemouth were bossing it as tensions rose, with Kluivert booked for giving Gomez a hand in the face.



And the hosts emerged from the restart with a bit between their teeth, having not had a single shot on target so far.

They were building as Benat Turrientes sent a dipping and curling shot towards the bottom corner, which Petrovic saved.

Their pressure paid off as Gomez whipped in an unbelievable cross, which beat everyone, including Petrovic, and sailed into the far corner.

The decibels rose and Goncalo Guedes wriggled between two defenders and teed up World Cup star Mikel Oyarzabal, who lifted it on to the roof of the net.

There were few dry eyes left in the away end as David Brooks took the place of Kluivert, five years after his cancer diagnosis.



The visitors were under the cosh, though, and Arsen Zakharyan slid it through for Orri Oskarsson but Petrovic made an epic save.

Real Sociedad really thought they had levelled but Petrovic produced another blinding save from a close-range effort from Oskarsson as Bournemouth held on to a truly historic win.

Sports.title: Premier League cult icon’s son, 17, scores twice for Man City on his DEBUT in Carabao Cup clash vs Norwich
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER CITY starlet Floyd Samba made a glittering first-team debut with a stunning bace in the Carabao Cup against Norwich.

Floyd, 17, was part of City manager Enzo Maresca’s starting line-up at the Etihad where the first team hosted the Canaries.



And the midfielder did Maresca proud as he scored twice on his first ever first-team appearance.

The England Under-17 international opened the scoring just before the half-hour mark with a beautiful header.



That was after Allan picked up a beautiful cross from Nico O’Reilly at the left and delivered a ball of his own from the far post before finding the academy star in the middle.

That finish would make Floyd’s father and Premier League cult hero Christopher Samba very proud.

Ex-Blackburn, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa ace Christopher, 42, was also good in the air.

But Floyd wasn’t done just yet as he sealed a dominant victory for a heavily-rotated Man City side on 54 minutes.

Rayan Ait-Nouri gained possession down the left flank and passed it to the central midfielder who fired a magical curling shot that smashed Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw’s bottom left corner.

Floyd made it 4-0 for the hosts after another two goals by Rayan Cherki and Allan – that was before Ryan McAidoo made it five.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The versatile midfielder, who can also operate as a playmaker and a centre-forward, counts a total of 29 goals and 11 assists in 58 appearances across the Citizens’ youth ranks.

Christopher spent a total of seven years in the Premier League, five of which were with Blackburn.

The former centre-back also picked up 26 caps with Congo during his 16-year career.

Floyd could get some more minutes in the Carabao Cup as City are now set to host Brighton in the fourth round.

Sports.title: Man City 5 Norwich 0: Samba, 17, scores two on debut as Allan and McAidoo also get on scoresheet to set up Brighton tie
Sports.content:
Next

BACK of the net!

Manchester City have a new signing called Allan – so it seemed fitting that he should use Norwich to make his name.



However, unlike with their ‘favourite son’ Partridge, this was no laughing matter for the thousands who made the journey up from Norfolk.

The Brazilian winger was a £34million signing from Palmeiras in the final few days of the transfer window and his arrival went almost under the radar.



His new club were busy finalising deals for the likes of Ayyoub Bouaddi, Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez – so nobody was too interested in this one.

But he marked his debut by scoring one and creating another for fellow debutant Floyd Samba, who ended up stealing the show from Allan by grabbing two goals.



Samba is the son of former Blackburn defender Christopher – who loved watching his 17-year-old boy’s sensational first run out from the stands.

The young winger has already made something of a name for himself when he scored in the FA Youth Cup final against neighbours United in May.

He is one of three academy players Enzo Maresca has promoted to the first team here along with Ryan McAidoo and Kaden Braithwaite.

Samba is the youngest and the last of the trio to get his chance and he did not let his manager down with his performance here.

The youngster was involved right from the start, playing in Rico Lewis only for the full-back to lift his shot over the bar.

Phillipe Clement had made nine changes to his team – one fewer than Maresca – and his team looked up for it early on before two goals in three minutes killed the tie.

Just before the half hour, Nico O’Reilly’s cross to the back post was lifted back across by Allan and Samba flicked a header into the far corner.

It was a special moment for him – but he was far from finished there, playing a clever pass into the feet of Bouaddi moments later.



The Moroccan’s ball was inch perfect for Rayan Cherki to spring the offside trap and finish emphatically past former City trainee Daniel Grimshaw.

The visitors knew the game was up for them – while Maresca was closing in on a sixth straight win since the Community Shield disappointment.



But his team were far from finished there and Allan got his big moment three minutes after the re-start.

The winger picked up the ball on the left and twisted and turned past his man before shooting low beyond Grimshaw for a super individual goal.

He only played 71 minutes but already seems to have secured cult status with the Etihad faithful – who gave him a standing ovation when he was subbed.



By then he had been upstaged by Samba who collected a pass from Rayan Ait Nouri before curling a delicious shot into the corner.

His old man – who made his mark as an imposing 6ft 6in centre back in Mark Hughes’ Rovers team – could hardly stop smiling.

Norwich thought they had a consolation their travelling fans deserved when Mohamed Toure latched onto a pass from Antony Musaba.

And in the closing minutes, McAidoo, on as a half time sub for Cherki, swept home number five as he got on the end of O’Reilly’s low cross.

The Canaries have now conceded 24 goals in their last five visits to this stadium with just one goal to cheer along the way.

Sports.title: Premier League star Leif Davis hailed for joining Noah Woods search and huge donation
Sports.content:
Premier League star Leif Davis hailed for joining Noah Woods search and huge donation

Leif Davis, who plays for Premier League club Ipswich, was among the 1,000-plus search party looking for three-year-old Noah Woods, whose body has now been found

View 3 Images Leif Davis has donated to the family of Noah Woods (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

Ipswich defender Leif Davis has been hailed for donating £2,000 to the family of Noah Woods. Davis, 26, is said to have been among the group of at least 1,300 volunteers who went looking for the three-year-old in the early hours of Wednesday morning.

‌



Noah went missing from a playground in Brantham, Suffolk, at around 3pm on Tuesday, having becoming separated from a relative. A body was discovered the following day in a lake known as Decoy Pond and police say that it had been formally identified.

‌



A Just Giving page has been set up by 'Good Dads Club' in support of the family, with more than £71,000 raised already. Davis kindly gave a £2,000 donation, receiving widespread praise on social media.

‌



"That's an amazing thing to do," one user posted on X. "A lovely bloke," another wrote.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



On the Just Giving page, an Ipswich fan said that Davis had joined the search shortly after Tuesday's clash with Arsenal in the Carabao Cup at Portman Road. "Leif came down to help with the search on Saturday (sic) straight after coming off the pitch," the supporter said. "Top class fella. Respect to Ipswich Town."

Ipswich paid tribute to Noah on Thursday. Club captain Dara O'Shea and goalkeeper Christian Walton also laid a wreath at the playground where he was last seen.

View 3 Images Police have identified Noah Woods' body (Image: Suffolk Police / SWNS)

‌



"The thoughts of everyone at Ipswich Town are with the family and friends of Noah Woods at this tragic time," the Premier League club said. "We will be wearing black armbands for this weekend's fixtures, in memory of Noah."

Ipswich's men's first-team will play away to Everton on Saturday. The Tractor Boys' next home game will be against Fulham on October 10 following the international break.

Noah's father, Rhys, said in a post on Facebook that his son 'will be loved forever' and nothing can describe the family's loss. Rhys said: "Noah was the sweetest and most innocent little boy, with nothing but love to give, and we are going to miss him so very much.

‌



View 3 Images Leif Davis gave an incredible donation (Image: Just Giving)

"This was the most heartbreaking outcome for us, we were just hoping that he would be hiding somewhere obvious where someone could find him. That's what we kept telling ourselves the whole time."

He added: "It seems he has made an impact across the whole nation. You have all taken Noah into your own hearts, with all the overwhelming help, we were all just trying to bring him home to us safe and sound."

Sports.title: Todd Boehly's colourful legacy will raise a laugh - but not from Chelsea supporters
Sports.content:
Todd Boehly's colourful legacy will raise a laugh - but not from Chelsea supporters

The American has sold his stake in the Premier League club after four years in the boardroom and leaves behind a history of big spending and long contracts

View 3 Images Todd Boehly has ended his association with Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Todd Boehly, it seems, will enjoy a ‘small profit’ from the sale of his stake in Chelsea Football Club. It is hard not to laugh.

‌



To be fair, Boehly has provided amusement during his four years at Stamford Bridge. His answer to the complex issue of financial arrangements with the English Football League and the tiers below?

‌



“You could have a North versus South all-star game for the Premier League. That would fund whatever the pyramid needed very easily.”

‌



Brilliant. And then there was the time Ruud Gullit introduced himself to the Chelsea chairman.

“What do you do?” asked Boehly. With such an in-depth knowledge of the game, it was no wonder Boehly liked to visit the dressing-room in the immediate aftermath of a fixture.

Chelsea make huge announcement as Todd Boehly steps down as chairman READ MORE :

“Todd comes to the changing room every game,” former Chelsea keeper Kepa Arrizabalaga said. “He had different chats with us after different games.”

‌



Goodness knows what those chats were about. He might have tried to explain Chelsea’s transfer policy but that would have taken more than a few minutes after a match.

Where do you start with Chelsea’s recruitment under Boehly? When Boehly installed himself as interim sporting director in 2022, one of the first things he did was sign Raheem Sterling for a fee of £50million on a five-year deal which paid the player £325,000 a week.

And in the context of Boehly’s contractual dealings, that five-year deal was a short-term agreement. In January 2023, Chelsea paid £70million for Mykhailo Mudryk. They gave the Ukrainian an eight-and-a-half year deal.

‌



And we know how it has gone for those two players. In just over four years of Boehly’s involvement, the club has signed 65 players with an outlay of around £2billion.

View 3 Images Raheem Sterling was signed by Chelsea when Todd Boehly was the interim sporting director (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Billionaire bottle-jobs, as Gary Neville once said. At least Boehly was refreshingly honest about his shortcomings.

‌



At a conference earlier this year, he reflected: “I was stuck being interim sporting director for the summer having no idea what made a good football player. But knowing that Marc Cucurella, if Manchester City want him, I want him. It was really simple that way.”

Really simple. After finishing tenth last season, Chelsea do not have European football on their current agenda. They have won two of their four Premier League games this season.

“I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success,” said Boehly in a statement about his departure. Well positioned? If you include interim managers Frank Lampard and Calum McFarlane, Chelsea are playing under their EIGHTH manager in four years.

‌



Goodness knows what the compensation payments come to. Enough to pay up Mudryk’s contract, possibly.

View 3 Images Behdad Eghbali became the most influential co-owner but Todd Boehly had an input into managerial appointments at Chelsea (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

After eight months in his post, Graham Potter received a pay-off of £13million. And what was the Liam Rosenior appointment all about?

‌



To be fair, after his initial six months as a sort of sporting director, Boehly’s influence in Chelsea’s strategy might not have been as strong as some people imagined. But he was still a key figure in a period of time when Chelsea lost any sense of identity.

They were pilloried by Neville, but he was far from alone. Boehly has always seemed to be quite an affable character.

He clearly loved being involved in Chelsea. And he brought new owners to the club when the future was uncertain.

Article continues below

So, good on him and good luck to him. But on a list of chairmen who don’t really understand the game, he was right up there.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim already in huge trouble at AC Milan as bosses plan crisis talks
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim already in huge trouble at AC Milan as bosses plan crisis talks

Former Manchester United head coach Ruben Amorim is facing criticism from the AC Milan board and supporters after they were beaten at home in the Europa League

View 2 Images The pressure is mounting on ex-Man United boss Ruben Amorim at AC Milan

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale is set to hold an 'internal meeting' with Ruben Amorim on Thursday following their dismal 2-0 defeat to Benfica in the Europa League.

‌



Amorim was appointed as Milan's new head coach in the summer and has made an unbeaten start to life in Serie A, winning two and drawing two of his opening four league matches.

‌



But, after beating Torino and Venezia, Cardinale has been left disappointed with Milan's performances across their last three games, having drawn 1-1 at Juventus and 2-2 at Lazio, before losing against Benfica at San Siro.

‌



Now, according to reports in Milan, Cardinale has scheduled crisis talks with Amorim to discuss their start to the season and recent performances.

Cardinale and Amorim, as well as with chief executive officer Massimo Calvelli, are poised to sit down in the coming hours to assess the difficult period the team are going through.

Roy Keane tells Man Utd exactly what to do after JJ Gabriel exit threat READ MORE :

Julian Alvarez 'suffering' after failed Arsenal transfer as statement made before Liverpool READ MORE :

US businessman Cardinale, who brought Milan through his investment firm RedBird Capital Partners back in 2022, is expected to ask Amorim to account for the long list of flaws that he himself set out on Wednesday in the post-Benfica press conference, as well as for the statement he made about the squad to Sky Italy.

‌



Calciomercato.com add that, despite Cardinale and Calvelli's concerns, Amorim still has the full support of the Milan board and they have no plans of making a change in the immediate future.

Milan were fortunate to pick up a point against Juventus, having registered just THREE shots with one on target across the entire game. In contrast, Juve had 18 shots with five of them on target.

They then went to Lazio and had to come from 2-0 down to pick up a point at Stadio Olimpico. Although Milan were much more threatening on this occasion, they still didn't do enough to win the match.

‌



View 2 Images Ruben Amorim is under pressure (Image: Image Photo Agency, Getty Images)

Wednesday's defeat to Benfica was the most concerning of the three-match winless run, as Milan failed to score a goal for the first time this season and didn't create a single big chance.

They were booed off by the Milan supporters after the game and Amorim tried to explain his side's issues post-match, admitting that they are not creating enough opportunities to score.

‌



"This conversation of my idea is to play football," Amorim said. "To do that, we need to play the ball, but we are creating more problems for ourselves when we have the ball than when the opponent has it.

"We are trying to create the routines to have more possession in the box, we had some in the second half, but we are not creating, we lack creativity near the box.

"In the first half, when we conceded the goal, we totally lost control of what we were meant to be doing, we wanted to do it all so fast and without quality. If we look at the game, when we have the ball is when we need to be prepared for the danger, because we lose it dangerous situations for our goal."

Article continues below

Next up for Amorim and Milan is a crucial home game against Lecce, who have made a mixed start to the season having won two and drawn two of their first four matches, on Sunday.
