Sports.title: Alexis Mac Allister's dad delivers honest truth about Liverpool exit talk as Real Madrid eye deal
Sports.content:
Alexis Mac Allister's dad delivers honest truth about Liverpool exit talk as Real Madrid eye deal

The father of Alexis Mac Allister's has spoken out about his son's situation at Liverpool

View 3 Images Alexis Mac Allister has openly commented about his Liverpool contract situation (Image: Gaspafotos/MB Media, Getty Images)

Alexis Mac Allister's father has moved to quash speculation that the Liverpool midfielder is looking to quit the club amid the impasse over a new contract. Carlos Mac Allister insists it is entirely within the club's remit to decide when they wish to open talks over fresh terms.

‌



That follows a candid admission of frustration from the Reds star last week. Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch, who arrived at the club in the same summer as Mac Allister in 2023, have both been handed contract improvements this year, prompting the former Brighton man to say he was "very, very sad" about his own situation.

‌



But his father - himself a former Argentina international - has sought to downplay the matter. Acknowledging that Liverpool had yet to make contact following last week's remarks, he told Scores 365: "No one from Liverpool's management has contacted us to renew his contract yet.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"We have a contract that is valid and we are committed to it with Liverpool. And if the club does not offer to renew the contract, it is their right. For now, Alexis has to give his best for the club in every game over the weekend.

"Alexis is not disappointed. This is a decision that the club makes, and we don't judge their decisions, we just prepare for what's to come."

‌



Rumours linking him with a move to Real Madrid have been dismissed, with Carlos stating: "No-one from Real Madrid has contacted us at any point in the entire career of Alexis."

Mac Allister made his eye-opening comments ahead of last week's Champions League victory over Atletico Madrid, another club he was linked with in the summer. He said: "There were options to leave this summer.

View 3 Images Dominik Szoboszlai has signed a new deal recently (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

‌



"I think as everyone knows I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which of course makes me very, very sad.

"I think I give 100 per cent for this football club every single day in training, games. Of course, I can have very good games, bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

"I see Dominik and Ryan renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it, but at the same time, it makes me a little bit sad I didn't get mine.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Mac Allister is in great form despite his unhappiness over his contract situation (Image: Liverpool FC, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

"Of course, there is still time, the fans don't need to worry because I will give 100 per cent until the last day I am here. We will see what happens. But I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give my 100 per cent to the club."

The in-form Mac Allister, who has netted twice in his last two games, is set to feature when the Reds visit Bournemouth on Sunday.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho's telling post about JJ Gabriel suggests Man Utd have dodged a bullet
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho's telling post about JJ Gabriel suggests Man Utd have dodged a bullet

OPINION: Alejandro Garnacho may have just proven why Manchester United shouldn't worry about losing wantaway wonderkid JJ Gabriel

View 5 Images JJ Gabriel wants out of Manchester United (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Fifteen is an age usually reserved for stressing over GCSE mocks and applying acne cream. JJ Gabriel, however, operates on a somewhat loftier plane of self-importance.

‌



Manchester United's latest academy messiah has formally requested to leave the club. Gabriel is, by all accounts, a generational talent, but would losing him for nothing really be as catastrophic as it sounds?

‌



On the face of it, the answer is a shuddering yes. Gabriel is an absurdly gifted footballer, a boy who glides through midfield with the kind of precocious, disrespectful ease that makes defenders contemplate early retirement. But behind the highlight reels lies a grimly familiar theatre: whispers of a gargantuan ego and a kid convinced the world owes him a throne before he's even old enough to drive.

‌



Enter Alejandro Garnacho. Never a man to let a piece of self-involved drama pass him by, the former United starlet waded directly into the fray.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Roy Keane tells Man Utd exactly what to do after JJ Gabriel exit threat READ MORE :

Taking to TikTok - the modern footballer's equivalent of a press conference - Garnacho reposted a video appearing to defend the wantaway United youngster.

‌



It featured screenshots of the reports surrounding Gabriel's exit, adorned with the caption: "JJ Gabriel wanting to leave Man Utd after being called one of the greatest talents itw [in the world]... and he's rumoured to join other big clubs... where have we seen this before?" This was, of course, followed by a montage of some of Garnacho's goals in red.

It was a fascinating, if entirely oblivious, piece of digital solidarity. It's just a re-post, but Garnacho is clearly drawing parallels between himself and Gabriel. Both highly-rated Carrington graduates. Both apparently misunderstood by the rigid, joyless adults in the room. Both destined for bigger and better things, apparently.

View 5 Images Alejandro Garnacho reposted the clip on TikTok (Image: TikTok)

‌



But if the Argentinian genuinely sees himself in JJ Gabriel, then Manchester United shouldn't just open the door for the 15-year-old, they should order him an Uber, pack his sandwiches, and wave him off with a big smile.

Let's answer Garnacho's rhetorical question. Where have we seen this before? We saw it last year, when his relationship with Ruben Amorim deteriorated over disciplinary concerns and a failure to meet the manager's tactical demands. Garnacho did little to repair the damage, and United eventually sold him to Chelsea for well below his market value at the time.

And how has that grand pursuit of greener pastures worked out? Not especially well. Garnacho arrived at Chelsea with plenty to prove but made next to no impact - wandering through matches with the gloomy detachment of a teenager dragged along to a garden party. For all the talk of his enormous self-belief, there was precious little evidence of it, with Garnacho producing nothing but a series of low-wattage, utterly forgettable cameos.

‌



View 5 Images Alejandro Garnacho's TikTok re-post speaks volumes (Image: Getty)

Twelve months after taking him off United's hands for a cut-price fee, Chelsea threw up their hands and offloaded the winger at the first whiff of buyer's remorse. Now parked on loan at Aston Villa, Garnacho is discovering that changing his postcode has done little to change his fortunes. The same sense of inertia that dogged him at Old Trafford and at Stamford Bridge has simply packed its bags and followed him up the M6.

On Wednesday night, Garnacho was once again an unused substitute as Villa faced Coventry in the League Cup. He sat on the bench, presumably pondering his own greatness, while a team of, let's be honest, Championship players ran around in front of him - an image that sums it up perfectly.

‌



If Gabriel is cut from the same cloth as Garnacho - disruptive, arrogant and entitled - then United aren't suffering a tragedy so much as dodging a bullet. Talent can only take you so far. Being a technical wizard with a stratospheric ceiling is one thing; having the application, humility and hunger to learn is quite another. Plenty of prodigies have dazzled at 15 only to discover that potential means very little if the attitude doesn't match it.

View 5 Images Garnacho struggled to make an impact at Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

By kicking up such an entitled fuss before he's even legally allowed to buy a Red Bull, Gabriel is teetering dangerously close to the Ravel Morrison precipice. Morrison was another United prodigy blessed with extraordinary ability, only for off-field chaos and a troublesome entourage to help smother his potential. He became a tragic monument to one of the most frustrating questions in football: just how good could he have been?

‌



Gabriel urgently needs a dose of reality. He needs to shut out the noise, pull up his socks, and concentrate on playing football. That means dropping the off-field posturing and forgetting about which European giant might offer him and his father the most lucrative signing-on fee.

Manchester United clearly rate him. The pathway to the first team is right there in front of him. If Gabriel really is as special as those around him insist, his football will do the talking soon enough. Keep working, keep learning and, before long, he could be knocking on the door of the senior squad.

View 5 Images JJ Gabriel is one of the most highly-rated youngsters in Europe (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



But kicking up a storm like this at 15 is a grim omen. Whether this attitude is coming from the boy himself or the people whispering in his ear, it's a glaring red flag, one that raises questions about whether his temperament will match his jaw-dropping talent.

Having your bridge-burning rebellion rubber-stamped by Alejandro Garnacho - one of the most exhaustingly self-involved figures in United's recent history - is not a flex, nor a seal of quality. It's a high-decibel warning siren. When a walking cautionary tale becomes your spiritual cheerleader, you haven't arrived - you've lost the plot.

United shouldn't spend another second wringing their hands over Gabriel's grand exit. They should simply open the door, wave him off, and quietly count their blessings. Because if this is how the story starts, perhaps the best thing United can do is make sure they aren't around for the ending.

Sports.title: Antonio Conte 'tops Man United shortlist' to replace Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Antonio Conte 'tops Man United shortlist' to replace Michael Carrick

Michael Carrick insisted he wasn't concerned by any pressure on his position at Manchester United despite falling to a 3-2 Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton

View 2 Images Antonio Conte has been out of a job since leaving Napoli at the end of last season (Image: Getty Images)

Antonio Conte is on a shortlist of potential managers to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United, according to reports in Italy. While it's still early in the campaign, Carrick's side have managed just one win from their opening four Premier League games and crashed out of the Carabao Cup to Brighton on Wednesday night.

‌



United again threw away a 2-0 advantage at Old Trafford, with early goals from Shea Lacey and Mason Mount overturned by an excellent Brighton side. The Stretford End booed the players at full‑time and chanted 'what the f****** hell was that?', with the defeat marking United's third loss in six games across all competitions.

‌



"We all know it's there," Carrick said after the game. "We know it's there whether it's good or whether it's not good. How you deal with that is the important thing.

‌



"Being here toughens you up over a period of time, and it depends how you deal with it. You've got to deal with it in a way where you can cope with it and you can bring out the best in yourself, and whatever, however you do that, with your motivation and the confidence deep within yourself to, as a whole group I'm talking about here, that we know we can win football matches and that's what we are here for is to win.

"It feels pretty quick, as I just said about the couple of little things that go one way and we've gone out of the cup tonight, and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that."

‌

The defeat at Old Trafford, after leading 2-0, marked the first time United have thrown away such a lead in 50 years. While it may be too early to say the 45‑year‑old is facing a must‑win game at Fulham this weekend, reports in Italy have already positioned Conte as a potential successor to Carrick.

Corriere della Sera (via Sport Witness) even claims the club 'aren’t entirely sure about Carrick,' suggesting United have 'begun to evaluate his future' and that 'another managerial change could be considered soon.' Conte is said to be at the top of that shortlist.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick has seen pressure grow after his Manchester United team lost to Brighton in the Carabao Cup (Image: Getty Images)

The Italian has been out of work since the end of last season and is believed to be waiting for the right project to restart his career, with growing noise around a possible return to Juventus. Pressure is mounting on Luciano Spalletti, with Juve sitting eighth in Serie A after winning just two of their opening four games.

Meanwhile, Carrick has insisted he feels calm about his position, saying: "I don't feel under pressure. Either way, that doesn't bother me one bit.

Article continues below

"It generally doesn't bother me one bit. I understand what goes on outside and how the world works, but it doesn't bother me."

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho 'behind' as ex-Man Utd star facing brutal Aston Villa reality
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho 'behind' as ex-Man Utd star facing brutal Aston Villa reality

Alejandro Garnacho left Manchester United in the summer of 2025 to join Chelsea, but the former Red Devils forward has struggled for minutes while on loan at Aston Villa

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho moved to Aston Villa in the summer but has struggled for minutes so far (Image: Nigel French/PA Wire)

Aston Villa star Alejandro Garnacho has been given some words of advice by manager Unai Emery after missing out on minutes in the Carabao Cup. He was left on the bench for the 3-1 win at Coventry City on Wednesday night.

‌



Garnacho left Manchester United in the summer of 2025 to join Chelsea on a permanent move worth around £40million. It was this summer that saw Garnacho on the move again after making just 43 appearances for Chelsea, where he went on to sign for Villa on a season-long loan, which also includes an option to make the deal permanent.

‌



However, Garnacho has been restricted to just three substitute appearances for Villa since his move to the Midlands, all of which have come in the Premier League.

‌



Garnacho would have hoped to get minutes in the Carabao Cup third round tie against Coventry on Wednesday night, but was an unused substitute as Emery decided not to give the former United winger any time on the pitch.

La Liga clash postponed minutes before kick-off after tunnel flooded by torrential rain READ MORE :

Roy Keane tells Man Utd exactly what to do after JJ Gabriel exit threat READ MORE :

When pressed on his decision not to give any minutes to the former United star, Emery offered advice to the Argentina international.

"Continue working. Work, work, train, work," he said, via BirminghamLive. "When he can have minutes to play, try and play well. He is progressing, but we have players in front of him now.

‌



"George [Hemmings] is playing fantastic. Alysson is also understanding things well and is giving us things I want. [Ibrahim] Mbaye also responded well.

"We want a competitive team and players to compete in the style we have. Garnacho is a little bit behind because of some circumstances we had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs."

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho moved to Aston Villa in the summer (Image: Matt McNulty/Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Emery has previously made clear his desire to retain Garnacho at Villa for a "long time" as he outlined the club's ambitions for the former United star.

"We want him at the same level he was for Chelsea in the first part of last season and in Manchester two years ago," the Villa boss said last week.

Article continues below

"He is a player we have signed for a long time, and we will help him to feel comfortable and confident to get his quality."

Sports.title: Van Gerwen dumped out in first round at World Series of Darts Finals
Sports.content:
Michael van Gerwen's title defence at the World Series of Darts Finals came to an end in the first round after he was beaten 6-5 by Daryl Gurney.

Van Gerwen missed six match darts at 5-4 up before being taken to a deciding leg which Northern Ireland's Gurney controlled despite boos and whistles from the Amsterdam crowd.

It is just the second time Van Gerwen has lost his first match at the event as his difficult 2026 season continued.

"It was really hard work. I can't remember the last time I won on a major stage," said Gurney, who has largely struggled to perform on the big stage in recent years outside of the World Cup of Darts.

"I put my darts away twice because Michael had six [match] darts. In all honesty, I was very lucky to even go 5-5 and I had the throw I was like 'please I need trebles'."

Gurney earned a late call-up to the World Series of Darts Finals after visa issues caused Philippines players Alexis Toylo and Lourence Ilagan to withdraw.

Netherlands' Maik Kuivenhoven and Gurney were the highest-ranked players on the reserve list, so replaced the Philippines duo.

Image: Daryl Gurney silenced the crowd in Amsterdam (Credit: PDC/Kelly Deckers)

Gurney raced into a 3-0 lead as Van Gerwen did not even get a dart at double but the match swung quickly as the three-time world champion won the next five legs and looked on course for victory.

However, Gurney stopped the rot to make it 5-4 then capitalised on Van Gerwen's half a dozen missed match darts to break throw and held his nerve to book a spot in the second round against Ross Smith, who beat Kevin Doets 6-3 earlier.

Humphries battles through as Rock beats Bunting

Also on Thursday, Luke Humphries battled past Dutchman Jermaine Wattimena 6-4 in another dramatic contest.

The opening four legs were shared before Humphries broke with a spectacular 132 checkout (bullseye, bullseye, double 16).

However, at 5-3 up, Humphries missed eight match darts but managed to get over the line, after missing three more match darts in the next leg, to set up a meeting with Dirk van Duijvenbode in Saturday afternoon's second round. Van Duijvenbode had earlier fought back from 4-1 down to beat Sweden's Viktor Tingstrom 6-4.

Image: Luke Humphries had to fight hard to beat Jermaine Wattimena (Credit: PDC/Kelly Deckers)

Josh Rock also made a comeback to defeat Stephen Bunting 6-5 by winning the last three legs after the latter missed match darts.

Rock will play Ryan Searle, who cruised past Rob Cross 6-2, while Gian van Veen beat Chris Dobey 6-2 and Karel Sedlacek saw off Ben Robb 6-4 in the other matches.

On Friday, the first round will conclude with Luke Littler, Gerwyn Price, Jonny Clayton, James Wade and Nathan Aspinall among those in action.

Littler has won every major title this year and will look to continue his remarkable record by winning the World Series of Darts Finals for a second time.

Sports.title: MK Dons still searching for first win after goalless draw at Wimbledon
Sports.content:
MK Dons are without a win in seven League One games this season after being held to a 0-0 draw by AFC Wimbledon at the Cherry Red Records Stadium.

The hosts could have taken an early lead when Myles Hippolyte put Callum Maycock through on goal but his effort sailed over the crossbar.

They went close again in the 11th minute when Jayden Stockley flicked a header into the path of Steve Seddon, whose effort at the back post forced a superb save from Will Dennis.

The ball fell at the feet of Callum Paterson in the 32nd minute, only for the MK Dons star to fire a shot straight down the throat of Joe Bursik.

After a fiery start to the second half, Bursik made another crucial intervention to clear Aaron Collins' cut-back before it drifted into the path of Sam Nombe.

Alistair Smith almost sent the Cherry Red Records Stadium into a state of ecstasy in the 72nd minute but his long-range thunderbolt drifted wide of the top-right corner.

Stockley got on to the end of a delightful delivery into the box as the half progressed, but he could not turn the ball towards goal from close range.

Both sides pushed for a winner as the contest drew to a close but the decisive goal never came, leaving MK Dons with six draws and one defeat in their opening seven fixtures.

What the managers said...

Wimbledon boss Johnnie Jackson:

"Pride [is my overriding emotion], to be honest. I think this game always brings out the best of us at this football club. I think that was on show again tonight. On the pitch, in the stands.

"I am a bit gutted we did not win it but I am pleased we did not lose it. So yeah, a bit of a mixed bag to be honest but I could not ask any more of the boys.

"I am super proud of them. They caused us some problems for the first 20 minutes of the second half.

"I think we made some adjustments on the pitch and the lads got to grips with it.

"I think we grew back into the half, we needed to get a little bit more control with the ball, which we started to do and then we had threats on the counter-attack.

"I felt like by the end of the game, if someone was going to win it it was going to be us, but you are only a moment away from a set-piece or a long throw and I was really happy with how we stood up to that."

MK Dons boss Paul Warne:

"I really enjoyed it, I don't know why. I built it up in my head like people would be trying to hit me with flamethrowers or darts or something and I was going to be coming out with my neck in bits. But everyone has been really nice, I found it weird to be honest.

"I was prepared. Everywhere I went I was tense and I was prepared to tell people to leave me alone but there was not any of that.

"Both sets of fans were loud, but those are the games you want to be in.

"My memory is horrific. I'm not making a joke about it, I can't remember many games, but I will remember this one and hopefully later on I will remember the home game and I will remember it because we won.

"It was how football should be, it was loud, it was a bit aggressive, and two sets of committed players."

Sports.title: Chris Samba's son Floyd shines on debut as Man City ease past Norwich
Sports.content:
Floyd Samba enjoyed a dream debut by scoring twice as holders Manchester City booked their place in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 5-0 home win over Norwich.

Samba, 17, the son of former Premier League defender Chris, introduced himself in perfect style with his stooping header to open the scoring before Rayan Cherki doubled City's lead soon after.

Having assisted the first for Samba, fellow debutant Allan joined in on the scoring after dancing into the box and driving a low shot into the bottom corner to mark another emphatic introduction to the home fans at the Etihad Stadium.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Samba, son of former Premier League defender Chris, scored a double for Man City double on his debut against Norwich

Samba built on his strong start to life in the senior squad, as his father watched on from the stands, when he calmly curled home a fourth goal for City.

Norwich were denied a consolation goal when substitute Mohamed Toure's effort was disallowed for offside, meaning the visitors walked away without a shot on target registered, and Ryan McAidoo would add to their misery with a late goal to make it five for the hosts.

A sixth straight win for Enzo Maresca's side now tees up a fourth-round clash with Brighton at home in the next round.

The key moments from the Etihad

29: GOAL! Dream debut for 17-year-old Samba as his stooping header opens the scoring.

32: GOAL! Cherki doubles the lead with a neat finish into the bottom corner after latching onto an Ayyoub Bouaddi pass.

39: BIG CHANCE FOR SAMBA! The young forward takes it in his stride and breaks into the box but Bruno Alves makes a strong recovery challenge to deal with the danger before he can shoot.

48: GOAL! Allan scores on his debut after assisting the opener with a low driven shot into the bottom corner.

54: GOAL! The pick of the goals as Samba grabs his second with a curling effort into the bottom-right corner.

68: MCAIDOO DENIED! Samba at the heart of it again as he feeds in McAidoo, who has a low strike across goal which is well saved by Daniel Grimshaw.

74: DISALLOWED! Toure slots a consolation goal in but the offside flag cuts their celebrations short.

90: GOAL! McAidoo completes the scoring with a fifth goal for the hosts.

Image: Manchester City's Floyd Samba reacts after scoring against Norwich City (AP Photo/Dave Thompson

Maresca praises debutants Samba and Allan

Man City boss Enzo Maresca:

"Not just for the two goals, for the entire performance he was good. He didn't play many games as a nine, we tried in the last two or three games.

"He is very good at finishing the action. It was a good game for him. I have said since day one, I am happy with the way we are working.

"It was not an easy game. The players were serious and professional."

On the performance of Allan on debut: "It was not easy for him, first time with 90 minutes. It is always complicated but it was important for him to play.

"English competition is different to South America. He has scored a goal and an assist so overall, he is happy.

"We have many games and we are just at the beginning of the season. The ones who play tonight will play Premier League or Champions League."

'Enzo's dream start at Man City rolls on'

Sky Sports News' Ben Ransom at the Etihad Stadium:

"Enzo Maresca's perfect start as Man City boss is rolling on. Since his players lifted the tempo, they have shown more than enough energy and craft.

"To make 10 changes and win so handsomely is a real statement of intent. Not many would have predicted Maresca winning his first six competitive matches after taking over from Pep Guardiola.

"With Cherki off at half-time attention can now firmly switch towards the visit of Sunderland at the weekend, and the ambition to make it a perfect seven before the international break."

Clement blames naivety for City defeat

Norwich City boss Philippe Clement:

"The team played in a good structure, well organised and the boys were disciplined. After 20 minutes, Man City started to get a little bit annoyed because they could not create.

"Then you get the first goal and we need to do better on that cross. Then on a transition they get a second goal; we were naive.

"There are good lessons to take. We missed the right choices in the final third; we had some good opportunities. We scored a goal but it was offside.

"I saw good individual performances from players but it is hard to take five goals with just six shots on target. Those are not good statistics."

Sports.title: Sloppy mistakes cost Celtic again as they lose Europa League opener
Sports.content:
Celtic were punished again for their defensive errors as they followed up their Old Firm loss with a 3-1 home defeat to Ferencvaros in their Europa League opener.

Martin O'Neill vowed his team would get things right after their League Cup collapse against Rangers, but it was more of the same after a promising start against the Hungarians.

They had plenty of early possession, but were soon a goal down when Liam Scales turned Bamidele Yusuf's shot into his own net after Kieran Tierney had failed to deal with a cross.

With half-time approaching, Mika Baur slammed the ball into the net to pull Celtic level only for the visitors to quickly restore their lead.

Image: Mika Baur pulled Celtic level

Yusuf beat Tierney and Callum McGregor was too slow to clear the ball, leaving Kristoffer Zachariassen to flick the ball past the returning Viljami Sinisalo.

The mistakes continued in the second half. Colby Donovan, handed his first Scotland call-up this week, was caught out and Australian winger Daniel Arzani smashed the ball into the top corner.

Image: Mistakes cost Celtic any points from their Europa League opener against Ferencvaros

Celtic did have a flurry of late chances, but they could not salvage anything from the game as the fans who stayed until the full-time whistle made their frustrations clear.

It is back-to-back defeats for O'Neill's side ahead of Sunday's Premiership clash with Rangers, live on Sky Sports.

The key moments from Celtic Park:

8: CHANCE! James Forrest crosses the ball into Camilo Duran. He takes a double touch and it's past the post.

20: GOAL FERENCVAROS! Tierney fails to deal with a cross and it falls to Yusuf. His shot takes a final touch off Scales before it hits the back of the net.

23: SAVE! Arzani gets past Cameron Carter-Vickers, but Sinisalo gets down to push the ball wide.

31: CHANCE! Haissem Hassan tries to meet Forrest's cross at the back post, but Cadu is there to clear.

32: CLOSE! Hassan sends the ball to McGregor on the edge of the box, but his strike is deflected past for a corner.

44: GOAL CELTIC! What a time to equalise! Tierney sends the cross into Baur to slam into the net.

45+1: GOAL FERENCVAROS! Nightmare from Celtic! Yusuf beats Tierney and McGregor before setting up Zachariassen to flick the ball past Sinisalo.

47: GOAL FERENCVAROS! Celtic lose possession far too easily and Arzani punishes their latest mistake with a brilliant strike into the top corner.

67: CHANCE! Carter-Vickers sends the ball to Duran to cross in for Kasper Hogh, but it just evades the Celtic sub.

68: WIDE! Benjamin Nygren sends a curling effort just past the post.

72: SAVE! Sebastian Tounekti's powerful strike is pushed clear by Adam Varga.

73: CHANCE! With Varga well off his line, Nygren strikes from distance but it is over the bar.

More questions than answers

Image: It was another frustating night for Celtic

Sky Sports' Alison Conroy:

Celtic started well, and Forrest appeared to be rolling back the years as he caused problems for Ferencvaros down the left.

But their defensive frailties soon proved costly, again. The goals were self-inflicted.

How to solve the problems at the back is the big question, but there is no obvious answer.

O'Neill made four changes from Sunday's defeat to Rangers but they did not appear to make any difference.

Celtic's big summer signings like Duran and Hogh have yet to step up in the big games this season and, for a frustrated Hoops support, that is a real worry.

Image: Summer signings Camilo Duran (R) and Kasper Hogh have failed to impress in the big games

O'Neill admits he is still trying to work out his best starting XI, but he does not have too much time to figure that out.

No matter what happens on Sunday, they will be top of the Premiership heading into the international break. But they need a win - two Old Firm defeats and a Europa League loss in eight days would not be accepted by the fans.

Just months after snatching a league and cup double, is the pressure now on O'Neill?

O'Neill: We'll get ourselves together

Image: Celtic's defensive frailties proved costly again

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill:

"We're naturally disappointed getting beaten.

"It's not the start we wanted. We have seven games in which to try and get some points on the board. Really need to concentrate now on Sunday [against Rangers].

"Tonight was a European lesson for us in many aspects. We'll get ourselves together. We need to re-energise ourselves as much as anything else.

"When we have decent possession of the ball, just don't give it away. But also I think taking a few risks as well too - risks in the proper areas of the field."

Image: The stands began to empty well before full-time

On the full-time booing, O'Neill added: "I've been here 25 years ago where the crowd can react like that, so it's genuinely nothing new to me.

"I think that they were showing a lot of frustration as well. At times when we had the ball, we looked as if we were going forward and the next thing you know we've put two passes backwards.

"So those things definitely frustrate you and that's something that we'll have to try and iron out."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Banton and record-breaking Buttler propel England to series win over Sri Lanka
Sports.content:
Tom Banton notched an inspired 52no off 24 balls to steer England to a comprehensive six-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the second T20 to clinch the three-match series with a game to spare.

Banton was aided by useful cameos from skipper Harry Brook (23 off 8) and Jos Buttler (30 off 16) - the latter becoming the first player to make 15,000 T20 runs - as the home side sauntered past Sri Lanka's modest 145-9 with 7.5 overs to spare.

The victory is England's 14th in succession over Sri Lanka, and their 22nd in their last 25 T20 internationals as Brook's side continue to go from strength to strength under the leadership of head coach Brendon McCullum and new white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jos Buttler makes history in the T20 format by passing the 15,000 career runs milestone - the first to do so

How imperious England strolled to dominant series victory

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Two in two for Liam Dawson following Jamie Overton's superb catch for the first, Kamil Mishara then chips the first ball he faces straight back to the bowler

Sri Lanka's innings got off to a quick start, with openers Pathum Nissanka (37 off 21) and Lahiru Udara (21 off 20) putting on 55 runs without loss in their first five overs, but standout bowler Liam Dawson (3-32) took the wickets of Udara and Kamil Mishara (0) in successive balls to seize momentum from the batting side.

Jamie Overton (2-23) eventually sent Nissanka packing after the powerplay, and it was not long before he struck again, forcing Kamindu Mendis (12 off 8) to chop on, with Dawson compounding Sri Lanka's pain by dismissing Shanaka just three balls later to leave the tourists reeling at 95-5 having been 56-0.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jofra Archer flattens the middle stump to help wrap up Sri Lanka's innings

A determined fifth-wicket resistance from skipper Charith Asalanka (31 off 31) and Wanindu Hasaranga (27 off 22) gave the tourists some needed respite, but the ever-dependable Adil Rashid (1-18) and the impressive Sonny Baker (1-15) dismissed both batters respectively in the space of six balls, before Jofra Archer took two wickets in the final over of the innings to leave Sri Lanka nine down having set England a target of 146.

England began to make quick work of their opponents, with openers Buttler (30 off 16) and Aneurin Donald (21 off 13) putting on 50 runs in the first 25 balls before Dushmantha Chameera (1-29) and Eshan Malinga (1-27) dismissed the pair in the space of three balls.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook hits three sixes but is then caught out by Sri Lanka's Eshan Malinga

Brook, then, looked to up the pace, smashing three sixes in four balls, but was then caught by Malinga on the boundary, ending a sensational run of 311 runs without dismissal in T20 internationals for England.

His side's middle order, though, were undeterred, with top scorer Banton combining with a useful Jordan Cox cameo (12 off 7) to finish off the chase and claim victory.

Brook lauds 'special performance' - and 'ridiculous' Buttler!

Image: Brook smashed 23 off 7 balls before his dismissal

England white-ball captain Harry Brook, speaking to Sky Sports:

"Tonight was a special performance, very clinical. Sri Lanka got off to a flier but the way we fought back with the ball was outstanding.

"The way Dawson reads the game was outstanding, too. He is an awesome bowler and a great bloke. He uses all of his nous.

"Everyone bowled phenomenally and the way Banton hits different parts of the ground with the bat was great to see.

"[Buttler's 15,000 T20 runs] is ridiculous. Long may it continue. He has been phenomenal for 15 years and someone you want by your side and in the changing room."

Sports.title: Palace power past Lech Poznan to win on Europa League debut
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace cruised to victory in their first-ever Europa League game with a 4-0 win over Polish champions Lech Poznan at Selhurst Park.

Last season's Conference League winners almost got off to the worst possible start, but Mikael Ishak missed the target for the visitors from six yards out, with just three minutes on the clock.

They were made to pay moments later when Yeremy Pino intercepted a 20-yard throw across the edge of his own penalty area from Terry Yegbe, with Pino striding into the area and popping the ball into the corner.

Palace's second was even more simple, with Chris Richards rising highest at the back post from an Adam Wharton corner to steer his header across the goalkeeper and into the net.

Image: Chris Richards heads in to double Crystal Palace's lead

Pino was also instrumental in the third, intercepting on the left flank before gliding into the area where he was clumsily brought down by Radoslaw Murawski.

The referee gave a penalty and Jorgen Strand Larsen made no mistake, drilling across the goalkeeper and into the top-left corner.

Image: Jorgen Strand Larsen scores Crystal Palace's third goal

Murawski was sent off late in the second half after collecting his second caution of the game and Palace capitalised just before full-time with a nice finish from substitute Eddie Nketiah.

Nketiah had come on at the same time as Ismaila Sarr, who received a mixed reception from Palace fans as he made his first appearance of the season since a failed summer move to Liverpool.

3: CLOSE! Ishak spruns a gilt-edged opportunity to put Lech Poznan in front. He misses the target from close range!

10: GOAL! Pino capitalises upon an awful throw from Yegbe. He strides into the area and calmly slots Palace into the lead.

Sage satisfied but targets more consistency

Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage after the 4-0 win over Lech Poznan:

"Lot of satisfaction (after beating Lech Poznan) because we scored four goals in a different way with four different players.

"It was a clean sheet too, that's really important for us because we worked a lot on these things after the game in Ipswich.

"I remember during the first half and the second half, we had two periods when we struggled a little bit in the play.

"We have to be more consistent, especially with the ball, because when we recovered the ball in these two times, we gave it back too quickly because I think we wanted to play too quick forward and we need to have more control."

Sports.title: Kluivert and Rayan rock Real Sociedad as Bournemouth win on European bow
Sports.content:
The first goal that AFC Bournemouth ever scored in Europe could be heard out on the Bay of Biscay. A tradition from Real Sociedad’s old Atotxa ground, once lost but now recovered at Anoeta, dictates that a single flare is set off every time the visitors score while two are lit when the home team do; that way those out to sea know the score. And so it was that at 21.41 on a Thursday night in September 2026, Justin Kluivert found the net and a man named Juan Iturralde ran out into the street to let everyone know what had happened.

Back in Dorset and high in Anoeta, where 2,000 Bournemouth fans sang their way through this most special of occasions, they knew. They had waited their whole lives for this and it was a nice way to mark the history they made, their arrival announced to Europe with fireworks and a 2-1 victory in San Sebastián, the city where it all began for Andoni Iraola, the manager who brought them here.

Iturralde ran into the night three times – he went once more when Rayan made it 2-0 after 20 minutes and again when Sergio Gómez made it 2-1 on 57 – and might have gone more too. After a superb first half, Bournemouth had to hang on, sometimes desperately, in the second. For a while it had seemed a lead would slip away from their grasp for the fifth time in six games this season, but Djordje Petrovic came to their rescue with two astonishing saves from Orri Óskarsson in the final, dramatic minutes. They had done it, everyone at the final whistle. It had been some battle and they had given everything.

That resistance hadn’t appeared necessary an hour or so earlier. Bournemouth had waited 127 years for a first European game and considerably less for their first goal. They had been playing 10 minutes and 43 seconds and when it came they celebrated it twice. A lovely shift of the body from Evanilson started it, the Brazilian receiving and releasing Adrien Truffert. The cross was perfectly placed, bent behind the defensive line for Kluivert to score.

High in the north-east corner Bournemouth’s fans went up but down in the south-west corner the flag did too, it didn’t take the video assistant referee long to prove that was wrong, and allowing them to do it all again while Iturralde set off into the street. Truffert was on the run again soon after, Alex Scott’s glorious long, looped, curling ball dropping into just the right place for Rayan to head the second.

View image in fullscreen Justin Kluivert fires Bournemouth into an early lead. Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images

There was an ease about the way Scott had completed the pass – an almost gentle turn of the ankle, the ball delivered as if by hand – and about the way he played. Amid the speed and intensity he glided. Around him, teammates flew everywhere, Marcus Tavernier especially, and Real Sociedad could not keep up. Three times they threatened from dead balls too: Evanilson headed the first off the post, António Silva headed the second wide and Óskarsson just about headed away a third. Songs from the corner sung to a backdrop of frustrated whistles from the rest of Anoeta.

From the home fans there was relief when half-time arrived without the lead being extended. There was also a reaction, a dash from Ander Barrenetxea signalling their intent and an increase in volume. Petrovic made a superb save from Beñat Turrientes on 56 minutes and almost immediately Real Sociedad pulled one back. Gómez’s curling cross bent all the way through, past the outstretched legs and into the far corner.

This was a different game and a different place now, Real Sociedad’s version of Bad Moon Rising interrupted by an “huuy!” when Gonçalo Guedes’s effort was pushed past the post by Petrovic. Already this season Bournemouth had lost leads against Manchester City, Everton, Newcastle and Brentford, most of them late, and a familiar feeling only increased as Gómez’s fantastic ball sent Guedes through on the left, only for the Portuguese winger to try to cut inside rather than shoot. From the loose ball, Mikel Oyarzabal’s subtle, clipped shot floated onto the top of the bet.

Gómez was not their only problem. Luka Sucic shot wide on 81 minutes and then Gómez slipped Óskarsson in for what should have been the equaliser. Petrovic though saved that and, somehow, stopped the Iceland striker from five yards in the final minute.

Ultimately, the fireworks were finally over on Bournemouth’s famous night as a European journey that was once unimaginable was heard across the sea.

Sports.title: Pino kickstarts Crystal Palace’s Europa League rout of Lech Poznan to ease Sage’s worries
Sports.content:
It was worth the wait for Crystal Palace. After being denied their rightful place in the Europa League last season, Pierre Sage’s side made the perfect debut by brushing aside Lech Poznan with a victory that will take some of the heat off their new manager.

The Frenchman has big shoes to fill in replacing Oliver Glasner after his predecessor won three trophies in the space of 12 months and there had been some talk of disquiet behind the scenes following his decision to drop the teenager Jaydee Canvot at the weekend. But while Palace face a testing trip to face in-form Leeds on Sunday, having conceded 11 goals from their opening four Premier League matches, they were given a big helping hand by their opponents here well before Radoslaw Murawski was sent off late on for a reckless foul on Canvot.

The result was never in doubt after Poznan gifted Yéremy Pino a goal direct from their own throw-in, with Chris Richards and a Jørgen Strand Larsen penalty making the points safe by half-time. Eddie Nketiah rounded off the win with a late fourth and Sage was delighted to have shared in Palace’s historic moment before a meeting with his former club Lyon next month.

“I saw a lot of videos about the fans, especially during the journey in the Conference League last year,” he said. “They were incredible and I want to share the same thing with them this year.”

It’s a measure how quickly things have moved on in south London that Palace didn’t even have the chance to stage a parade to celebrate their Conference League triumph. But after a difficult start to the new campaign, the captain Dean Henderson had urged supporters to “park the negativity” when he signed a contract extension on Wednesday.

View image in fullscreen Jørgen Strand Larsen makes it 3-0 from the penalty spot. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

Poznan’s European campaign started on 21 July and the Polish champions were backed by a vociferous travelling support. They were almost able to celebrate a goal inside the opening two minutes but the captain Mikael Ishak fluffed his lines as Palace showed their defensive frailties again.

As well as some noise around Sage following Saturday’s defeat by promoted Ipswich, there have been concerns about the atmosphere at Selhurst Park after the disbanding of influential supporters’ group the Holmesdale Fanatics. But after Terry Yegbe’s disastrous throw-in helped Palace take the lead, they were treated to two more goals before the break.

Richards headed in a deep corner from Adam Wharton and Strand Larsen dispatched a spot-kick after Pino was brought down by Murawski. There could have been another in spectacular fashion after Yegbe hammered the ball into his own net just before half-time but thankfully for him the assistant flagged for offside against Strand Larsen.

The Poznan fans decided that was the moment to perform the dance they have made famous. After their side’s poor first-half performance, it was no wonder that they preferred to turn their backs. At least they could amuse themselves by letting off a series of flares in the second half just as Pino came close to adding his second of the night.

Ismaïla Sarr’s first appearance of the season was greeted with the odd boo after his hopes of a move to Liverpool were dashed in the transfer window. But the reception for the Senegal forward was largely positive as Nketiah also came off the bench to complete the job on a night that Palace will hope can kickstart life under Sage.

Sports.title: Floyd Samba’s debut double lifts Manchester City to Carabao Cup win over Norwich
Sports.content:
Floyd Samba lit up this tie with a debut that will have the 17-year-old grinning for a while after a superb goal in each half ensured Manchester City advanced to face Brighton in the last 16 in their defence of the Carabao Cup.

Samba has an older brother by a year, Tyrone, who is also in the academy. Their father, Christopher, is a former Blackburn and QPR defender.

With a game featuring speed, awareness and a poacher’s eye, he hopes to make a case for regular first-team game time. Given the elite-level forward competition this will be tough, but tonight was a fine calling card.

Samba said: “A debut like that is mind blowing. I couldn’t believe it – that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me.”

For Enzo Maresca, a sixth successive win maintains a 100% record for his nascent project (barring the Community Shield) and points to how the manager is shrugging off doubts about succeeding Pep Guardiola.

Of Samba, he said: “Satisfying for the two goals, the entire performance he was good. He didn’t play [before] as a 9, we tried in the last two or three days. He is very good at finishing so it was a very good game for him. He is not a 9 for sure but he was good.”

View image in fullscreen Ryan McAidoo (left) congratulates Floyd Samba after he scored Manchester City’s fourth goal against Norwich. Photograph: Nigel French /Apl/Sportsphoto

City host Sunderland here on Sunday. Defeat Régis Le Bris’ side and Maresca will enjoy his three-week international break. You would not bet against them doing so – City are improving with each outing, as they did against Norwich.

Many opponents are blown away at the Etihad, so for the 14th-placed Championship side to initially tap the ball about was impressive.

Maresca’s formation was fluid and reaped a first dividend when Nico O’Reilly’s cross was fumbled by the visiting goalkeeper, Daniel Grimshaw. The ball dropped to Allan and he delivered it back across for Samba to cutely head home.

City doubled their lead when Samba laid the ball off to Ayyoub Bouaddi, the midfielder hit the ball to Rayan Cherki and, as Grimshaw advanced, he beat the keeper to his right.

Watching from the touchline, Philippe Clement hoped his side were not about to crumble as the first half neared its end. He was relieved when Samba, running in, was thwarted by a Grimshaw dive at his feet.

Yet his men ended the period chasing City: an exhausting task that showed the control the hosts exerted. In a sparsely attended tie, this was precisely what Maresca wished – it meant that his main man, Cherki could be rested, as Ryan McAidoo replaced him for the second half.

Soon, Allan joined Samba in registering on his City bow. From the left, the Brazilian zigzagged in, beat Sam Field once, cut back to beat him again, then found the far corner with a lethal strike.

Maresca will have been displeased after the restart to see a Norwich raid that swooped down the left and had the ball bouncing to Kellen Fisher in the area, but the right-back missed the target.

Fisher’s profligacy was punished when Samba made himself a cert for the player-of-the-match award with a second. He collected the ball inside Norwich’s area and shaped a sweet finish into the far right corner, the helpless Grimshaw watching it sail by.

Maresca was delighted with this and also the wider picture of how his side executed the gameplan. With each win he oversees, the Italian’s authority and stature grow, his appointment appearing ever shrewder.

The game’s closing stages were lit up by McAidoo’s sharp finish: an apt end to an impressive City victory.

Clement said: “After 20 minutes Manchester City started to get a bit annoyed because they could not create anything but then you get the first goal against and we need to defend better. In the second half we were more dangerous – I saw several good individual performances, but it is hard to take – six shots on target, five goals.”

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Bees sense chance to sting Blues’ backline

Chelsea have not won this west London derby since Brentford’s first Premier League season. Each visit since October 2021’s 1-0 win, Ben Chilwell the scorer, has been a draw. This season has continued the divergence between the clubs’ respective approaches, Brentford’s solidity and continuity compared to Chelsea attempting their latest reboot. Kevin Schade, after two well-taken goals at Bournemouth, will fancy facing a defence not yet attuned to Xabi Alonso’s configurations. Only one team has won a Premier League title with a defensive trio: Chelsea’s last title team, in 2016-17 under Antonio Conte. Alonso’s attack has been rather more successful, presenting another challenge for Jannik Schuster. Replacing Nathan Collins, the 20-year-old central defender had a tough examination from Bournemouth’s Evanilson on his first Premier League start, emerging with credit. For Chelsea, João Pedro has registered three goals and three assists, but doubts surrounding his fitness could lead to Danny Welbeck’s first league start. John Brewin

Brentford v Chelsea, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

2 Spurs and Villa meet in desperation derby

What happens when a very stoppable force meets an extremely movable object? We will be tuning into the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday to find out as 19th-placed Aston Villa arrive in north London. Both teams have scored just one goal between them in the league and are desperately hoping for a first Premier League win. The return of Pedro Porro is big for Roberto De Zerbi and that should bring the Archie Gray Experiment at right-back to a merciful end. No Premier League starting XI feels less settled than Spurs – most players look as if they are a mistake or two from being dropped – which has culminated in a side that seems governed by fear and continuously prefers to take the safe option. After coming off the bench against Everton and Liverpool in the past week, the injury-plagued James Maddison will be itching to start and take some sort of initiative for Tottenham. Michael Butler

Tottenham v Aston Villa, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Mateus Fernandes will hope Spurs can get their first league win of the season against Aston Villa. Photograph: Alex Morton/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock

3 Hürzeler’s scoring express meets champions

When Fabian Hürzeler spoke about Brighton’s success being founded on them being “well structured” after their stirring comeback against Manchester United at Old Trafford on Wednesday, he could have been referring to Malick Yalcouyé. The 20-year-old Ivorian moved to the south coast in 2024 after spending just a few months with IFK Gothenburg in Sweden but had to wait until this season to make his senior debut for Brighton after being sent on loan to Sturm Graz in Austria and then Swansea last season. With Jack Hinshelwood sidelined due to injury until after the international break, Yalcouyé has taken his chance in the No 10 role and already found the net twice in the Premier League as Brighton have made a brilliant start. Champions Arsenal are up next for the division’s top scorers – who have registered 13 goals from their opening four matches – and Mikel Arteta should be wary of the threat posed by Yalcouyé and co as they prepare for a fourth away game in succession. Ed Aarons

Brighton v Arsenal, Saturday 3pm

4 Mykolenko form a boost for Moyes

Vitalii Mykolenko’s early season improvement has gone largely unheralded so far – and probably always will be among his detractors – but at a time when David Moyes needs experienced players to step up and defy the constraints of a small squad, the Everton left-back has produced. Having signed a new three-year contract in the summer, and seemingly bulked up, the Ukraine international has kept his critics quiet with several impressive displays for a defence that has kept four clean sheets in six matches. There remains a problematic lack of cover at left-back after the decision to loan Adam Aznou to Málaga for the season but Mykolenko, the better defender, has eased the concerns that surrounded his position ahead of the new campaign. Ipswich’s new forward recruits, Emersonn and Zian Flemming, will test Everton’s solidity but Moyes’s side will have made an encouraging start should they sign off with a win before the extended international break. Andy Hunter

Everton v Ipswich, Saturday 3pm

5 Jaissle refuses to delete Newcastle blueprint

As befits a lover of direct football, Matthias Jaissle likes to get straight to the point. On Thursday he was asked if, in the light of Monday night’s 4-1 thrashing at Leeds and a raft of injuries, he was tempted to perhaps switch to a back five or modify his beloved “vertical” approach when Hull visit Tyneside on Saturday. The reply proved unequivocal. “No,” said a manager unafraid to answer questions with a single word. Instead Jaissle expects his young team to retain faith in a wider vision as Newcastle – who signed eight players aged 24 and under this summer – adapt to life after Bruno Guimarães, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon. “It’s a brave journey the club is going on and I’m fully committed in that,” said Eddie Howe’s successor. “If there’s one setback, we shouldn’t delete our journey or our vision. We’re fully committed. We’re fully aligned. We anticipated that something like that against Leeds would happen. It’s on us to respond. But while still believing. We don’t change.” Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Hull, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen ‘We’re fully aligned,’ says Newcastle’s Matthias Jaissle. Photograph: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

6 Delap hopes to impress as Wood regent

Many scoffed at the £45m that was paid for Liam Delap in the summer but Nottingham Forest feels like the perfect place for the striker to regain his form. Forest previously thrived with Chris Wood as their arrowhead and Delap is something of a younger Wood regent – powerful, instinctive and willing to bring others into play. During Saturday’s away win at Villa, Morgan Gibbs-White and Delap looked as if they already have an understanding and both will be keen to capitalise against a Coventry side that has conceded eight goals in the past two games. After a nervy campaign last season, Forest feel back in the ascendancy and will have been delighted that plans to increase the City Ground’s capacity from 31,000 to 52,500, at an estimated cost of £790m, were approved by the local council on Wednesday. MB

Nottingham Forest v Coventry, Saturday 5.30pm

7 Iraola faces test on south-coast return

After watching Bournemouth make their European bow from afar in San Sebastián, a city Andoni Iraola knows inside out, the Basque head coach will return to his previous club on Sunday. Iraola – whose assistants Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper played for Bournemouth, the former captaining the club into the Premier League in 2015 – led Bournemouth into the Europa League after recording their best-ever finish. His body of work on the south coast earned him the Liverpool opportunity and a warm welcome is a guarantee. Despite the Cherries’ slow start under Iraola’s successor, Marco Rose, they will pose tricky opposition. Rose spent a couple of hours in Iraola’s company before officially starting in June and both will be braced for an all-action contest. Eddie Howe failed to beat Bournemouth in the eight league games he managed against them with Newcastle and Iraola and his staff will expect a tough test. Ben Fisher

Bournemouth v Liverpool, Sunday 2pm

8 Calvert-Lewin: man on a mission

Dominic Calvert-Lewin will be a man on a mission against Crystal Palace at Elland Road on Saturday. Daniel Farke’s centre-forward hopes to become the first Leeds player to score in six consecutive home league games since Arthur Hydes back in 1932. Managers often, quite rightly, say that players matter more than formations but, in Calvert-Lewin’s case, Farke’s switch to 3-5-2 late last November proved a road to Damascus moment. Until then he had struggled as the team’s lone striker but, paired with Noah Okafor or Lukas Nmecha, the goals started to flow. Granted, Leeds sometimes play 3-4-3 or, occasionally, revert to a back four but Calvert-Lewin has emphasised the importance of attacking partnerships. After collecting eight points from their opening four games, Farke’s team have registered the best beginning to a top-tier campaign of any Leeds team since David O’Leary’s class of 2001-02. Will it continue at Palace’s expense? Is Hydes’s record under threat? Might 3-5-2 be the answer to ending more strikers’ goal droughts? Louise Taylor

Leeds v Crystal Palace, Sunday 2pm

9 Le Bris plots party crash in Manchester

Manchester City’s maximum 12 points from their first four Premier League games featured 1-0 wins (over Coventry and Manchester United), a 2-1 victory (Bournemouth), and a 4-1 success (Crystal Palace). Allowing only two goals while registering eight is an impressive record that is only marginally bettered by the champions, Arsenal (one conceded, eight scored in their 12-point tally), and it seems a rosy augury that Enzo Maresca’s team will be genuine title contenders this season. Régis Le Bris, though, plots to halt City’s perfect start, and can draw on guiding Sunderland to a share of the points last season against the FA Cup holders, though that was at the Stadium of Light. In the corresponding fixture at the Etihad Stadium, City cruised to a 3-0 win. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Sunderland, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Sunderland’s Enzo Le Fée reacts after scoring against AZ on their midweek European return. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

10 Bobb needs to provide more end product

Oscar Bobb came off the bench against West Ham and fired Fulham into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup with a clinical late winner at the London Stadium on Tuesday night. It was a fine piece of individual play from the Norway winger but he needs to do it more often. The goal was Bobb’s first since joining Fulham last January and a player of his ability should be producing more of an end product. The 23-year-old is a clever dribbler and looked ready to establish himself at Manchester City before a serious injury curtailed his development. The talent is clear. Bobb had a good World Cup and should be full of confidence when Fulham, still seeking their first win in the league this season, host Manchester United. Jacob Steinberg

Sports.title: Europa League roundup: Ferencvaros pile more misery on troubled Celtic
Sports.content:
Celtic suffered another European embarrassment as the Scottish champions were beaten 3-1 at home by Ferencvaros in the Europa League. Just weeks on from crashing out of the Champions League qualifiers to Austrian side Lask, despite at one point holding a four-goal lead, Celtic’s defensive flaws were exposed once more.

Martin O’Neill’s team also suffered a chastening 3-0 defeat to rivals Rangers last weekend and failed to deliver on their manager’s promise to respond. Bamidele Yusuf opened the scoring for the visitors before Mika Baur equalised late in the first half. However Kristoffer Zachariassen quickly put Ferencvaros back in front before Daniel Arzani’s sensational strike, on his return to Celtic Park, capped a fine night for Ferencvaros.

“We’re naturally disappointed getting beaten,” said O’Neill. “We started off very brightly. We had a number of balls that were flashed across the goal and no one there to put the ball in the net for us.

“Their first proper attempt, really, on goal yielded a goal for them. We came back into the game, got the equaliser just before half-time and then conceded a really poor goal. We’re hit on the break for the third goal. While we had a number of balls flashed across the box, even in the last 20 minutes, we didn’t get there to the front post a number of times that could’ve kept it alive and we’re beaten in the game.

“It’s a huge frustration, obviously, but it’s also psychologically quite damning as well. It’s not the start we wanted. We have seven games in which to try and get some points on the board. Really need to concentrate now on Sunday [against Rangers].

“Tonight was, I think, a European lesson for us in many aspects. We’ll get ourselves together. We need to re-energise ourselves as much as anything else.”

Juventus hammered Dutch side NEC Nijmegen 5-0 at home with help from two ⁠errors by the goalkeeper Nikolas Polster and Marseille lost 4-1 away at Besiktas as the first ⁠round of Europa ⁠League matches wrapped up.

View image in fullscreen Nick Woltemade of Juventus battles for the ball during the victory against NEC. Photograph: Alessandro Di Marco/EPA

The first howler from Polster allowed Nicolás González to nip in ahead of him ⁠and steal the ball to give Juve the lead in the ninth minute. A goal from Kerim Alajbegovic and a penalty ⁠from Nick Woltemade sent them in 3-0 up at the break.

Zeki Celik made it 4-0 in the 75th ‌minute before Polster again ‌came out of his goal and failed to clear the ball; this ‌time it was Randal Kolo Muani who rolled it into the empty net to complete the rout.

Marseille’s disastrous start to the season continued as they followed up three straight defeats in Ligue 1 with a comprehensive beating at the hands of Besiktas, with the Turkish side scoring three ‌goals without reply in the second half.

Earlier in the evening, Greek side OFI Crete beat Germany’s Hoffenheim 2-0 at home, while RB Salzburg picked up a 1-0 win away to Levski Sofia in Bulgaria.

Sports.title: FA chair Hewitt demands Infantino release records of failed World Cup plan
Sports.content:
The Football Association’s chair, Debbie Hewitt, has written to Gianni Infantino demanding that Fifa releases all documents relating to his abandoned World Cup sell-off plan and the decision to lift the USA striker Folarin Balogun’s suspension during last summer’s tournament.

The Guardian revealed last month that Hewitt and other members of the Fifa council were lobbying for an independent review of the proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) sell-off and the Balogun controversy. Their requests have been formalised in a letter sent to the Fifa president and his deputy, Mattias Grafström.

The letter, first reported by the Times, has been sent in advance of the Fifa council meeting in Zurich on 15 October. That is due to be the first time since the FFE plan emerged in July that Infantino will meet the other 36 members of the group that acts as Fifa’s board of directors.

A number of members of the council, which comprises 28 representatives of the six confederations, eight vice-presidents and Infantino, attempted last month to call an extraordinary general meeting to hold Infantino to account over FFE and Balogun.

The rebels were unable to get the 19 votes required to trigger such a meeting, however, and Hewitt’s call for the release of documents and an independent review is also likely to fail.

Infantino has not had any contact with the Fifa council since writing to it to withdraw FFE at the start of August and has been lobbying for support before next year’s presidential election, making visits to the Caribbean, South America, Morocco and Qatar.

Balogun’s ban was lifted after a phone call from Donald Trump to Infantino despite the player being shown a straight red card for serious foul play in the USA’s World Cup last-32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. That allowed him to play against Belgium in the last 16, a match the USA lost 4-1.

View image in fullscreen Debbie Hewitt is taking the lead in holding Gianni Infantino to task despite the risk that it could affect the UK’s chances of hosting the 2035 Women’s World Cup. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty Images/PA

Fifa has said it followed due process, with the decision taken independently by its ethics committee, but has yet to publish a written report on the hearing. A request from the Royal Belgian FA for an explanation went unanswered.

Hewitt’s letter is understood to make reference to other governance issues at Fifa, particularly its response to the crisis caused by the FFE controversy this summer.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The FA’s willingness to take the lead in holding Infantino to task comes with some risk because the UK is the currently sole bidder for the 2035 Women’s World Cup. A decision on the hosts of that tournament and the 2031 edition is due to be made at an extraordinary Fifa congress on 23 November.

The deadline for candidates to stand in March’s presidential election is five days earlier. Infantino is the only candidate to publicly reveal his intention to stand, with Uefa and Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation – working to find someone to stand against him.

The FA sent a letter of endorsement for Infantino’s fourth term as president before the World Cup but, along with several other European countries, has since withdrawn its backing.

Sports.title: Tuchel considers England recall for Cole Palmer in Nations League squad
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel is considering an England recall for Cole Palmer and could include Alex Scott in his squad for the Nations League.

Tuchel’s first selection since the World Cup will be confirmed on Friday morning and the head coach has been weighing up claims from a host of players who failed to earn a place in his plans last summer. Palmer was one of those to miss out after struggling for form and fitness but the Chelsea attacker has started the season with four goals and two assists, raising optimism around his hopes of inclusion.

England, who finished third at the World Cup but faced criticism for their performance in their semi-final defeat by Argentina, have a host of players competing for the No 10 spot. Tuchel took Jude Bellingham, Eberechi Eze and Morgan Rogers to the World Cup and snubbed Phil Foden, Morgan Gibbs-White and Palmer. Gibbs-White has started the season well for Nottingham Forest and is in contention. Fulham’s Josh King is another contender for a spot.

King was one of four youngsters included as a training player for England’s camp in Florida before the World Cup. Scott, the Bournemouth midfielder, was also selected after failing to make the cut. The 23-year-old is in impressive form and was close to going to the World Cup. Scott is yet to make his international debut but is admired by Tuchel, who regretted not taking the Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha to the World Cup.

England are likely to name an extended squad as they open their campaign in Nations League Group A3 with games against Spain and Croatia and a double header against Czechia. Tuchel could shake things up, especially as some players who went to the World Cup are injured. Dean Henderson, Djed Spence, Dan Burn, John Stones and Jordan Henderson have fitness issues.

Players hoping to catch Tuchel’s eye include the Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and the Forest forward Liam Delap. The Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton is yet to convince Tuchel. Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite and Chelsea’s Levi Colwill are options in central defence and Newcastle’s Lewis Hall could provide competition at left-back.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The uncapped duo of Everton’s Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Bournemouth’s Marcus Tavernier are dark horses in attacking midfield. There is intrigue over whether the Real Madrid right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold will be picked after more than a year out of the international picture. Kobbie Mainoo’s situation is also a source of debate after Tuchel gave the Manchester United midfielder zero minutes at the World Cup.

Sports.title: Alessandro Costacurta: ‘San Siro is an icon – it’s incredibly beautiful but it’s not functional’
Sports.content:
Alessandro Costacurta lasted 15 minutes of his first game at San Siro. He was, admittedly, not playing, but tagging along to watch his older brother’s favourite team.

“I grew up in the province of Varese, north of Milan,” he says. “So as a kid I was a Varese fan. It was my brother who supported Milan. The first time I went to San Siro, I was 12, my brother was 14. I think it was Milan-Bologna. But San Siro wasn’t covered back then, and suddenly this downpour started, so much rain. We were with our dad and after a quarter of an hour he just said: ‘No, that’s it, we’ve got to go.’ So that was the first time I saw San Siro.”

But happily, far from the last. Costacurta was recruited into Milan’s academy a year later and played 663 times for their first team – helping them win Serie A seven times and the European Cup five, either side of its Champions League rebrand. Only his fellow defenders Paolo Maldini (902) and Franco Baresi (719) have made more appearances for the Rossoneri. Many of those were alongside him.

At one point, Costacurta refers to that Milan team as the “best in the world for 25 years”. He quickly corrects himself to “one of the best”. If he wanted to avoid boastfulness then let me say it for him: the back four he formed with Maldini, Baresi and Mauro Tassotti might be – for quality and longevity – the greatest ever.

View image in fullscreen Alessandro Costacurta (front row, second right) celebrates with his Milan teammates after they won the 1989 European Cup final. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

And they played in one of the planet’s most famous arenas. We are speaking in the days leading up to San Siro’s 100th birthday, an occasion that feels more profound for the knowledge it will not host football games much longer. Milan and Inter completed a joint-purchase of the stadium, and a surrounding parcel of land, from the city council at the end of 2025. They plan to begin construction of a new ground early next year.

A necessary step, for Costacurta. “San Siro is not a modern stadium,” he says. “It’s an icon, it’s incredibly beautiful, but it’s not functional.” He reels off a list of shortcomings, from a shortage of elevators to dated lounges. A mention of the stadium’s infamously grim toilets draws a sheepish grin. “That’s the first thing I wanted to say!”

It will be replaced by a multifunction venue designed by the architect firms Foster + Partners and Manica, with the area around the stadium being regenerated with new retail and hospitality facilities. The realisation of a new stadium has been a central pillar of the vision set out by Milan’s owners, RedBird, since its takeover in 2022.

The project is shared with their co-tenants at San Siro, Inter. There is something in that collaboration that reflects the nature of the rivalry – less bitter than we see between neighbours elsewhere.

“Milan is a particular thing,” says Costacurta. “It’s rare to breathe such friendly air when you go to different derbies around the world. There are chants of course, but also a lot of mixing between fans. And when I was playing, between players too.”

View image in fullscreen The camaraderie between the Milan teams was demonstrated in 2005 as Inter’s Marco Materazzi and Milan’s Rui Costa waited together for flares on the pitch to be cleared during their Champions League quarter-final second leg. Photograph: Stefano Rellandini/Reuters

Still, the games against Inter were the best ones to win – especially when your team was officially the “away” one. “When you’re playing in any great team, the biggest satisfaction of all is ‘conquering’ another great team’s home stadium. I remember a 6-0 when we were ‘away’ to Inter [in May 2001]. At 4-0 we could see their fans walking out.”

Construction is intended to be completed in 2031, ready to host games as well at Euro 2032. It will be a boon to Milan and Inter, providing revenue streams that can make them more competitive on a continental stage, at a time when Serie A – like every other league – has struggled to keep up with the Premier League’s earning power.

Even accepting all this, we can acknowledge the sadness of saying farewell to San Siro. Costacurta has visited Europe’s most famous grounds as a player and spectator. What makes San Siro unique, he says, is the steepness of the stands.

“Lots of stadiums are made this way,” he says, holding his hands at a shallow angle. “San Siro is like this.” Now he is pointing his fingers straight downward. “The first time I was out beside the pitch as a ballboy – which everyone does when you get to the youth team – it made me almost afraid. It felt like all those people were going to fall on top of me.”

View image in fullscreen Fans enjoy the atmosphere in the stadium during the Serie A match between Milan and Brescia at San Siro in May 2004. Photograph: New Press/Getty Images

“Maybe [Real Madrid’s Santiago] Bernabéu is a bit like that. But still, like San Siro? I don’t think so. In Rome, they have a different way of making you feel close – that anthem they sing before kick-off at Roma is beautiful. But it’s different. At San Siro, when you’re up there at the top, it’s like you’re in a tower above the pitch, leaning out of the window.”

San Siro was opened on 19 September 1926, the realisation of the then Milan president Piero Pirelli’s vision for a football-specific stadium unlike anything in Italy at the time. There was no running track, only four stands with capacity for 35,000 spectators.

Pirelli was said to have taken inspiration from stadiums in England, but San Siro was also a product of its setting. Stables, hay barns and storage space were incorporated below the stands to serve the horse racing track next door.

View image in fullscreen The San Siro Stadium seen from the adjacent Hippodrome soon after it was built in 1926. Photograph: Touring Club Italiano/Universal Images Group/Getty Images

The stadium was bought by Milan’s city council in 1935 and expanded with connecting sections between stands. Inter joined Milan as co-tenants in 1947 before a second tier was added, opening in 1955. In 1980 the stadium was renamed for Giuseppe Meazza, the two-time World Cup-winning midfielder for Italy who played 14 seasons with Inter and two with Milan, though it has remained San Siro to most fans.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen A second tier was added to the stadium, opening in 1955. Photograph: Keystone/Getty Images

View image in fullscreen A view of the stadium exterior in the 1950s. Photograph: FC Internazionale Archive/FC Internazionale/Getty Images

Construction of the final third tier, with a roof at last to shield supporters from the rain, was completed before the 1990 World Cup. Costacurta played the first match after its opening, a 1-0 defeat in the return leg of Milan’s Coppa Italia final against Juventus.

“I remember there was more noise, but the main thing I remember is the pitch,” says Costacurta. “They hadn’t understood how to manage the airflow with the extra tier, and the pitch was really ugly. For a year and a half, our pitch was the worst in Europe.”

Clearly, they adapted. Milan went on a record-breaking 58-game unbeaten run in Serie A from May 1991 through to March 1993. Maybe that ugly pitch even became an asset?

“I think it was a disadvantage for visiting teams that came to San Siro,” says Costacurta. “And San Siro is a stadium that puts a lot of pressure on, there’s this incredible noise.”

He switches to the English word, “Roar!”, for emphasis. He’s not wrong. San Siro on a big occasion is astonishingly loud, to the point that you can find it hard to hear people speaking right next to you.

View image in fullscreen The construction of the final third tier was completed ahead of the Italia 90 World Cup. Photograph: Colorsport/Shutterstock

View image in fullscreen Dancers on the pitch during the 1990 World Cup opening ceremony. Photograph: Michael Kunkel/Bongarts/Getty Images

“Nobody’s really talking on the pitch though,” says Costacurta, who insists the real conversations take place on the training ground.
