Managers bawling from the touchline are engaged in a futile act. “They hope they can pass a message down the line but, trust me, the message almost never gets there.”

But fans have their ways of getting a message across. San Siro still had standing sections when Costacurta made his first-team debut in 1987. “People would be holding on to the railing beside the pitch, sticking their heads out, shouting, shouting, shouting.

“I was lucky because I came through the youth team, so I didn’t take the hardest insults. They said things to me in a Milanese dialect. Insults, but amusing ones. They called me “pè de ghisa”, which means iron foot, because I didn’t have an acceptable level of technical ability for a team like that yet. But my teammates who weren’t from the youth team got proper insults.”

He won them round in the end. Costacurta laughs at the memory of the “rubbish” chant fans made for him. “It was just ‘Billy! [his nickname] Billy! Vai! Vai! Vai!” [Billy! Billy! Go! Go! Go!] The worst chant of any player at Milan.” But on the day of his final game at San Siro, thousands waited outside the stadium to thank him.

View image in fullscreen Milan supporters display a banner paying tribute to Costacurta during his final match for the club in May 2007. Photograph: Luca Bruno/AP

View image in fullscreen Costacurta acknowledges the fans after his final match for the club. Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/Reuters

Memories like that will always remain, even when San Siro joins him in retirement. Milan and Inter have said that some part of the old stadium will be preserved in the new development. Costacurta, who became a fan of Arsenal over the years too, admiring Arsène Wenger’s teams from affair, finds encouragement in their move away from Highbury, now converted into apartments.

“I played there in the European Super Cup,” he says. “Nil-nil. [Milan won 2-0 in the return leg at San Siro.] Great. Beautiful. Iconic. I think everyone suffered the change at first, but the Emirates is great now. So why not?”

Sports.title: Jamie O’Hara: Tottenham could win the Bundesliga and would challenge Real Madrid and Barcelona for LaLiga title
Sports.content:
Jamie O’Hara: Tottenham could win the Bundesliga and would challenge Real Madrid and Barcelona for LaLiga title

Jamie O'Hara believes that Tottenham Hotspur could win the Bundesliga and compete with Real Madrid and Barcelona for the LaLiga title.

The wild claim came after a clean sweep of wins for Premier League teams in Europe to show just how strong the English top-flight is.

4 Tottenham are without a goal in the Premier League, but to O'Hara, European leagues wouldn't be a problem Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Last week, the Champions League returned, and there were wins for Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool, Aston Villa and Manchester United.

The Europa League took centre stage this week with Sunderland, Bournemouth and Crystal Palace winning with relative comfort.

Spurs are yet to score in the Premier League this season and are coming into the year off the back of consecutive 17th place finishes.

However, due to the strength of the Premier League, O'Hara believes Spurs win the Bundesliga, Ligue 1 and would then compete for the LaLiga title.

It's fair to say that Jason Cundy couldn't believe what he was hearing.

Speaking on The Sports Bar, O'Hara said: "The Premier League is like a super league. No one can compete."

Cundy then asked O'Hara where he thinks Spurs would finish in the Bundesliga.

"I would say second, but it would be a title challenge with Bayern Munich," O'Hara responded.

"It would be PSG and Tottenham fighting it out, and LaLiga would be a three-horse race. I am saying Tottenham because I am a Tottenham fan, but I also think Bournemouth would be the same.

"Spurs could 100 per cent win the Bundesliga. You have only got to beat Bayern Munich, that's it. In LaLiga, it's a three-horse race, and that is how strong the Premier League is.

4 Cundy was left a little bit in disbelief at what he was hearing

Cundy then wanted to know what happened to Atletico Madrid, who knocked Spurs out of the Champions League last season.

O'Hara responded: "They are guff. They are not good. They are only good because they are playing in a crap league.

"We 100 per cent finish third in LaLiga. I don't think it is ridiculous what I've said.

"The Premier League is too strong for every other league. I watched AC Milan the other night, and they are absolute garbage.

"I am telling you, we would bop teams in Europe. Europe is guff. They are nowhere near good enough.

"It's just pointless. The Europa League is boring. The English teams get to the final."

4 Cundy's reactions were top drawer as O'Hara continued to make his point

Spending power

The financial might of the Premier League can be shown in the summer transfer spend.

And it isn't a new trend either as all top-flight teams splash the cash to try and achieve their aims in the Premier League.

But when you look at the actual numbers, they are quite staggering.

Over the past five seasons, the net spend of the Premier League is £5.5billion.

Compared to that, we have Serie A and LaLiga with net spend of £815m and £121m.

4 Bournemouth claimed their first-ever win in Europe, winning 2-1 at Real Sociedad Credit: Getty

Money makes the difference

There is no surprise that Premier League teams in Europe swat other sides away when you see the difference in transfer spend.

Then when you add in the revenue difference as well, the gap is likely to only widen.

The Conference League's inception was meant to give some teams from lesser countries a chance to win a trophy.

But from five seasons, three Premier League teams have won. It has given West Ham United and Crystal Palace moments they'll always treasure, while Leicester City and Aston Villa also went deep into the competition.

Last year, Villa claimed Europa League glory while Nottingham Forest got to the semi-final, only to lose to the Villans.

The evidence is there that the Premier League is growing stronger and stronger, and if you put teams from the top-flight in those leagues, they would almost certainly do well.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho handed major career warning in brutal dressing down from Troy Deeney
Sports.content:
Troy Deeney believes Alejandro Garnacho must look in the mirror to find out the culprit for his recent struggles.

Garnacho joined Aston Villa this summer, marking his third club in as many years, previously being at Chelsea and Manchester United.

3 Garnacho has played just 31 minutes for Villa this season Credit: Getty

However, the Argentinian winger's stint in the West Midlands has not quite gone to plan, having failed to start in any of his three appearances for the club.

Unai Emery reveals Alejandro Garnacho is 'behind' his teammates

Garnacho was an unused substitute for Villa in their 3-1 win over Coventry City in their Carabao Cup third round tie on Wednesday.

And when asked why Garnacho didn't get any game time, Villa boss Unai Emery stated it was because he'd slipped down the pecking order behind teenage academy graduate George Hemmings and Alysson.

"Garnacho is a little behind because of some circumstances we had in pre-season," Emery said.

"It is time to be patient for the time he needs."

But Deeney, speaking on talkSPORT's Premier League All Access podcast, wasn't having it.

Troy Deeney's brutal verdict on Alejandro Garnacho

"I think Unai Emery is the type of manager that hopes to get the best out of somebody for a small period of time to get them moving, and he's willing to take that risk," Deeney said.

"He (Emery) believes that the group was strong enough that Garnacho would go into that and fall into line, in terms of what everybody else does and works on.

"But ultimately, I said this when he was at Chelsea because remember, he wanted to leave Manchester United, went to Chelsea and he was going to make it better, it was all Manchester United's fault.

"He goes to Chelsea, doesn't play, moves on and now it's all Chelsea's fault.

3 The 22-year-old's stock has fallen significantly in recent seasons Credit: Getty

"At some point, it might be you.

"I don't know the kid and don't ever want to know him, doesn't look like my cup of tea. But it might be that you are the fella that's the problem.

"When you're worried about your Instagram and your six-pack and how many earrings you've got in, you just need to worry about your football.

"You're not involved in the World Cup squad and you had it all there for you, you're not involved in the national team squad because [Lionel] Messi can't stand you.

"And now, year-on-year, your standards are going lower and lower.

"Considering he came up trying to be Cristiano Ronaldo, he does the opposite. He doesn't work hard and he doesn't deliver."

3 Emery has shown he's not afraid to make tough team calls Credit: Getty

Could Alejandro Garnacho endure a similar situation to Harvey Elliott?

Given Garnacho's Villa career has endured a stuttering start, some have inevitably drawn comparisons to Harvey Elliott's situation.

Elliott joined the Villans on a season-long loan from Liverpool last year, which would have become a permanent deal for £35million had he made ten Premier League appearances.

However, Emery made clear he did not plan to trigger the obligation, which left Elliott out in the cold for practically all of last season.

Like Elliott, Garnacho's move to Villa included a conditional obligation to buy should he reach a certain amount of appearances, although it is unclear what the conditions are.

But if Garnacho cannot win Emery over, he faces a season wasted on the sidelines.

At age 22, there is still plenty of time for Garnacho to revive his career and Emery has proven capable of doing so for the likes of Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio, who both enjoyed successful loan stints under the Spaniard.

Yet if Garnacho cannot knuckle down and usurp the likes of Hemmings and Alysson, there's every chance his season is over before it began, much like Elliott.

And, according to Deeney, there'd only be one person to blame.

Sports.title: Gary O’Neil’s dad dies as Ipswich boss pays emotional tribute
Sports.content:
Graham O'Neil, the father of Ipswich Town boss Gary, has passed away.

The Tractor Boys' manager confirmed the devastating news in an Instagram post on Thursday.

2 O'Neil shared the news of his father's passing on social media Credit: Getty

Gary O'Neil's touching tribute to his father

"Thanks for everything Dad," O'Neil wrote.

"I couldn't have done any of it without you.

"You taught me football, you taught me values and you taught me how to look after everyone that's important to me.

"What an incredible example you set. I'll miss you forever mate!"

Ipswich pay tribute to O'Neil's father

Ipswich also paid tribute to Graham via a post on X.

"All at Ipswich Town are deeply saddened by the passing of Gary O'Neil's father, Graham," the post read.

"Our thoughts, condolences and love are with Gary and his family at this incredibly sad time."

Confirmation of O'Neil's father's passing came two days after Ipswich's Carabao Cup exit to Arsenal.

The Tractor Boys were beaten 4-2, although they had already conceded all four goals before the hour mark.

Anis Mehmeti pulled one back in the 62nd minute for Ipswich before Chuba Akpom added another consolation goal in second-half stoppage time.

2 As it stands, O'Neil will take charge of Ipswich against Everton on Saturday Credit: AFP

Despite the loss, O'Neil, who was in the dugout for the match, believed there were positives to take.

"I thought they had a right go and stuck at it," O'Neil said.

"It didn't feel like a 4-0 game at any point, but the quality they have meant they got into that position.

"We found a way to fight our way back into it, though. I'm disappointed that we didn't win because that's what we're here for, but there are lots of positives to take.

"We managed to get some minutes into a lot of players that need it, and we still look a threat, which is the important thing for me.

"Arsenal are a good side defensively. They don't concede many chances at all, and we were still bale to get through. We were still able to create problems for them."

O'Neil's side is next in action on Saturday away at Everton, with kick-off scheduled for 3pm.

Sports.title: Man City-bound wonderkid, 16, handed USMNT call-up in new era after World Cup humbling
Sports.content:
Teenage whiz Cavan Sullivan's stock has taken yet another sharp rise.

The 16-year-old was named in Mauricio Pochettino's United States national team squad for the upcoming international break.

3 Sullivan is the Union's third-highest goalscorer this season with nine Credit: Getty

The make-up of the 28-man roster very much signifies a new era for the USMNT, with 12 players receiving their first call-up.

Adding to the freshness of the squad is that the average age of those called up is 22 years and nine months.

That is aided by the fact six players in the squad are aged 18 or under, including Sullivan, who turns 17 on September 28.

What has Mauricio Pochettino said about the USMNT squad?

"This is the beginning of a fresh start for everyone and we are excited in these first matches to bring a group of experienced players along with some young talents who have great potential," Pochettino said.

"It will be important that they all understand our culture, our way of working, and of course the principles of how we want to play.

"Most importantly, they must show the commitment to representing the country in the way our fans deserve."

Which big US names were not included in the 28-man squad?

There are a string of notable omissions, with Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie all left out.

However, McKennie is injured while Pulisic recently returned to fitness from a leg fracture he sustained at the World Cup.

As for Balogun, he has not featured for Monaco this season following his failed deadline day move to Everton.

Despite the trio's absence from the roster, all eyes will be Sullivan to see if he makes his debut.

Mauricio Pochettino's US squad for September and October international break Goalkeepers: Chris Brady, Matt Freese, Diego Kochen, Brian Schwake Defenders: George Campbell, Sergino Dest, Alex Freeman, Peyton Miller, Neil Pierre, Chris Richards, Antonee Robinson, Miles Robinson, Auston Trusty, Frankie Westfield Midfielders: Tyler Adams, Sebastian Berhalter, Zavier Gozo, Adri Mehmeti, Yunus Musah, Brooklyn Raines, Gio Reyna, Cavan Sullivan, Malik Tillman Forwards: Mathis Albert, Cole Campbell, Justin Ellis, Julian Hall, Ricardo Pepi

3 Pochettino led the US to a round of 16 berth at the World Cup Credit: Getty

Should Pochettino hand Sullivan his first senior cap, he would not be the USMNT's youngest ever player.

That record belongs to Freddy Adu, who made his international debut against Canada in January 2026 aged 16 years and 234 days.

How has Cavan Sullivan performed this season?

Regardless, the opportunity to get in front of Pochettino will be invaluable for Sullivan, who has dazzled for the Philadelphia Union this season with nine goals and nine assists.

Impressively, Sullivan has also made 21 starts for the Union this term, underlining how he has become a trusted member of the team despite his young age.

Unfortunately Philadelphia won't have Sullivan, who operates predominantly as a right midfielder, for much longer.

As part of the deal that brought him to the club at age 14, a clause was inserted into the contract that he would join Manchester City when he turns 18.

3 Maresca is gaining one of the US' brightest prospects for nothing next season Credit: Getty

Given Sullivan is only one year out from his 18th birthday, City boss Enzo Maresca will soon have to factor in the American midfielder into his plans.

But once the move is complete, Sullivan faces a serious challenge to break into City's starting line-up.

Antoine Semenyo, who joined City from Bournemouth in January, figures as the club's first choice at right wing.

English star Phil Foden is another right wing option, although he has struggled for form and was controversially sent off in his last outing.

The USMNT face Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada in their first matches since the World Cup, which saw them exit at the last 16 with a 4-1 thumping against Belgium.

Sports.title: Michail Antonio banned from driving for six months after being found guilty of offence
Sports.content:
Michail Antonio banned from driving for six months after being found guilty of offence

Watford striker Michail Antonio has been hit with a six-month driving ban.

Antonio was charged by the Metropolitan Police after he failed to identify the driver of his Lamborghini when it was suspected to be involved in a motoring offence in London in November.

2 Antonio found himself in hot water Credit: PA

The 36-year-old told Uxbridge Magistrates' Court he was not behind the wheel that night.

Instead, Antonio said he loaned out his car to his cousin while he was away in Manchester.

Antonio claimed he did not receive the police's initial letter, which asked for the driver's identity, and suggested it got lost in the post.

The ex-West Ham ace also gave evidence he was 'shocked' to learn, back in February, that he had been charged with failing to identify the driver.

He told the court that he left his cousin to respond to the charge and believed he had provided details of the guilty driver.

Michail Antonio's punishment in full

However, Antonio was ultimately found guilty of failing to provide information regarding the identification of the driver when required.

Along with a six-month driving ban, Antonio was ordered to pay a fine and court costs which totalled £2,050.

Antonio was hit with a £1,000 fine, £650 in prosecution costs and a £400 victim surcharge.

Prior to the verdict being handed down, Antonio already had six points on his licence.

He had previously been convicted of driving without insurance in July 2025.

2 Antonio said he was visiting his children in Manchester when the incident happened Credit: Getty

The additional six points he was given on Thursday meant an automatic six-month disqualification.

Antonio also stands accused of failing to respond to West Midlands police over a speeding offence in his Lamborghini and is set to stand trial over that charge next March.

Michail Antonio's troubling few years

The 36-year-old's latest off-field woes continue what has been a tumultuous few years.

His football career changed in an instant when he crashed his Ferrari in December 2024 and broke his leg. However, the player admitted he was fortunate to be alive after the crash.

Luckily for Antonio, he was able to complete a full recovery and returned to play with Qatari side Al Sailiya.

He then joined Watford on a one-year deal in September.

Sports.title: EFL legend still playing aged 51 reveals how he rejected Man United transfer to join Class of 92
Sports.content:
EFL legend still playing aged 51 reveals how he rejected Man United transfer to join Class of 92

Jamie Cureton has revealed why he rejected a move to Manchester United that would have made him part of the 'Class of 92'.

The Class of 92 consists of David Beckham, Paul Scholes, Gary Neville, Nicky Butt, Ryan Giggs and Phil Neville, and Cureton could have been part of that.



4 The Class of '92 formed the backbone of Man United for a long time Credit: Getty - Contributor

The majority of them went on to become huge parts of Sir Alex Ferguson's early and later Man United sides.

In fact, Scholes and Giggs are arguably two of the best players to have ever represented Man United.

But Cureton turned down the opportunity to be involved.

Incredibly, after a storied career at various different levels, he is still playing football at age 51.



Cureton represents Holland in the Eastern Counties League Division One.

Jamie Cureton explains why he turned down Manchester United

And he joined Paul Hawksbee and Perry Groves to discuss lots of topics around his career and wider football discussions, including how he almost joined the Red Devils.



"Sir Alex Ferguson rang my house and put an offer on the table," Cureton said on Hawksbee and Jacobs.

"I was a Man United fan, but my dad never put me under any pressure. He said, 'it's your decision.'



"I was 14."

Hawksbee then asked why he turned down the offer.

4 'Becks' was one of the most high-profile names to emerge from the 'Class of 92' Credit: Getty

"I was at Norwich and had been at Norwich for a year or two, and I was quite comfortable," Cureton replied.

"What the younger generation won't realise is that Norwich were finishing second in the First Division and playing in Europe, and they had a team that was producing youngsters.

"Man United, up until that point, were buying players, and I felt I had a better opportunity going there and playing.



"It was the Class of 92, so I would have been in that group. The one thing they never had was a centre-forward, and I would have been it.

"But I made my debut at 19, played against Man United at Old Trafford, so in my head, I'd done the right thing because I was involved."

And of course, Ferguson wouldn't let Cureton forget.

4 In another life, the legendary Ferguson could have managed Cureton Credit: Getty

"I was playing for Bristol Rovers and played in Lee Martin's testimonial," the 51-year-old said.



"He was chatting to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, and I was only 22 at the time, and he made a comment.

"He was following my career and knew what I was doing, so that was quite nice."

Legend

Cureton made his first-team debut for Norwich in 1993 and is still playing 33 years later.

The striker has played nearly 1,100 games across all divisions from the Premier League to where he is now.



Goals have never been a problem either for Cureton, netting a whopping 402 across the course of his career.

4 Cureton has played for 25 clubs in his career

Cureton is best known for his stints at Bristol Rovers and Reading, having made over 100 appearances for both.

Why are they called the Class of 92?

The team that won the FA Youth Cup in 1992 was Manchester United.

Within that side were the likes of Scholes, Butt and Beckham, while a few of them officially joined the year prior.



And though some went on to be Man United legends, others didn't but still had successful football careers.

One of those such players is Robbie Savage.

But all of that group received coaching from 1966 England World Cup winner Nobby Stiles as well as Brian Kidd, and eight of the 14 players signed in 1991 made first-team appearances for Man United, and four of them made a total of 2,000.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer set for England squad recall and two uncapped players could get nod from Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer set for England squad recall and two uncapped players could get nod from Thomas Tuchel

Cole Palmer is set to be handed an England recall following his World Cup snub, talkSPORT understands.

Chelsea star Palmer was one of the biggest names left out by Thomas Tuchel this summer but has started the season in excellent form.



4 Palmer already has four goals and two assists this season Credit: Getty

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, part of England’s pre World Cup training camp in the USA, is also in strong contention for a place in the squad for the upcoming Nations League games.

With Dean Henderson sidelined by injury, Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, highly regarded withing the FA, could get his first senior call-up with Brighton's Jason Steele his main rival for a spot.

talkSPORT understands Rushworth is in the provisional 55-man squad as is Everton midfielder Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall. Tuchel names his squad on Friday at 10am.



England have four Nations League fixtures in the upcoming international break, beginning their campaign against Spain at Wembley on Saturday September 26.

They travel to Czechia three days later before facing an away clash at Croatia on October 3.



The final match of the extended international break sees the Three Lions play host to Czechia on October 6.

All of these matches are live on the talkSPORT network.

Palmer back in the mix

A poor 2025/26 season saw the former Manchester City man fail to make it into the 26-man squad at the World Cup in the summer.



In a campaign which saw him get affected by injury, Palmer managed just 11 goals and and three assists in 34 appearances.

However, he's started this term with real purpose having scored four goals, two of them in the Premier League. He also has two assists to his name this season.

4 Palmer is hoping to add to his 14 senior England caps Credit: Getty

New look England?

It remains to be seen who else gets the nod, but there could be first England caps earned by Scott and Rushworth over the coming weeks.



As mentioned, Bournemouth midfielder Scott flew out to America for England's pre-World Cup training camp but did not join them once the tournament started.

Scott, heavily linked with transfers to Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United during the summer, has represented England at under-18, under-19, under 20 and under-21 level.

Coventry City goalkeeper Rushworth has made just four appearances in the Premier League conceding ten goals upon what's been a difficult return to the top flight for the Sky Blues.

However, the 25-year-old has been tipped for a call-up to the England senior squad following his impressive campaign in the Championship last season.



talkSPORT understands Rushworth was disappointed not to be selected by Tuchel in the summer with Steele serving as England's fourth goalkeeper during the pre-tournament training camp.

4 Scott is understood to be valued at £80million by Bournemouth Credit: Getty

4 Rushworth joined Coventry on a permanent transfer from Brighton in a £22.5m deal, a club record Credit: Getty

Explaining the decision to pick Steele over Rushworth, Tuchel said: "Jason is a bit of a particular one because we’re planning to take four goalkeepers to the World Cup and the fourth goalkeeper then has a special role.



“The three goalkeepers will compete and support each other for the matches but they will also compete for a place in goal.

“The fourth goalkeeper in a World Cup is then a specialist. He will support the goalkeeper group, he will support the goalkeeper coach, he will support a penalty-taking group and take a lot of workload off the other shoulders and that’s why we need an experienced guy.

“We need a guy with quality, with experience and with the right energy and attitude and we believe that Jason is this guy, so this is kind of a trial to find out how this group works together for the World Cup."

Sports.title: Todd Boehly takeover was ‘horrific’ as full scale of £1.7billion Chelsea chaos laid bare
Sports.content:
Todd Boehly's reign as Chelsea chairman has been branded a catastrophe after his exit was announced on Wednesday.

After taking over from Roman Abramovich in 2022, the American tycoon and director Mark Walter have sold their 25 per cent stake to majority owners Clearlake Capital, fronted up by co-founder Behdad Eghbali.



7 Boehly has grabbed his coat and left Chelsea four years after he arrived Credit: Getty

It comes after a chaotic four years at Stamford Bridge, characterised by wild transfer business, managerial upheaval, and not a lot of success on the pitch.

talkSPORT host Andy Goldstein said: "From my understanding, every single Chelsea fan says good riddance.

"Every single one. There won't be one tear shed from any Chelsea fan.

"It's been pretty horrific, hasn't it, since he's come in?"

Ex-England striker Darren Bent responded: "The majority of their signings have been atrocious. Even the way they've run the club, the football operation, where it was buying these young players rather than buying ready-made superstars, because that was what Chelsea were.



"They still had deep pockets, but they opted to try and make money out of Chelsea and the club's ambition got put on hold. Simple as that. It was all about turnover and profit, as opposed to what Chelsea were."

Bent added: "When you look back at his [Boehly's] tenure, it just looks like someone who didn't have a clue."



So what sort of legacy does Boehly leave behind? talkSPORT.com takes a look at his most significant contributions to the club and assesses whether they were a hit or a miss.

Interim sporting director - miss

Despite knowing very little about the inner workings of top-level football, Boehly stepped in as the club's transfer chief immediately after arriving at Stamford Bridge.



Any trace of the Abramovich era was quickly eradicated, as director Marina Granovskaia, chairman Bruce Buck, and technical advisor Petr Cech all left.

7 Granovskaia was famously the brains behind much of Chelsea's success under Abramovich Credit: Rex Features

Boehly's first move as interim sporting director was to spend £250million in one summer.

Raheem Sterling, Marc Cucurella, Kalidou Koulibaly, and Wesley Fofana all arrived in big-money deals during the 2022 summer window.



Then in September, manager Thomas Tuchel was sacked and replaced with Graham Potter.

Boehly admitted himself that he was in too deep. Reflecting on that period, he said: "Having taken over in the circumstances that we did, basically the whole management team left, I was stuck being interim sporting director for a summer, having no idea what made a good football player."

Record signings - hit

Before handing over to Laurence Stewart and Paul Winstanley, Boehly spent £300m in the January winter window of 2023.

This included the record £107m signing of Enzo Fernandez from Benfica, which most would consider to be a success.



7 City signed Fernandez for a record-equalling £125million on deadline day Credit: Manchester City FC

Not only was Fernandez a key player for Chelsea across three-and-a-half seasons, they still sold him to Manchester City for profit earlier this month.

It was also around January 2023 when Boehly popularised amortisation - the art of signing players on super long contracts to spread costs and balance the books.

This was coupled with the selling of homegrown talent (and hotels) for 'pure profit' - with Boehly constantly searching for loopholes to avoid breaching financial regulations.



With the professionals now helping Boehly in the technical department, the Blues sacked Graham Potter, got Frank Lampard back for an interim spell, and finished 12th in the 2022/23 season - their worst league position since 1996.

The summer of 2023 saw more record spending as Moises Caicedo arrived for £117m - which, again - proved to be money well spent.

After two years of upheaval, Chelsea appeared to be making progress under Mauricio Pochettino by 2024, as their young team rallied to a sixth-place finish.

7 Caicedo remains one of Chelsea's best players Credit: AFP via Getty



Managerial chaos - miss

As reports emerged of a power shift in the boardroom around 2024, it appeared Boehly became less involved in the decision-making at Stamford Bridge during the final two years of his chairmanship, with Egbahli growing more influential.

Pochettino left due to a difference of opinion with the Chelsea board - and many questioned why this bridge was only crossed one year into his Blues tenure.

Enzo Maresca was appointed and delivered two trophies: the Conference League and the Club World Cup, while guiding Chelsea to a fourth-place finish and a Champions League return.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro became perhaps the two strongest examples of shrewd business under Boehly.



Both were signed for a combined £100m, less than Liverpool spent on forwards Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak individually.

Suddenly, there appeared to be method to Boehly's apparent madness, as his expensively-assembled young squad started to gel.

7 Palmer and Pedro have become one of the most prolific partnerships in the Premier League Credit: Getty

But while the American had built a strong team, Chelsea continued to come unstuck by a lack of stability in the dugout.



Maresca's messy exit led to the disastrous appointment of Liam Rosenior - and the man taken from sister club Strasbourg was sacked within four months as the Blues crawled to a tenth place finish.

Xabi Alonso arrived as a 'manager' rather than a 'head coach' - suggesting Chelsea had completely backtracked on the philosophy that forced Pochettino to leave.

This was backed up by the immediate arrival of experienced, veteran players including Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.

Selling - hit

Chelsea fans took a while to accept the shift from Abramovich's 'Galactico' approach - buying proven talent to win trophies - to the player-trading philosophy of their new owners.



Suddenly, players arrived at Chelsea as long-term investments, rather than ready-made winners.

Season Expenditure (Gross Spend) Income (Sales Revenue) Net Spend / Balance Key Transfers 2022–23 £548.0M £59.0M -£489.0M In: Enzo Fernandez (£105.3M), Wesley Fofana (£70M), Marc Cucurella (£56.8M)



Out: Timo Werner (£17M), Emerson (£13.5M) 2023–24 £389.5M £245.5M -£144.0M In: Moises Caicedo (£117M), Romeo Lavia (£54M), Cole Palmer (£41M)



Out: Kai Havertz (£65M), Mason Mount (£58.8M), Mateo Kovacic (£25M) 2024–25 £225.5M £206.0M -£19.5M In: Pedro Neto (£52.2M), Joao Felix (£45.3M), Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall (£30.8M)



Out: Ian Maatsen (£37.5M), Conor Gallagher (£36M), Lewis Hall (£28M) 2025–26 £204.0M £195.5M -£8.5M In: Joao Pedro (£55.4M), Jamie Gittens (£48.7M), Estevao (£29.6M)



Out: Noni Madueke (£48.7M), Christopher Nkunku (£32M), Joao Felix (£30.4M) 2026–27 (up to Sep 2026) £318.5M £354.5M +£36.0M In: Morgan Rogers (£120M), Maxence Lacroix (£52.8M)



Out: Enzo Fernandez (£125M), Andrey Santos (£49M) TOTALS ~£1.68 Billion ~£1.06 Billion -£625.0M

Still, Boehly did his best to turn the Blues into a sustainable winning machine.

He self-reported misdemeanors under the Abramovich regime, which the FA admitted would have likely gone unnoticed otherwise.

And in a PSR world, Chelsea under Boehly were quite remarkable sellers.



They generated around £1billion in transfer sales during his regime, including more than £375m in the 2026 summer window alone.

So despite some rather questionable signings at the start, the Blues always usually found a way to recoup and ensure no lasting damage.

New stadium - miss

This was arguably Boehly's biggest miss.

7 Chelsea's stadium remains far too small for a club of their stature and blocks them from extra revenue Credit: Getty

Abramovich specifically chose him from a long list of prospective buyers because of his commitment to redeveloping Stamford Bridge or building a new stadium, something that was close to the Russian's heart.



With little more than 40,000 seats and a infamously nightmarish logistical situation in west London, Boehly was expected to at least make some progress.

He did not.

Overall PR - miss

Boehly never did himself any favours when it came to overcoming the 'goofy American billionaire in English football' label.

In his early days, he was ridiculed for calling for a Premier League 'All-Star Game' and claiming Mohamed Salah and Kevin De Bruyne were Chelsea academy graduates.

His attitude towards the club's actual academy graduates - like Conor Gallagher and Trevoh Chalobah - left a lot to be desired among the club's fan base.



7 Many Chelsea fans have wanted Boehly gone for a while Credit: Getty

And his role on the board of Vivid Seats - a secondary ticketing platform that often listed Chelsea home matches at extortionate prices - did little to improve that reputation.

BlueCo has not been particularly popular at Strasbourg either - with the club's fans protesting what they consider to be a feeder club system.

Verdict - miss

Considering the billions involved, all Boehly has to show for four years at Chelsea is one fourth-place finish and two trophies, neither of which were the big four domestic prizes.



Off the pitch, his lack of progress over a new stadium and various unpopular schemes made him difficult for Chelsea fans to like, as shown by widespread protests against BlueCo.

The club's transfer business might not end up being quite as disastrous as it once appeared, with a strong squad and a clear knack for selling unwanted talent.

But at best, Boehly left with the transition from Abramovich still unfinished.

Chelsea league finishes during Boehly reign 2022/23: 12th 2023/24: 6th 2024/25: 4th 2025/26: 10th

At worst, it was a failure.

Sports.title: Martin O'Neill admits his Celtic side were taught a harsh European lesson in timid defeat to Ferencvaros
Sports.content:
Exasperated Celtic boss Martin O’Neill insisted his side were given a European lesson as they crashed to a demoralising home defeat to Ferencvaros in their Europa League opener.

Already hurting from their bruising 3-0 Premier Sports Cup quarter-final defeat to Rangers at Ibrox last weekend, O’Neill’s men failed to lift spirits in the east end of Glasgow as they slumped to a thoroughly unconvincing loss to a side currently sitting fifth in the Hungarian top flight.

To rub salt in the wounds, one-time Celtic winger Daniel Arzani tormented his former side with an impressive display and a killer third goal shortly after the interval.

The visitors had gone in front through Bamidele Yusuf’s deflected shot but Celtic levelled in the 44th minute through Mika Baur.

However, in an all too familiar European collapse from the home side, they conceded a goal to Kristoffer Zachariassen a minute later to leave O’Neill cursing their fragility.

The Celtic manager said: ‘It’s a huge frustration, obviously, but it’s also psychologically quite damning as well.

Martin O'Neill admitted Celtic didn't take enough risks in Europa League defeat to Ferencvaros

‘Just when you’ve fought your way back into the game and you think, well if you can’t deal with the minute the fourth official puts up, at least defend it properly and we didn’t do that. That was really disappointing.

‘It’s not the start we wanted. We have seven games in which to try and get some points on the board. Tonight was I think a European lesson for us in many aspects.’

O’Neill insisted his side have to be braver – starting with Sunday’s crucial Premiership clash with Rangers at Celtic Park.

‘When we have decent possession of the ball, just don’t give it away,’ he said. ‘But also I think taking a few risks as well too — risks in the proper areas of the field.

‘We really need to concentrate now on Sunday [against Rangers]. We’ll get ourselves together. We need to re-energise ourselves as much as anything else.’

O’Neill had shaken up his team following their Ibrox defeat last weekend, with misfiring striker Kasper Hogh dropping to the bench and Camilo Duran selected to start up front.

Viljami Sinisalo and the Celtic defence react in horror after Kristoffer Zachariassen's goal

There was also a change between the sticks as Sam Johnstone – shaky in the Premier Sports Cup defeat to Rangers – was dropped for Viljami Sinisalo.

Asked by TNT Sports trackside reporter Connie McLaughlin to explain his thinking behind the decision to replace Johnstone with Sinisalo, O’Neill snapped: ‘No, I won’t talk to you about the thinking behind that there. Sinisalo was always going to play.

‘Believe it or not Connie, my job is not to explain every single situation to you, much as you are going to ask and I’m delighted you are.’

When pressed by McLaughlin over the fact supporters might want to hear his reasoning, O’Neill replied: ‘Well, why don’t I tell the fans through Celtic TV?’

Sports.title: A new star is born for Man City as Floyd Samba's double steals the show, how Allan fared on his long-awaited debut and Enzo Maresca copies from the Pep Guardiola playbook in 5-0 thrashing of Norwich
Sports.content:
A new star is born for Man City as Floyd Samba's double steals the show, how Allan fared on his long-awaited debut and Enzo Maresca copies from the Pep Guardiola playbook in 5-0 thrashing of Norwich

Rayan Cherki raced back to halfway. He'd just given former Manchester City academy graduate Daniel Grimshaw the eyes, a second home goal of the evening, and then compelled to get the tie restarted as quickly as possible.

Clearly, Cherki wanted more goals. More opportunity to make up for the lost half at Old Trafford last weekend, when he was withdrawn at the break owing to Phil Foden's red card. More opportunity to have some fun. Maybe to prove a point, if such things are possible on a straightforward Thursday night against Championship opposition, although Maresca visibly sighed at some flicks.

Fortunately for Mathias Kvistgaarden, his wits were very much about him by the time Cherki had made it back to the centre circle, hurling the ball in the Dane's direction. With impressively quick hands, Kvistgaarden just about stopped it from bursting through his fingers.

The trouble was, the majority of City's players were still celebrating up the other end after two goals in as many minutes on the half-hour had effectively secured their spot in round four here against Brighton.

And despite Cherki's efforts, the evening really belonged to a 17-year-old who first set foot on this campus as a junior.

Rayan Cherki was on the scoresheet as Manchester City beat Norwich 5-0 in the Carabao Cup

FAMILY AFFAIR

When all eyes were on JJ Gabriel of Manchester United, Floyd Samba curled home a wonderful 25-yard free kick in last May's FA Youth Cup final. A genuine moment of class. The pedigree was there for all to see.

Just four months later, he has topped that - and then some.

His mother, Theresa, was already emotional before Ruebyn Ricardo blew the first whistle. Sat next to Tyrone, the older brother also in City's ranks, she was crying as the teams lined up and spotted her son among them. To be fair, with the blonde locks, he is tricky to miss.

Samba's opener, heading in other outfield debutant Allan's cross, was reward for a tremendous bow as a senior player. Usually an attacking midfielder, Samba - son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Chris, also sat with pride in the corporate Tunnel Club - was thrown up front and linked play brilliantly.

For Cherki's goal, it was Samba dropping off the front and laying to Ayyoub Bouaddi that made the move. Intelligence City approve of. By the time Samba curled home from the edge of the box to secure a brace after half-time, a sumptuous effort, Chris was leaping in the air in much the same way as Premier League strikers had witnessed for so many years previous.

'A debut like that is mind blowing,' said an ecstatic Samba who only found out he was in the team on Tuesday. 'I couldn't believe it myself - but that's just the beginning, I've got a big career ahead of me.'

This experience must whet the appetite of another son in City's academy, Emerson, a central defender in the club's Under 13s. Samba Sr was later gladly taking the adulation from other parents behind the dugouts on yet another occasion that shows off what the youth setup has put together in these parts - especially in the context of what has happened over the road with Gabriel this week.

That two other teenagers who featured, Ryan McAidoo and Kaden Braithwaite, also starred in May's Under 18s final speaks volumes. And McAidoo's top finish in stoppage time was further testament to the ability of those coming through.

Floyd Samba had plenty to smile about after a goalscoring debut during Manchester City's win

THE KEY FOR ALLAN

City had been tracking Allan, the 22-year-old winger signed from Palmeiras last month, for some time. Director of football Hugo Viana says for the past two years and there is a belief that he can be moulded into a useful option.

Viana has instructed staff to give the Brazilian - who hails from Florianopolis, an island off the country's southern coast - the time required to adapt to life in England. They think he can operate on either side, evidenced here, but are pleading for patience.

MATCH RATINGS Man City (3-1-5-1): Rulli 7; Khusanov 7, Reis 7, Bouaddi 7; Allan 8 (Braithwaite 71, 6), Lewis 7, Cherki 8 (McAidoo 46, 7), O’Reilly 7, Ait-Nouri 7; Samba 9 Manager: Enzo Maresca 7 Norwich City (4-2-3-1): Grimshaw 5; Fisher 6, Darling 6, Alves 6 (McConville 71, 6), Yongwa 6; Wright 6, Field 5; Crnac 6 (Musaba 62, 6), Slimane 5 (Toure 71, 6), Diallo 5 (Maghoma 46, 6); Kvistgaarden 6 Manager: Philippe Clement 6 Referee: Ruebyn Ricardo 7

There is probably good reason for that - marker Darlin Yongwa occasionally more physical in duels - but the debut will go down as a triumph.

‘It was not easy for him, his first start, it's always complicated but it was important for him to see a little bit the English competition,' said Maresca post-match.

'That is a bit different from South America so overall it was good.’

Allan's instinctive half-volleyed cross for Samba's opener showed strong instincts. More of that was seen three minutes after half time, chopping from left foot to right and then squirming past Grimshaw – a goal that will do him no harm and the Etihad Stadium's south stand appeared quickly to fashion a terrace chant to the tune of 'I Predict a Riot' by Kaiser Chiefs.

Even so, there were signs that Allan may be here for other reasons too. Palmeiras have utilised him as a wing back in recent months and in his final game for the club, a 4-1 win over Vasco, he did most of his best work tracking back.

That was obvious inside five minutes of his City debut, tracking in behind right back Rico Lewis to thwart a threatening Norwich counter that had the hosts briefly scrambling for position.

'Coming to the Premier League from Brazil is a big step but we also believe that he will be an important player in that position,' Viana said.

Allan impressed for City and was also on the scoresheet during the third-round cup victory

NORWICH HAD THEIR OWN BRAZILIAN TALENT ON SHOW

Allan was not the only young Brazilian unfamiliar with the English game. Bruno Alves, a 21-year-old central defender, signed on loan from Cruzeiro in the summer and Norwich have an option to purchase at around £2million in the summer.

Alves had only featured for 70 minutes so far this season but challenges like this are seen as key in his development.

ENZO THE ECCENTRIC

It's already become clear that Maresca will not pass up the chance to lean into his tactical creativity and the sight of City's formation in the opening 20 minutes underlined some similarities with his predecessor.

Three at the back – but one of them was holding midfielder Bouaddi, with the Moroccan having to check himself a couple of times into remembering exactly where he was playing in different phases of the game.

Mateo Kovacic held midfield on his own and then the other six – including the goalscorers, Lewis, Rayan Ait-Nouri and Nico O'Reilly – ploughed forward. This could potentially be some sort of blueprint for league matches where City expect the opposition to sit in deep.

Perhaps the biggest takeaway for Maresca himself, though, was that Erling Haaland had the entire night off - not even on the bench.

Sports.title: CELTIC 1 FERENCVAROS 3: It's another European horror show for Celtic as alarm bells begin to sound at Parkhead
Sports.content:
CELTIC 1 FERENCVAROS 3: It's another European horror show for Celtic as alarm bells begin to sound at Parkhead

At the end of his pre-match press conference on Wednesday, a visiting journalist invited Martin O’Neill to give a simple answer to a simple question.

The inquisitor asked the Northern Irishman if he saw a Celtic victory as the only acceptable outcome of the Europa League opener with Ferencvaros. In cricket parlance, it was a straight delivery.

O’Neill’s answer prompted a double take from those assembled in the Jock Stein Suite. He didn’t necessarily see it that way, he insisted.

Listen, perhaps there was an element of the veteran trying to take some of the burden off his players after a tough few days. An old trick from the managerial playbook.

But he wasn’t pulling the wool over anyone’s eyes. Celtic had to win here and had to win well. How could it possibly be any other way?

To capitulate in Linz against LASK in the Champions League play-off was bad enough. To deliver such a spineless display in the Premier Sports Cup at Ibrox really sent alarm bells ringing.

Kieran Tierney and captain Callum McGregor react at full-time after another Celtic horror show

Questions pertaining to the side’s make-up had come from all quarters since they folded like a cheap suit on Sunday.

O’Neill asked plenty of his own in the same media conference, mostly about the character of his players.

If he thought his pointed words would prompt a response from a group of which were hurting after failing to turn up in the derby, though, he was sorely mistaken.

This was another desperate affair for the Northern Irishman and his beleaguered side. Second best against a Ferencvaros side presently sitting fifth in their own league, there was little evidence of improvement from the diabolical display they turned in against Rangers.

On Sunday, skipper Callum McGregor opined that Celtic looked like a team of individuals. Nothing, it seems, changed in the four intervening days.

Not only does this Celtic side lack quality and creativity, it has no heart or grit. At the first sign of trouble, the players go weak at the knees.

A promising start to the season feels like it happened an age ago. If the club hasn’t yet reached crisis point, then it’s now well within sight. Right now, the visit of Rangers in the league on Sunday holds limited appeal.

One-time Celtic winger Daniel Arzani scored a brilliant third for the visitors to silence Parkhead

The team is a mess and right now neither O’Neill or his backroom staff look like they know how to fix it. This season could all unravel very quickly.

Deservedly behind, Celtic levelled with a minute of the first period remaining through Mika Baur and still managed to go in behind at the break. From the minute the visitors struck again two minutes into the second half, the game was up.

O’Neill really had no option but to shake things up. Having been dropped for two games without doing a great deal wrong, Viljami Sinisalo returned in goal at Sam Johnstone’s expense.

Oliver Sorensen displaced Benjamin Nygren with Camilo Duran filling Kasper Hogh’s role as the striker. Haissem Hassan replaced Duran on the right with James Forrest in for Seb Tounekti.

The Hungarians’ left-winger would have been vaguely familiar to the home fans. There were high hopes for Daniel Arzani when he arrived at Celtic on a two-year loan from Manchester City in 2018 only for a crucial ligament injury to restrict him to two appearances.

The Australian certainly made a point of underscoring his credentials upon his return to Glasgow with a quite brilliant strike to complete the scoring.

Celtic actually started brightly. You might argue that anything had to be an improvement on their efforts at the weekend.

Arzani's curling strike gave the visitors a two-goal lead that Celtic were unable to recover from

With Kieran Tierney and Forrest seeking an immediate breakthrough, the home side forced three corners in the opening three minutes.

What does it say about Celtic’s recruitment over so many years that Forrest, now aged 35, is still one of the best players at the club?

After dropping the shoulder, the winger set up Duran with the Colombian volleying just wide. Forrest then went alone after leaving Oliver Nagy in his wake. He went for the glory when there were better options and Adam Varga beat away his shot. And with that, Celtic’s early surge fizzled out.

It all became very slow and predictable. If there was an easy option to take it, one of O’Neill’s players did exactly that.

Realising there was little to fear, Ferencvaros grew into the contest. Bamidele Yusuf had all the time he wanted to pick out Kristoffer Zachariassen. The skipper headed just over.

The warning shot wasn’t heeded. On the 20-minute mark, Yusuf again gathered on the right and was afforded time to do as he pleased. He fired the ball in the general direction of goal. Liam Scales’ outstretched leg did Sinisalo no favours and the Hungarians were ahead.

How would Celtic react to adversity? Predictably, by going into their shells and making bad decision after bad decision.

When Baur jumped to try and win a ball he should have left alone, Yusuf fed Arzani. The Australian got the better of Cameron Carter-Vickers but not Sinisalo.

Martin O'Neill now faces a lot of serious questions and a crucial home game against Rangers

The frustration among the home fans was growing. A smartly worked short corner allowed McGregor to try his luck only for a deflection to preserve Ferencvaros’ lead.

Duran’s speculative effort from 30 yards was typical of Celtic’s lack of imagination. Their equaliser on the stroke of half-time came out of the blue.

Forrest again justified his selection with a typically precise pass to find Tierney, who’d ghosted in behind. Baur smartly held his run, took the cut-back in his stride and swept the ball home with his left foot.

The clock said 44 minutes. For Celtic to fail to go up the tunnel level at half-time was grossly negligent.

It was another desperate defensive episode. Yusuf beat Tierney all too easily then popped the ball through McGregor’s legs. As he rolled the ball across goal, Celtic’s defenders just stared at each other. This time Zachariassen didn’t miss.

O’Neill withdrew Sorensen and threw on Hogh at the break as he went to a 4-4-2. Hopes that a change of shape would bring about a change of fortune lasted all of two minutes.

Another cheap turnover by Colby Donovan saw Yusuf emerge with the ball. He fired a superb pass across the pitch to Arzani. With Carter-Vickers backing off, the winger smashed the ball into the top corner from the edge of the box. Ferencvaros were threatening to run riot.

O’Neill threw on a raft of substitutes hoping that something or someone would change the flow of the game.

Nygren curled one effort wide and chipped another onto the roof of the net from 35 yards. Tounekti forced the keeper into a smart stop after some neat footwork. A consolation would have been more than Celtic deserved.

Sports.title: Bring back Cole Palmer? Throw Rio Ngumoha into the mix? And should Trent Alexander-Arnold be given a second chance? Our experts pick their England squads ahead of Thomas Tuchel's big selection
Sports.content:
Bring back Cole Palmer? Throw Rio Ngumoha into the mix? And should Trent Alexander-Arnold be given a second chance? Our experts pick their England squads ahead of Thomas Tuchel's big selection

The first international break of the season is almost upon us and while the World Cup scars are still healing, England must now regroup and build again.

It's an unprecedented stretch, with Thomas Tuchel having three weeks to work with his players.

The Three Lions have four Nations League games, starting with a the toughest of examinations against world champions Spain at Wembley.

Then there are two games against Czechia either side of a meeting with familiar foes Croatia and it will be fascinating to see how the manager develops his side.

We'll find out which players make the cut on Friday, so ahead of the official selection, our experts have picked who they think should be included.

OLIVER HOLT

I don’t think Thomas Tuchel will include Trent Alexander-Arnold when he names his squad for England’s upcoming Nations League fixtures against Spain, Croatia and the Czech Republic but he should.

Tuchel excused his moribund tactics in England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina by saying his players don’t have the technique to keep the ball under pressure.

HOLT'S SQUAD: Goalkeepers: Pickford, Trafford, Henderson Defenders: Alexander-Arnold, James, Branthwaite, Konsa, Guehi, Colwill, Hall, O’Reilly Midfielders: Mainoo, Wharton, Bellingham, Gibbs-White, Anderson, Rice Forwards: Rogers, Palmer, Kane, Saka, King, Gordon

If he can’t coach that, then maybe he should pick England’s best technical players instead of exiling them. Alexander-Arnold would be near the front of that queue and so would Morgan Gibbs-White and Cole Palmer.

Tuchel needs to accept he fell short in the United States this summer, as well as his players, and that means making some changes.

It should lead to recalls for the likes of Kobbie Mainoo and Adam Wharton to supplement star names such as Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers.

I have seen Josh King play for Fulham this season and was incredibly impressed not just with his ability but also his attitude.

We are at the start of a new cycle and it is time to give the 19-year-old his opportunity.

Trent Alexander-Arnold should be included in Thomas Tuchel's England squad

IAN LADYMAN

It’s a tough squad to pick because not only does Thomas Tuchel have to keep an eye on the future, he also has to win games to make sure England do well in the Nations League. The first game is also against the World champions, Spain, and if England lose Tuchel will be under pressure heading to Prague for game two.

LADYMAN'S SQUAD: Goalkeepers: Pickford, Trafford, Henderson Defenders: James, Livramento, Alexander-Arnold, Guehi, Konza, Branthwaite, Hall, O’Reilly Midfielders: Mainoo, Anderson, Rice, Rogers, Scott, Bellingham Forwards: Rashford, Gordon, Saka, Palmer, Kane, Calvert-Lewin

In summary, I think it’s time to move on from the Dan Burn-Jordan Henderson ‘good tourist’ era and pick 23 players actually capable of starting a big game for England.

There are a bunch who are in on form – Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Alex Scott, Elliot Anderson etc – and another who are in because they are our best players. The likes of Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold (who has zero chance of actually being in) and Marcus Rashford are in that group.

At the back, Everton’s Jarrod Branthwaite is a wild card but he is talented and, now that he is free from injury, it’s time for him to step up.

Jarrad Branthwaite has started the season on brilliant form for Everton

CRAIG HOPE

HOPE'S SQUAD Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford, James Trafford, Dean Henderson Defenders: Reece James, Djed Spence, Marc Guehi, Ezri Konsa, John Stones, Jarrad Branthwaite, Nico O’Reilly, Lewis Hall Midfielders: Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice, Elliot Anderson, Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer, Alex Scott, Josh King Forwards: Harry Kane, Liam Delap, Bukayo Saka, Anthony Gordon, Rio Ngumoha

If we work off the premise of 20 outfield players and two for each position, I have accommodated both Rogers and Palmer at the expense of a second left winger, meaning Rogers would likely be the deputy in that role behind Gordon.

Max Dowman would be my back up to Gordon, but perhaps that is one for the second half of the season.

Delap’s strong start at Forest – he was awesome at the weekend – gets him the nod ahead of Calvert-Lewin, who also looks in fantastic shape.

Ngumoha, King and Scott deserve elevation to the senior ranks and represent the future, while it’s time for Branthwaite to stamp his mark as an England international. When fit, I think he should be a starter.

That squad has a nice blend of youth and experience.

Cole Palmer's inclusion could raise the technical level of the squad and freshen it up

JACK GAUGHAN

GAUGHAN'S SQUAD: Goalkeepers: Pickford, Trafford, Rushworth Defenders: Guehi, Konsa, James, Colwill, O’Reilly, Quansah, Spence, Hall Midfielders: Anderson, Bellingham, Rice, Rogers, Gibbs-White, Scott, Eze Forwards: Kane, Palmer, Gordon, Saka, Rashford

A couple of injuries, notably to John Stones, have laid bare a lack of depth in certain positions. A few newer or returning faces – Colwill, Gibbs-White, Scott, Palmer – should freshen the squad up ahead of four matches where England will have to find different ways of playing.

Harry Kane is the only out and out striker in the group of 23, with Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney having not forced their way into Thomas Tuchel’s thinking during the World Cup.

The likes of Gordon and Palmer have played as false nines for England’s age group teams and could offer alternative options in the way the Three Lions attack teams. Phil Foden has done that to good effect at Manchester City too but needs a stronger run of performances before earning a recall.

Sports.title: Why Pierre Sage deserves patience at Crystal Palace amid troubled start as Eagles begin Europa League campaign with comfortable 4-0 win over Lech Poznan, writes WILL PICKWORTH
Sports.content:
Why Pierre Sage deserves patience at Crystal Palace amid troubled start as Eagles begin Europa League campaign with comfortable 4-0 win over Lech Poznan, writes WILL PICKWORTH

It hasn't been the smoothest start to life in England for Pierre Sage but he took an important step in the right direction as Crystal Palace marked their long-awaited Europa League debut with a thumping 4-0 victory over Lech Poznan.

Yeremy Pino opened the scoring, with Chris Richards and Jorgen Strand Larsen adding further first-half goals before Eddie Nketiah completed the rout late on.

Sage's side were perhaps flattered by the scoreline thanks to some woeful Poznan defending - including a kamikaze 35-yard own goal from Terry Yegbe that was disallowed for offside after he threw the ball straight to Pino for the opener - yet they looked threatening every time they attacked.

Promising patterns of play were on display, and Palace looked a lot more comfortable on the ball than on many of their European nights here last season.

Sage has barely been able to call upon Jean-Philippe Mateta or Ismaila Sarr, in the squad for the first time this season, yet it's now 13 goals in six games in all competitions for his side.

One worry will be Palace's defence, the leakiest in the Premier League, and although they kept a clean sheet here, Poznan squandered several chances.

Crystal Palace kicked off their Europa League campaign with a 4-0 victory over Lech Poznan

Yeremy Pino scored and won a penalty on an impressive night for the Spanish attacker

Crystal Palace 4-0 Lech Poznan: MATCH FACTS Crystal Palace (3-4-2-1): Benitez 7.5; Richards 7.5 (Canvot 73, 7), Disasi 7.5, Ahanor 7; Khalail 7 (Mingueza 61, 6.5), Timber 7.5 (McNeil 61, 7), Wharton 7.5 (C), Mitchell 7; Kamada 8 (Nketiah 73, 7), Pino 8.5; Strand Larsen 7.5 (Sarr 73, 6.5) Subs not used: Matthews (GK), Benetto (GK), Chilwell, Osorio, Tomiyasu, Williams Manager: Pierre Sage 7.5 Goalscorers: Pino 10, Richards 27, Strand Larsen 35 pen, Nketiah 89

In fairness to Sage, just two members of his back-five played regularly here last season - plus back-up keeper Walter Benitez is currently filling in for the injured Dean Henderson - and they will surely improve with time as their understanding develops.

Axel Disasi made some important interventions as he attempted to make up for his red card on Saturday, while Quinten Timber is a smart addition in midfield.

'There's still a lot to work on, it's still early days with lots of new signings,' Palace skipper Adam Wharton said post-match.

'We are trying to gel as fast as we can. It has been a slow start but tonight was a great step forward.'

Sage will be particularly pleased with the performance of Pino as the attacking midfielder continues to go from strength-to-strength under his leadership.

The Spaniard showed signs of his quality during his first season in English football but often appeared shorn of confidence as he adapted to a more physical style of play.

Now a World Cup winner, he reminded everyone just how good he can be.

His opener may have been gift-wrapped by the Poznan defence, yet Pino still demonstrated great poise and skill to take it past another defender and finish.

At times, he ran the show, won a penalty with more trickery and wasn't afraid to take on shots from distance.

With Sarr now back in the fold, and Mateta not too far away, Sage's attacking options appear to be in good shape.

It was an important result for Pierre Sage after a difficult start to life in South London

There was always likely to be a slight drop-off and transition after Oliver Glasner's departure, but there are plenty of signs that Sage's football can be a success in South London and he deserves the time to prove that.

'There's a lot of satisfaction because we scored four goals with four different players and a clean sheet too,' Sage added. 'That’s really important for us because we worked a lot on these things after Ipswich (Saturday's 3-2 defeat).

'We had two periods when we struggled a bit. We have to be more consistent, especially with ball. We give it back too quickly because I think we want to play quickly. We need to have more control.'

Sports.title: Gary O'Neil announces death of his father as Ipswich boss pays emotional tribute to 'incredible example'
Sports.content:
Gary O'Neil announces death of his father as Ipswich boss pays emotional tribute to 'incredible example'

Ipswich manager Gary O'Neil has paid a heartfelt tribute to his father as he announced his passing.

O'Neil took to Instagram to reveal the news, with his club leading the tributes in the comment section.

'Thanks for everything Dad!' the 43-year-old wrote. 'I couldn't have done any of it without you.

'You taught me football, you taught me values and you taught me how to look after everyone that's important to me.

'What an incredible example you set!! 'I'll miss you forever mate!

'Rest in peace, Dad!! Love you.'

Gary O'Neil has paid a heartfelt tribute to his father as he announced his passing

O'Neil said his dad was a 'great example' to him and that he will 'miss you forever'

Tributes flooded in from the footballing world, with Ipswich's official account commenting: 'The thoughts of everyone at Ipswich Town are with you and your family at this incredibly sad time, Gary.'

Aston Villa midfielder Joao Gomes, who played under O'Neil at Wolves, wrote, accompanied by a sad emoji: 'I'm sorry for you, Boss.'

O'Neil's daughter, Summer-Mae, wrote: 'Love you,' accompanied by a red heart emoji.

The former midfielder is in his first weeks in charge of Ipswich, having been appointed in the summer to replace Kieran McKenna.

He has so far led his side to two wins and two defeats in their four Premier League matches this season, and the Tractor Boys sit 10th in the table.

Ipswich were last in action on Tuesday, when they lost 4-2 against Arsenal in the League Cup, and will next play on Saturday, when they travel to Merseyside to take on Everton.

Sports.title: Inside Todd Boehly's Chelsea reign: How he became the target for irate fans, the major blunders he made and why the time was right to sell amid civil war at Stamford Bridge - and what happens next
Sports.content:
For Todd Boehly, Chelsea at Brentford is unlikely to rekindle romantic memories from that time he tried co-owning a Premier League club, even if he is a little richer for the experience now.

It was in March 2024 when his side were trailing 2-1 there as the away end turned on both him and his manager, Mauricio Pochettino. First, Chelsea’s fans sang ‘Roman Abramovich’. Then, ‘Boehly, you're a ****’. Next came ‘Jose Mourinho’. Followed by ‘F*** off, Mauricio’.

As the face of the original 2022 takeover, Boehly became a target when the times were bad, and no matter how good his intentions may have been, the American billionaire cannot say he helped himself. An astute business leader – clearly, for he has made a minor profit by selling his Chelsea shares to Clearlake Capital – but a man who made more than a few faux pas.

As Chelsea’s supporters return to Brentford on Friday, they may recall their hostile hymn sheet from two years ago, while remembering the other times their old co-owner indulged in the odd misadventure.

Remember that time he suggested the Premier League set up a north-versus-south all-star game? Remember that time he asked Ruud Gullit what it was he did for Chelsea?

Remember that time he named himself interim sporting director and asked Thomas Tuchel if he could sign Manchester United’s 37-year-old striker Cristiano Ronaldo? Remember that time he revealed he signed Marc Cucurella because he had heard Manchester City liked him?

Todd Boehly became a target when times were bad at Chelsea - now, he has left the club

Remember that time he brought in Raheem Sterling on a £325,000-per-week, five-year contract?

Remember that time he told Chelsea's players their season was ‘embarrassing’ in a dressing-room speech to Frank Lampard’s squad after a demoralising defeat by Brighton? Remember that time he was involved in a website which resold Premier League tickets at a premium?

Remember that time he took Pochettino for ‘a very nice dinner’ which resembled more of a last supper because the Argentinian was out of the job within the week?

Remember that time seven blokes dressed in green stood up behind the dugout and started brushing their teeth while Chelsea were playing Fulham to promote that flop of a film called Argylle?

Boehly caught hell for that one. He was the Hollywood investor who could do no right in the eyes of English football, ridiculed online for turning up at one game against Tottenham looking like the club shop had thrown up on him with his blue and white scarf and beanie.

That scrutiny will now fall on Clearlake, or, more specifically, Behdad Eghbali. Officially, he is the most powerful person at Chelsea. Sources close to Eghbali say he is determined to deliver success to the club, which means competing for the game’s grandest prizes. Those same insiders accept they will ultimately be judged on their actions, not words. It will take time to win over the naysayers, and despite the apparent civil war at ownership level that unfolded, Clearlake have expressed their gratitude to Boehly for his contribution ever since they succeeded Roman Abramovich.

To Eghbali’s credit, he is invested in Chelsea, and not only financially. While Boehly was there to collect the Club World Cup trophy from Donald Trump in his guise as Chelsea chairman, Eghbali is the owner who is forever there, home and away. Billionaires do not attend a Carabao Cup third-round tie away at Lincoln’s Sincil Bank on a Tuesday night unless they truly fancy it. Eghbali did.

Boehly did not. He became a regular on the worldwide conference circuit, but his attendance at Chelsea matches turned into a rarity over time, despite those within his camp insisting he had a skin thick enough to take any and all flak. It was needed.

All that criticism will now fall on Clearlake, or, more specifically, Behdad Eghbali (right)

The mockery was arguably at its most blatant in February 2024 when the Sky comedy show Fantasy Football League unveiled a sketch called ‘Who Wants To Be A Blue Billionaire Bottle Job?’

It was a week after Chelsea had lost the Carabao Cup final to Liverpool. Boehly was the contestant mimicked by Matt Lucas, and Gary Neville the presenter played by Elis James.

Boehly had already wasted £980million and only had to nail the final question for the confetti shower as he was asked by Neville: ‘There's a 19-year-old Dutch winger who's not that good. How much do you spend on him? Is it…’

A: Get him on a free.

B: Loan with option to buy.

C: Nothing, you desperately need a striker.

D: £135m.

Of course, Boehly chose D, and it was correct. To the very end, he was still the target, an AI video surfacing on social media last week showing Boehly punching Xabi Alonso because Chelsea's manager had asked for Enzo Fernandez to stay despite City offering a whopping £120m.

Rightly or wrongly, he was persistently the punchline. At least Boehly could tune in on Friday safe in the knowledge that his name will not be chanted by the Chelsea fans at Brentford this time.

Sports.title: Jos Buttler breaks new ground as England romp to another T20 victory over Sri Lanka as Harry Brook's ruthless side exploit their tourists' lack of confidence, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Jos Buttler breaks new ground as England romp to another T20 victory over Sri Lanka as Harry Brook's ruthless side exploit their tourists' lack of confidence, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

Harry Brook’s juggernaut T20 side racked up their 22nd win out of 25, as Jos Buttler – the man he replaced as captain – broke new ground on a one-sided night in Cardiff.

Thanks to a 24-ball half-century from Tom Banton, England raced to a six-wicket thrashing of struggling Sri Lanka with nearly eight overs to spare, to take an unassailable 2-0 lead going into Saturday’s series finale at Old Trafford. It’s hard to imagine they won’t complete a whitewash.

But it was Buttler who elbowed his way into the record books, becoming the first player to reach 15,000 runs in all T20 cricket – international and domestic – and leaving West Indian Kieron Pollard marooned on 14,999.

Buttler had given England’s chase a flying start by putting on 51 inside five overs with Swansea-born Aneurin Donald, who scooped his first ball for six but fell to Eshan Malinga’s slower ball for 21 at the ground he once called home.

And after Buttler departed for a 16-ball 30, top-edging Dushmantha Chameera high into the night sky to be caught by wicketkeeper Kamil Mishara, Brook continued the momentum, mowing leg-spinner Wanindu Hasaranga for three leg-side sixes in four balls before he was brilliantly held at deep square leg by Malinga aiming for a fourth.

That made it 79 for three, but any hope Sri Lanka had of clawing back a series-squaring win was snuffed out by Banton, who pummelled four sixes on a night when England outmuscled their visitors, clearing the ropes ten times to Sri Lanka’s two.

Jos Buttler became the first player to hit 15,000 T20 runs as England thumped Sri Lanka again

Sonny Baker impressed with the ball and is looking the part after tough debuts previously

Their batsmen had followed where their bowlers had led, with Sonny Baker – after a difficult debut in each of three formats over the past year – finding his feet, and his rhythm. He admitted after Tuesday’s win in Southampton, where he took three for 12 from four intelligent overs, that he had ‘almost wanted to do well too badly’ during his white-ball appearances last summer against South Africa and Ireland.

The first of those, an ODI at Headingley, produced figures of none for 76 off seven overs as Aiden Markram took him to the cleaners. In the second, a T20 in Dublin, he took none for 52 because he was ‘still probably trying to clutch back my ODI debut’.

But England have stuck with him, handing him a Test debut during the chaotic defeat by New Zealand at The Oval in June, when his match figures were an expensive three for 161, and now handing him new-ball duties.

He began with a maiden on Tuesday as the Sri Lankans set about the near-impossible task of chasing down England’s 254 for four, and finished his stint here with a wicket-maiden full of clever variations, and figures of one for 15, even outbowling Jofra Archer, who collected a couple of wickets as Sri Lanka’s innings dribbled to an underwhelming conclusion. Baker’s overall analysis in the two games so far is 8-2-27-4, which feels more Test match than T20.

Jamie Overton backed up his good work, bowling four overs off the reel mid-innings to finish with two for 23, while spinner Liam Dawson found himself on a hat-trick in his first over after Lahiru Udana failed to clear Overton at mid-on and Mishara provided a tame return catch first ball.

Dawson, who finished with three for 32 and the player of the match award, said: ‘We’ve had a settled side and we’ve got matchwinners throughout. Not many teams have that destructiveness in the batting. We’ve got some freaks in the team.’

Dawson’s double strike was the start of an alarming change of fortunes for the tourists after Udana and Pathum Nissanka had begun with a stand of 56 in 5.2 overs. From the remaining 14.4, they lost nine for 89, summing up a lack of confidence that this England side are more than happy to exploit.

‘Tonight was a special performance,’ said Brook. ‘It was very clinical. They got off to a flyer, and the way we dragged it back was outstanding with the ball. As for Jos, long may it continue. He’s been phenomenal for 15 years.’

‘They were too good,’ said Sri Lanka captain Charith Asalanka. ‘We have to improve a lot, honestly, because we are not up to the mark right now.’

Sports.title: Lewis Hamilton issues statement after 'asking Ferrari F1 worker to be replaced'
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton issues statement after 'asking Ferrari F1 worker to be replaced'

Lewis Hamilton allegedly demanded that a Ferrari trackside employee be sacked, with the seven-time world champion's hopes of winning a record eighth Formula 1 title fading fast

View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton has spoken out (Image: Bryn Lennon - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Lewis Hamilton has moved to deny a claim that he demanded the sacking of a Ferrari staff member. Hamilton, 41, has only won one Grand Prix this season and finds himself 99 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who replaced him at Mercedes last year.

‌



His DNF in Madrid on Sunday came off the back of a frustrating Italian Grand Prix in which made contact with team-mate Charles Leclerc and subsequently urged Ferrari to implement 'rules of engagement'. Fuel was added to the fire on Tuesday when Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera reported that Hamilton wanted a trackside employee to be replaced.

‌



The outlet also claimed that Hamilton's relationship with Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur had become strained. But in a post on Instagram, the Brit has denied asking for a colleague to be sacked.

‌



"I've seen some of the stories that have gone out and I want to clear it up here," Hamilton wrote. "I've never asked for anyone on my team to be replaced.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"Everyone I work with works hard every day, and their dedication is what moves us forward. I always try to empower and lift people to be the best versions of themselves or at least see the best in themselves.

"I may not always achieve that but it's my intention and what I'm here to do. We all work together and that will continue."

The seven-time world champion's post was accompanied by a picture of himself alongside Ferrari staff members. Hamilton did, however, become embroiled in a frosty exchange with his race engineer, Carlo Santi, just hours before qualifying in the Spanish capital.

‌



Hamilton had hit the barriers during practice which caused damage to his front wing, and he was told to leave the car in a safe position. But the 41-year-old defied Santi's orders, insisting that he could bring it back to the Ferrari garage.

It was only after the fifth time of asking that Hamilton finally stopped the car. Santi became his race engineer earlier this year after he parted ways with Riccardo Adami, who frequently clashed with Hamilton during his first season at Ferrari.

Will Lewis Hamilton regret joining Ferrari? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton Instagram (Image: Instagram/lewishamilton)

Before jetting off to Madrid, Hamilton held crunch talks with Leclerc and Vasseur following their drivers' clash in Monza. "What is great is that there was no shying away from having a discussion," he explained.

"We sat face to face, just him (Charles) and me, and talked about it and we were both honest and open and then we quashed it and moved on. That shows maturity from him and it is healthy. It is a relationship we have built over time.

Article continues below
