"Of course, there are going to be frustrations along the way. And there will be more times where we are close because we are approximate in pace and we both want to win as much as each other and do well for the team, but, yes, it is really positive.

"It has been really positive. I spoke to Fred on Monday and we had clearing out discussions. Naturally, we are going to have different opinions.

"But we come together to find a way forward and that is the positive of where we have got to over the past 15 months, when we can have really great communication internally and same with me and Charles. If you look at the history of the sport, this happened before, so it is no biggie."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick told who is putting his Man Utd job in 'danger' as players absolved
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick told who is putting his Man Utd job in 'danger' as players absolved

Manchester United have had a week to forget and will look to bounce back when they take on Fulham on Sunday afternoon

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has been warned about his Man United job. (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has been told that his tactics are putting his job at Old Trafford in danger. The team have suffered a difficult week, losing to both Manchester City and Brighton.

‌



The Manchester derby saw United unable to overcome 10-men for the majority of the game. Wednesday night then saw the team pegged back from 2-0 up to lose 3-2 against Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

‌



The full-time whistle was greeted with boos from around the stands, with some questions now being asked of Carrick. The former midfielder was appointed permanently in the summer, after leading United back to Champions League football.

‌



Former United striker Louis Saha has now hit out at Carrick’s tactics and highlighted what he believes could be improved. Speaking to Betano , he said: “The problem with Manchester United this season is not the players. Benjamin Sesko missed pre-season after his injury.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“Some players took their time to return after the World Cup. In truth I don’t think it was a good summer transfer window for Manchester United. But Michael Carrick has to adapt.

“I don’t see a team that has the animation it needs. Manchester United needs a system to play good football, with patterns of play.

“I think the way they are playing now is dangerous to Michael Carrick because this is not down to the players. Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, even Bruno Fernandes need a team that is playing with more fluidity, and I don’t think their teammates are doing that at the moment.

‌



“The two defensive midfielders look too comfortable passing the ball slowly, side-to-side. It does not provide the sort of passes forward to create those one-on-one moments.

“In transition they are too slow. It doesn’t matter who you put in these situations, whether it’s Sesko or Cunha or Mbeumo, if one of them isn’t taking more risks and pressing forward, it’s not going to help advance the play.

View 3 Images Man Utd crashed out of the Carabao Cup against Brighton

‌



“United create some chances but they are not clear cut chances, and they aren’t using the acceleration of Marcus Rashford to get behind teams, so they don’t have that dimension either. It’s all too slow.”

Midfield was a priority in the summer transfer window. United spent a total of £155 million on signing Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba.

But, despite the arrivals, it’s the exit of Casemiro, who left on a free transfer in the summer that Saha says has had the biggest impact.

‌



“How can Michael Carrick avoid falling short as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer did? What he must do now is support the team to animate the system, a way of playing, a certain motion and rhythm to what they do,” he added.

“Some of this comes naturally from the players you have but everything else must come from the manager. Last season a lot of that came from Casemiro. They still have not replaced him.

View 3 Images Casemiro left the club in the summer (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

‌



“People said he had no legs left but look at what Manchester United have lost now. He was the animator of the team. He gave everyone a belief in what they were doing.

“He was ready to seize the moment and take a risk and you could feel it in how they played. That’s why he is a great, great midfielder and has shown it over the years because he brought that balance.

“I think they can have that again with the players at the club but now it is Michael Carrick who must give this balance to the team as the manager. Maybe Carlos Baleba can offer this when he comes back from injury, which would also allow Bruno Fernandes to facilitate the strikers too.

Article continues below

“United need someone who excites the team, winning the ball, feeding the runners, lifting the crowd. United need something special there because they are missing a player who is dynamic and creative.”

Sports.title: Roy Keane slams Phil Foden for Manchester derby antics after red card - 'Get on the bus'
Sports.content:
Roy Keane slams Phil Foden for Manchester derby antics after red card - 'Get on the bus'

Phil Foden taunted Manchester United fans outside Old Trafford after City won Sunday's derby, despite him being sent off in the first half to give his team-mates an uphill battle

View Image Roy Keane has taken aim at Phil Foden (Image: The Overlap)

Roy Keane has called out Phil Foden for his behaviour outside Old Trafford following the Manchester derby. Foden, 26, was shown a red card in the 23rd minute of Sunday's fiery clash for a kick on Manchester United star Bruno Fernandes, although Manchester City defied the odds to win 1-0 in controversial fashion.

‌



Erling Haaland's strike which separated the sides should've been ruled out for offside, but the goal was allowed to stand because of a VAR error. Foden was a relieved man walking back towards City's team bus after full-time, although he took plenty of stick from United fans who standing on the Old Trafford forecourt.

‌



In response, the midfielder made a '1-0' gesture with his hands, taunting the home supporters. Keane took umbrage with his antics when he appeared on the Stick to Football podcast earlier this week.

‌



"Can I make a point on Foden?" the former United captain began. "Foden gets sent off at the weekend and gets left out of the England squad.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"He loves a YouTube video kicking it against a wall, he wants to learn to head the ball and might have scored a couple against [Crystal] Palace.

"Anyway, did you see him the other day walking onto the bus. He's holding his fingers up showing 1-0 to the United fans."

Jill Scott moved to defend Foden by saying: "But he's getting s*** isn't he? You do react." Keane wasn't having it, though, firing back: "You've just been sent off, what are you doing? Get on the bus."

‌



Should Phil Foden have been sent off? Have your say in the comments section.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Scott then argued: "You do react and he is a big City fan. I think he's being a fan as he's walking through there."

‌



Yet on Sunday, it was Keane who was defending Foden analysing the incident which led to his sending off. At half-time, the Irishman said on Sky Sports: "He (Fernandes) goes and tackles him, gives him a little boot on the floor. He does react, obviously.

"The strange thing is... I'm guessing it's classed as violent. To me, Bruno is the one who is violent. We see violence in a different way. I don't think that's a red card.

"Did the player give the referee a chance? Foden is daft, but so is Bruno. If Bruno got sent off we would be saying he is daft. Bruno has to do better there. Foden, I don't think it's a red card."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick is already under pressure at Man Utd - another defeat would be unthinkable
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is already under pressure at Man Utd - another defeat would be unthinkable

Michael Carrick picked Manchester United up by the bootstraps and through a wave of positivity took them back to the Champions League - now the mood is very different indeed

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is under pressure after a sticky start to the new season

Michael Carrick rode the crest of a wave last season to get Manchester United back on the biggest stage.

‌



This season, Carrick looks as if he is drowning in the expectation levels, demands and ongoing soap opera at Old Trafford.

‌



Make no mistake. Carrick is now under the cosh. United go into this weekend 13th in the table after a disappointing start. They are out of the Carabao Cup.

‌



And, worst of all, the United fans made their feelings plain. They booed Carrick and his players off the pitch after the defeat to Brighton. It felt a big moment in Carrick’s reign.

United’s fans are notoriously loyal, supportive and pride themselves in backing managers - rather than calling for them to be sacked. It is genuinely one of the best things in football.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The self-proclaimed biggest club in the world probably have more right than most to boo, jeer and get angry.

United have been stuck in a cycle of under-achievement and yet the fan base bought into Carrick because he is a club legend. Just like they did with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. They are desperate for it to work. And yet United are in serious danger of making the same mistakes all over again.

‌



Carrick gave the club such a lift as interim boss after Ruben Amorim’s spell in charge. After the shackles of Amorim’s rigid and failing tactics, Carrick felt like a breath of fresh air. He did a fantastic job. The upturn was remarkable.

It swept United along into the Champions League places and we were all guilty of making the same mistake: saying he deserved a chance. And, to be honest, it still feels like he did.

View 3 Images Those positive early days under Carrick now seem a long way in the rear-view mirror (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

‌



But this is Manchester United. You do not win prizes or become successful by making popular decisions. The summer was when United should have thought about bringing in a stellar name, elite manager and one who could have taken the club on the next step of the journey.

Sadly, it still feels like Carrick is the interim despite being given the job on a permanent basis. That is down to perception and also perhaps Carrick and his staff - including the vastly experienced Steve Holland - failing to convince us otherwise.

It was a patchy transfer window to put it mildly. Youri Tielemans was a good buy. Carlos Baleba is one for the future. Andrey Santos for £48m is mind-boggling. He was not a fixture at Chelsea.

‌



In the summer of 2025, United beefed up the attack - and yet still the three big purchases do not always start together. Benjamin Sesko is still largely a sub. Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are more regular starters but we’re still not sure how they dovetail together.

The defence lacks strong foundations. The midfield is a work in progress. And the heat is on the manager. To make matters worse, the academy’s jewel in the crown, JJ Gabriel, wants out.

‌



United could look to blame VAR for the Manchester City defeat. But excuses run out when you throw away a two-goal lead (the first time in 50 years at home) against Brighton.

This season was always going to be the real test. European football, bigger expectations and building on last season all with extra fixtures and a demand for silverware.

Carrick says he can deal with the pressure. Though that was not the case as he got bad tempered and snappy after the defeat at Hull City. He said, after they beat Ipswich the following week, the criticism was too much. No, it’s to be expected when United lose at Hull.

‌



View 3 Images Defeat to Fulham this weekend will leave Carrick under serious pressure

Now, United go to Fulham on Sunday knowing that another defeat will raise a hell of a lot of questions about Carrick ahead of a painfully long international break.

If United lose then the 20 days before their next game will be torture. Carrick will feel heat like never before. The longer break will only increase the pressure.

Article continues below

But it already feels like United are in danger of enduring another wasted season and going for the romantic, popular decision by appointing the likable club legend will have backfired badly.

Sports.title: Man Utd are back in an all-too familiar position - where do they go next?
Sports.content:
The new season may only be six games old, but it feels as though Manchester United fans have already lived through it a thousand times.

A run of underwhelming results - yielding just two wins - and performances means the goodwill and momentum built up by Michael Carrick during the second half of the 2025-26 campaign has already waned significantly. And while questions will inevitably be asked of United's former interim coach during the upcoming, prolonged international break if the Red Devils cannot sign off with a win at Fulham on Sunday, scrutiny should also be directed to those above Carrick in the hierarchy.

United's disappointing week went from bad to worse on Wednesday as they were dumped out of the Carabao Cup. While there was a sense of injustice over the Manchester derby defeat last Sunday given the offside controversy shrouding Erling Haaland's decisive goal, United were bang to rights against Brighton.

They crumbled after surging into a two-goal lead with Carrick becoming the first Manchester United manager to oversee a home defeat after leading 2-0 at half-time since Tommy Docherty in 1976.

‌



Carrick and his team left the field to a chorus of boos from supporters, whose early season optimism has already taken a pummelling.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And that has become a common trend for those taking their seats on the Stretford End. Just 12 months ago, United backed Ruben Amorim heavily in the transfer market, helping him rebuild their attacking options. But hopes of a second-season surge under the Portuguese were quickly extinguished, with his demise coming in January of this year.

‌



Go back another year and it was Erik ten Hag - fresh off after another summer of investment - who was clinging onto a job he would ultimately lose by the middle of October.

This represents a first crisis period for Carrick, who was handed the reins on a permanent basis after providing the perfect tonic to Amorim's torturous tenure by overseeing 11 wins and three draws from 16 competitive games.

View 3 Images Carrick had United purring last season, but he is now in the midst of his first really difficult patch (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

There were, understandably, parallels drawn between his impact in an interim capacity and that previously of Ole Gunnar Solksjaer. Crucially, though, Carrick has already proven he can navigate choppy waters; few would have envisaged a third-place finish for United given the condition they were in at the time of Amorim's implosion nine months ago.

‌



Since then, United have spent around £150million on a midfield overhaul designed to give Carrick the tools to continue the club's rehabilitation as they seek a seat back at the Premier League's top table.

But not only did the new partnership of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans get outfoxed by Brighton, there are already glaring holes elsewhere in the squad.

View 3 Images Man Utd crashed out of the Carabao Cup at the hands of Brighton

Luke Shaw's absence again highlighted United's failure to bring in adequate cover in that area during the transfer window for the here and now. And while it has already been suggested that the club will look to level up their defence next summer, choosing to rely so heavily on Shaw and Harry Maguire given their previous arcs - and where they are in their careers - for another year feels like a big call. Leny Yoro, signed for a significant transfer fee, has also yet to hit the desired levels in defence.

‌



In Benjamin Sesko, still yet to start a Premier League game this season, United have invested significantly. But the Slovenia international did not make the most of an opportunity to impress leading the line against Brighton. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha have Premier League pedigree and been rare transfer wins for United, but the fact Sesko was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee punctuates up a real dearth of quality depth in that No 9 area.

Strategic shortcomings like that cannot be attributed to Carrick, rather those above United's manager hierarchy. And solving them will not be cheap, nor will they be straightforward, even though United have managed to successfully move away from inflated figures in the transfer market.

Teething problems after a transfer window are not uncommon and perhaps United's business will age like wine rather than milk. After nailing their colours to Carrick's, he must, at least, be given the opportunity to steer United back on course. After all, a rinse and repeat would do nobody any favours.

‌



In two years the club will celebrate it's 150th anniversary; an event which Omar Berrada, United's chief executive, targeted back in 2024 as an occasion for United to mark by winning both men's and women's league titles.

Right now that feels fanciful. And while it will ultimately be down to Carrick to achieve the results which will ensure he gets the chance to see 'Project 150' through, others will be just as culpable if he is unable to do.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
